en: Vādhūla Śrautasūtra 6–7 (Jyotiṣṭoma). Checked: N1 (98.07.014); C checked (Caland’s handwritten copy, pp. 45–106).

6.1.1.1. One who is about to undergo initiation gathers the ritual materials: two kinds of milk, two black antelope skins, two garments for the initiated, freshly churned butter, ointment made from grain ground on the same day, a reed with its tuft intact, two bundles of *darbha* grass, three others, twenty-one others, as well as a yoke-thong, a girdle, a nose-rope, a black horn of an antelope, a staff of *udumbara* wood, a pestle, and the means for the bestowal of the vow.

6.1.1.2. On a clearly prepared sacrificial ground (*devayajana*), there is a hall with its rafters pointing eastward; it has openings toward the cardinal directions, is commensurate with the path of the stars, and has two doors, one to the south and one to the north. 6.1.1.3. He shaves his hair and beard. He trims his nails. Having become pure, he bathes and anoints himself. 6.1.1.4.

With the mantra, "Go forth from good to better" (TS 1.2.3.m), he proceeds toward the sacrificial ground after having performed the purification of the hall, reciting, "May Bṛhaspati be your forerunner."

6.1.1.5. With the verse, “Now come hither to this choice place on earth,” he causes [the sacrificer] to descend behind the hall with the words, “Drive away the enemies, O thou who art rich in all heroes.
6.1.1.6. With the verse, “We have come to this sacrificial ground of the gods on earth,” he consecrates the sacrificial ground with the mantra: “O All-gods... may we rejoice in nourishment.”

6.1.1.7. Taking the two bundles of *śākhā* branches, one with thorns and one without thorns, he drives them out from the interior of the hall toward the east with the formula, "Go away, depart, and creep away" (TS 4.2.4a), as far as the sacrificial ground (*devayajana*) of the hall. With the formula, "Those who are here, both ancient and recent—this world has been given to us," (TS 1.2.2b), he casts the two *śākhās* onto the rubbish-heap (*utkara*). Then he takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter. 6.1.1.8. Having placed the two *śākhās* on the *utkara*, he draws four portions of clarified butter.

6.1.1.9. He offers that [oblation] at the spot where the Audumbarī post stood, having placed gold upon a clump of *darbha* grass, with the verse: “O Earth, be soft for us; O home, grant us wide protection, svāhā!”—this is the *stambāhuti*. 6.1.1.10.

Having caused him to enter the hall by the eastern door, having churned the fire and distributed the fires, and having given [the food] to the ancestors on the *anvāhāryapacana* fire, he initiates the boy—or his son or brother—into the [sacrificial] color (*varṇa*).
5.1.1.16. Having prepared the ground to the depth of four finger-breadths and having brought forward the water, he offers the *dīkṣaṇīyā* oblation dedicated to Agni and Viṣṇu on eleven potsherds.
6.1.1.12. Once the offering has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.

6.1.1.13. Having released his speech at the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*), he offers the *Saptahotṛ* formula with clarified butter taken in four ladlings into the *āhavanīya* fire, and [he offers] for the twelve seasons: "To Madhu, svāhā! To Mādhava, svāhā!"—thus these [formulas].
6.1.1.14. When this has been dug out, he carries away the *stambayajus* (the grass-clump offering), encloses the altar (*vedi*), and mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
6.1.1.15. Being impelled, he performs the second enclosure of the altar.

6.1.1.16. Having leveled it and propped it up, he issues the call: "Set down the sprinkling waters; place the fuel and the sacrificial grass nearby; cleanse the dipping-spoon (*sruva*) and the offering-ladles (*sruc*); gird the wives; come forth with the clarified butter."

6.1.1.17. They perform this. 6.1.1.18. Having wiped the *sruva* and *sruk* ladles, he takes up the clarified butter; he sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmā-barhis*); he sprinkles the altar (*vedi*); he sprinkles what has been placed within it. 6.1.1.19. Having poured out the water, he takes up the *prastara* bundle.

6.1.1.20. He strews the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). 6.1.1.21. Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) and places two fuel-sticks (*samidh*) on the fire. 6.1.1.22. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing sticks, he yokes the fire.
6.1.1.23. Having come back, he places [the ladles] crosswise: the *prastara* on the two crosswise [ladles], the *juhū* on the *prastara*, and the other two *barhis*-blades on the *juhū*. 6.1.1.24.
When they have been set down together, he recites the *apānagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
6.1.1.25. Having touched them all together with the formulas, "The steadfast ones have sat down" and "That which of mine, O Agni," he recites the *daśahotṛ* formula.

6.1.1.26. He recites the invitatory verses for the fire being kindled. 6.1.1.27. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* spoon, he says: "O *Āgnīdh*, cleanse the fires three times each. 6.1.1.28.
Without letting the two offering-ladles touch each other, having stepped across and anointed the *dhruvā* ladle, and having set it down, he chooses the *pravara*.
6.1.1.29. The Hotṛ sits down.
6.1.1.30. Being impelled, he takes up the two offering-spoons.
6.1.1.31. He performs the fore-offerings.
6.1.1.32. Having performed the *prayāja* offerings and stepped across, he sprinkles the *dhruvā* ladle with clarified butter, then the oblation, and then the *upabhṛt* ladle.
6.1.1.33. He performs the two *ājyabhāga* offerings.
6.1.1.34. He offers the oblation to Agni and Viṣṇu.
6.1.1.35. He performs the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
6.1.1.36. Having stepped across and placed the two ladles (*srucau*) in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
6.1.1.37. Having touched water, he cuts off the *iḍā* portion.
6.1.1.38. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [the portion] for the *agnīdh*.

6.1.1.39. They consume it; they sprinkle themselves; they carry it around. 6.1.1.40. When the *prāśitra* has been consumed by the *brahmán*, he offers an oblation for the *hotṛ* following the continuity.

6.1.1.41. [The Adhvaryu] performs the after-offerings (*anūyāja*) with the formula, "O Brahman, we shall set forth. 6.1.1.42. Having returned, he separates the two offering-ladles (*srucau*) with the two *vājavatī* verses.
6.1.1.43. With the *śaṃyu* formula, he strews the *prastara* grass-bundle together with the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*).
6.1.1.44. Having gone outside, they perform the *saṃyājana* offerings for the wives.
6.1.1.45. Having offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation, having gone eastward and set down the *sruk* ladle, they go out toward the north.
6.1.1.46. To the north of the enclosed sacrificial hall (*śālā*), these very same materials for the initiation (*dīkṣaṇīyā*) are prepared: a water-pot and an unwashed garment.

6.1.2 [Dīkṣā] 6.1.2.1 A water-pot, an unwashed garment, freshly churned butter, freshly ground collyrium, a stalk of *śara* grass with its tuft, two bundles of *darbha* grass, and a razor. 6.1.2.2 Having led [the sacrificer] into this enclosed space, he anoints his right *godāna* (the hair near the ear) with [the butter], reciting: “May the waters moisten [you] for life” (*āpa undantu jīvase*) and “for long life and luster” (*dīrghāyutvāya varcase*).
6.1.2.3. With the three verses beginning, “O herb, protect him” (1.2.1b), he places [the hair] upon it using three bunches of *darbha* grass with their tips pointing eastward.

[Cf. 5.2.1.4] 6.1.2.4. With the verse, “O axe, do not harm him” (1.2.1c), he shaves [the hair] using the axe with the formula, “O god-hearer, shave these [parts]” (6.2.1.9). [Cf. 6.2.1.9] [N1, 57a3] 6.1.2.5.
With the verse, “May I attain prosperity in the future” (1.2.1d), he touches the remaining parts.
6.1.2.6. In this very same way, he sows the subsequent *gadāna* seeds.
6.1.2.7. Once they have been sown, he makes them fragrant with a razor.
6.1.2.8. He pours water over them with the mantra: "May the waters, our mothers, purify us. (TS 1.2.1f1)
6.1.2.9. With the words, “May those purified by ghee purify us with ghee” (1.2.1f2), he sprinkles himself with water.

6.1.2.10. With the words, “May they carry away all our impurity” (1.2.1f3), he looks at flowing streams. 6.1.2.11. With the words, “From them I emerge, bright and purified” (1.2.1f4), he steps out toward the north.

6.1.2.12. With the mantra, “Thou art the body of Soma; protect my body” (TS 1.2.1.g), he puts on an unwashed garment. 6.1.2.13. With the mantra, “Thou art the milk of the great ones; thou art the bestower of luster; bestow luster upon me” (TS 1.2.1.h), he anoints himself with fresh butter, following the direction of the hair.

6.1.2.14. With the mantra, “Thou art the pupil of Vṛtra; thou art the protector of the eye; protect my eye” (TS 1.2.1.i), he applies collyrium with a reed-shaft together with its tuft; three times for the right eye and twice for the left.

6.1.2.15. He throws [the grass] out along the southern [side], for the *Brāhmaṇa* says, "Do not let it remain hidden. [He does this] with twenty-one bunches of *darbha* grass. 6.1.2.16. He purifies him with seven [verses]: "May the Lord of Thought purify you; may the Lord of Speech purify you" (1.2.1k); and with seven [verses] beginning, "May the god Savitṛ purify you with a flawless filter, with the rays of the Vasu Sūrya."

6.1.2.17. With all seven [verses] together, beginning with "O Lord of the Purifier, by means of your purifier, may I be able to purify that for which I am purified" (1.2.1), he should purify the one born before.

6.1.2.18. With the verse "We entreat you, O gods... (1.2.1m-o), he causes him to enter the sacrificial ground, saying: "O gods, those who possess the law of truth at the sacrifice; protect us, O gods, while we exist. 6.1.2.19. With the eight-verse hymn dedicated to Pavamāna, beginning with "Pavamāna, the dweller in heaven," he causes him, who is standing to the north of the altar, to perform the ritual salutation (*upasthāna*).
6.1.2.20. With the words, “May we straightway attain truth,” he steps across the rear of the altar.
6.1.2.21. With the words, “Place me in prosperity,” he sits down in the sacrificer’s station.

6.1.2.22. With the formula, “To intention, to impulse, to Agni, svāhā! (TS 1.2.2a,b1), he offers the *yajus* formulas of the butter poured from the *dhruvā* ladle with the *sruva* spoon. He pours them together with the formula, “To wisdom, to mind, to Agni, svāhā; to consecration... to Pūṣan, to Agni, svāhā; O divine waters, vast, all-beneficent. (TS 1.2.2a–c).

6.1.2.23. Having offered with the *sruva* ladle while reciting, “May Heaven and Earth, the wide atmosphere, and Bṛhaspati increase us with the oblation, svāhā! (1.2.2b2–3), and having replenished the *dhruvā* ladle, he takes four portions into the *juhū* ladle. 6.1.2.24. Having filled it completely, he offers the full-oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) while reciting, “Every mortal chooses the god who leads for the sake of prosperity, svāhā! (1.2.2c). 6.1.2.25. Having silently poured out the *praṇītā* waters within the altar, he spreads a black antelope skin within the altar, with its neck toward the west and the hair facing upward.

6.1.2.26. Regarding those two, the *ṛc* and the *sāman*, he touches them while reciting, “You two are the crafts (*śilpe stha*)”; he touches the white and the black [parts] with the formula, “I take hold of you two; may you two protect me until the conclusion of this sacrifice. 6.1.2.27. Then, he pushes these two forward toward the east, not cutting through the surface of the earth, with the verse, “These two [are for] the one practicing his thought (*dhiyam śikṣamāṇasya*), O God... 6.1.2.28. Having bent his right knee, the sacrificer creeps forward with the formula, “May we board the ship, O Varuṇa, which is skillful and wise, the well-protecting earth and heaven, the faultless, for our well-being (*svastaye*).”
6.1.2.29. Having turned toward the east upon the black antelope skin (kṛṣṇājina) above, he sits down, making a lap.
6.1.2.E. With the words, “Thou art vigor, belonging to Aṅgiras,” the girdle (mekhalā) is fastened around him.
6.1.3.1. With the formula, "Thou art strength, belonging to the Aṅgirases," he girds on the girdle; with the formula, "Soft as wool, grant me strength. 6.1.3.2.

With the formula, "Protect me, do not harm me," he makes a knot. 6.1.3.3. With the formula, "Thou art the protection of Viṣṇu," he covers himself with the garment; [he says], "The protection of the sacrificer, grant me protection."
6.1.3.4. With the words, “O Heaven and Earth, cover me,” he covers himself, including his head.
6.1.3.5. With the words, “Protect me from being seen by the stars” (ŚB 1.2.2.h), he looks through the openings of the garment.
6.1.3.6. With the words, “Thou art the womb of Indra; do not harm me” (ŚB 1.2.2.i), he fastens the black antelope horn to its cord.
6.1.3.7. With the formula, “For cultivation, thee, for good harvest” (TS 1.2.2k), he draws three lines within the altar.
6.1.3.8. With the formula, “For the plants with good fruit, thee” (TS 1.2.2l), he ties a tuft of hair on the right side of his head.
6.1.3.9. With the formula, “May the divine tree be a good support” (TS 1.2.2m), he hands him a staff made of Udumbara wood, saying, “Standing upright, protect me until the completion.”

6.1.3.10. With the words, “You are praised; you are the giver of people; you are the one with whom there is a draught; protect me,” he places the cup for him so that it is not empty. 6.1.3.11. There are rice and barley, as well as a drop of clarified butter and a drop of water; from these, he warms his hands. 6.1.3.12. With the words, “I approach the consecration (dīkṣā),” [he approaches] truth, his own self, faith, the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), food, imperishability, and the world of Brahman.

6.1.3.13. Having recited three times, "I consecrate myself with breath, with truth," he dips his fingers into the cup, saying: "Svāhā! To the sacrifice with the mind; svāhā! To heaven and earth; svāhā! From the wide mid-air. (cf. 1.2.2n) 6.1.3.14.
Having dipped all [the fingers], he draws up four [drops] with the formula: "From the wind, I take hold of the sacrifice. (cf. 1.2.2n, last)

6.1.3.15. Here, they place him upon the black antelope skin with its neck pointing northward. The Adhvaryu says to him: "You are consecrated. "Speak the words of the consecrated; do not step down from the black antelope skin; let your staff be made of Udumbara wood; let it remain visible; do not release your speech before the stars appear; if you should release it, recite a verse addressed to Viṣṇu."

6.1.3.16. If he should emit [semen] while distracted, he should recite the verse addressed to Viṣṇu: “O Viṣṇu, you who are our closest, grant us protection, O Conqueror; your streams, dripping with honey, flow forth, bestowing inexhaustible [wealth]. 6.1.3.17.

“This Brāhmaṇa has been consecrated,” the Adhvaryu says three times in a low voice within the hall: “We announce such-and-such a person, the son of such-and-such a man, to Indra and Agni, to the All-gods, and to the Soma-drinking Brāhmaṇas.”

6.1.3.18. Another person, having gone out, loudly announces three times: "This Brahmin has been initiated"; then [the Adhvaryu] says: "So-and-so, the son of so-and-so, has offered Soma to Indra and Agni, to the All-gods, and to the Soma-drinking Brahmins.
6.1.3.19. Restraining his speech, he remains seated until the stars appear.

6.1.3.20. When the stars have risen, having gone out from the hall by the eastern door, he releases his speech with the words, “*bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar*. Having entered with the words, “*bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar, perform the vow, perform the vow, perform the vow! Agni is worthy of sacrifice; the waters are worthy of sacrifice; the cows are worthy of sacrifice; the gods are worthy of sacrifice; the sacrifice is worthy of sacrifice; I am worthy of sacrifice,*” he sits down in the sacrificer’s place. 6.1.3.21. Then they bring that vow to him.

6.1.3.22. With the words, “We meditate upon the divine thought,” he purifies himself with the verse: “For our welfare, for our aid, may she be a bringer of splendor, a carrier of the sacrifice, and one who leads us safely across.
6.1.3.23. With the words, “This is your seasonal womb,” he causes the fire to ascend into himself with the verse: “From whence born, do thou increase our wealth. 6.1.3.24.
With the words, “The gods who are mind-born and mind-yoked,” he undertakes the vow with the formula: “O you of pure skill, whose father is skill—homage to them, svāhā!”

6.1.3.25. Having performed the vow with the formula, "O Day, I am from you," he releases it with: "I am you; you are this mine. I am the womb, you are the womb. Carry the oblations to the gods each to their proper place, O Jātavedas, son of the father, the maker of the world.
6.1.3.26. He purifies himself with the verse, "We meditate upon the divine thoughts" (1.2.3.1a).
6.1.3.27. As he is about to lie down, he causes him to recite: "O Agni, you..."
“O Agni, you have been well-kindled; give us back our consciousness. 6.1.4.2.
He causes him to recite the *prabuddha-yajus*: “O Agni, you are the guardian of vows (1.2.3d1), O god, among mortals, you are to be praised at the sacrifices (1.2.3d3).”
6.1.4.3. He causes him to recite the *yajus* for turning around: "The All-Gods have turned toward me" (TS 1.2.3e1), and "May I be blessed with power and vigor. 6.1.4.4.

In this very manner, having heated [the milk] in the morning, they bring him his fast-food (*vrata*) according to the verse: "Before the time of the fast-food. 6.1.4.5. Before sunrise, he introduces speech [to the sacrificer] with: "Make the fires luminous! O consecrated one, restrain your speech! O wife, restrain your speech!"

6.1.4.6. If the wife has been initiated, he should release his speech with the *āditya* formula; then, if he should send out a messenger for alms (*sani*), he consecrates the departing messenger with the mantra: “May Pūṣan [be] with the gift” (1.2.3e2), and [the returning one] with “Soma... the giver of wealth” (1.2.3e). 6.1.4.7. He awaits the one bringing [the gift] with the mantra: “O Soma, grant this much, bring more” (1.2.3f), and [he addresses himself] with: “May I, while giving, not fail through the act of giving; may I not fail through my life-span” (1.2.3g).

6.1.4.8. He accepts gold with the words, “Thou art the moon; be for my enjoyment”; cloth with the words, “Thou art clothing; be for my enjoyment”; a cow with the words, “Thou art a draft-ox; be for my enjoyment”; a horse with the words, “Thou art a steed; be for my enjoyment”; a mule with the words, “Thou art a better steed; be for my enjoyment”; a goat with the words, “Thou art a goat; be for my enjoyment”; a ram...

With the words, “Thou art a ram; be for my enjoyment,” he addresses a ram; with the words, “Thou art a goat; be for my enjoyment,” a goat; with the words, “Thou art an elephant; be for my enjoyment,” an elephant or a man; with the words, “Thou art a bird; be for my enjoyment,” a chariot; with the words, “Thou art a draft-animal; be for my enjoyment,” a cart or a house; with the words, “Thou art swelling; be for my enjoyment,” milk or clarified butter; and with the words, “Thou art a herb; be for my enjoyment,” grain.

"Thou art of the forest trees; become for my enjoyment"—with these words he accepts whatever is of the forest trees, each according to its respective deity. 6.1.4.9. If, among the sacrificial gifts that have been collected together, one should fall away or be lost, he should say, "One must search for it. 6.1.4.10. If they should not find it, he should dedicate it with the formula: "To Vāyu, thee! (TS 1.2.3.i1-2).
6.1.4.11. With the words, “For Varuṇa you,” [he offers] that [cow] which might die in water, or which a snare might strike.

6.1.4.12. With the words, “For Nirṛti you,” [he offers] that which might break apart, or sink down, or fall into a pit. 6.1.4.13. With the words, “For Rudra you,” [he offers] that which a human weapon might strike, or which Mahādeva [might strike].
6.1.4.14. With the words, "For death thee," one should offer that [cow] which has died while being driven.
6.1.4.15. If they should find one that has fallen down, they should not include it among the sacrificial gifts (dakṣiṇās), nor should they tell the neighbors to guard it in the cow-pen.
6.1.4.16. At the time for the sacrificial gifts, one should give it to a Brāhmaṇa who is not a priest; that is its ritual function.

6.1.4.17. If a yoga (an encounter with a hostile force) should befall one who has been initiated (*dīkṣita*), he should, having performed the purificatory rites (*vrata*) and having tied up the calves, cause the fires to ascend into himself (*samārohya*). Then, reciting, “Go forth from good to better” (TS 1.2.3m), he should set out; and reciting, “Now we seek refuge in you” (TS 1.2.3n2), he should take shelter. 6.1.4.18. These same [rites] apply at the conclusion of the yoga for one who has been initiated. 6.1.4.19. If he should come upon flowing waters, they should either carry him across together or he should have them carried across; he must not step down into the waters.
6.1.4.20. He should take up two clods of earth.
6.1.4.21. Of these two, he should throw one into the water with the mantra: “O divine waters, O son of the waters, may I not step upon you” (1.2.3.k).
6.1.4.22. With the mantra: “May I follow the unbroken thread of the earth” (1.2.3.l), he should scatter the other while being moved forward or being gathered together.

6.1.4.23. Whatever remains of the clod of earth, he should place that on the far side and stand upon it, saying: "May I not be deprived of this [earth]. 6.1.4.24. Whenever he has determined that he is about to perform a sacrifice, at that time he should perform these rites.
6.1.4.25. He should consecrate that sacrificial ground with a mantra; he should drive out the [obstacles] from it; he should offer the *stambayajus* oblation upon it.

6.1.4.26. If he, being consecrated (*dīkṣita*), should see something impure (*amedhya*), he should cause him to recite: "Unbound is the mind (3.1.1.2); the eye is poor, the eye is poor; Sūrya is the best of lights. O Consecration (*dīkṣā*), do not abandon me! 6.1.4.27. Now, if it should rain upon him, he should cause him to recite: "Flowing, bestow strength (3.1.1.3a var.); bestow vigor, bestow strength! You are givers of vigor, givers of strength; do not destroy my consecration, do not destroy my ascetic heat (*tapas*)."
6.1.4.28. If he, being consecrated (*dīkṣita*), should shed tears, he should consecrate them with the formula: “Ye are the waters of distress; being consecrated by *svāhā*, go to the earth! 6.1.4.29.
If he should produce phlegm, [he should consecrate it with]: “Ye are the waters of joy; being consecrated by *svāhā*, go to the earth! 6.1.4.30.
If he should produce saliva, [he should consecrate it with]: “Ye are the waters of loathing; being consecrated by *svāhā*, go to the earth!”
6.1.4.31. If they should fall as sweat, [he says]: "O waters, you are those for asceticism; consecrated by *svāhā*, go to the earth. 6.1.4.32.
If they should rise up as blood, [he says]: "O waters, you are those for the flesh-eaters; consecrated by *svāhā*, go to the earth. 6.1.4.33.
If they should produce urine or feces, [he says]: "O waters, you are those that release from distress; consecrated by *svāhā*, go to the earth."
6.1.4.34. If he should spill semen, [he should offer with the formula]: "O waters, you are the shedders of semen; being consecrated by *svāhā*, go to the earth.
6.1.4.35. This is the consecration (*dīkṣā*); this is the conduct of one who is consecrated. 6.1.4.36. Indeed, even by means of this, one may become consecrated without formal initiation.
"Tomorrow is the King's purchase," [they say]; having washed the hide of a red bull with its hair turned upward, they beat it.

6.2.1.2. He gathers the garments for the four *uṣṇīṣas*: a she-goat and a ram, two tufts of wool—one white and one black, a non-twitching [wool], the king’s throne, the Soma-carrying vehicle, the two Soma-carrying oxen, the royal purchase-cow and the royal purchase-oxen, a bull, a pair consisting of an ox and a cow, a garment, a four-measure vessel, a vessel of clarified butter, and a tuft of *balbaja* grass.

6.2.1.3. In the morning, having released his speech with the *āditya* formula, having set out the sacrificial implements, and having carried forward the waters, he pours out the *prāyaṇīya* oblation with the formula: “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I pour thee out, acceptable to Aditi, to Pathyāsvatī, to Agnivati, to Somavati, and to Savitṛvati. Thus he pours out four handfuls of rice. 6.2.1.4. Once it has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
6.2.1.5. Having released his speech at the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*), he should initiate the wives, provided that they have not already been initiated.

6.2.1.6. To the east of the enclosed shed (*pariśrita*), these very materials for the initiation (*dīkṣaṇīya*) are prepared: a water-pot, an unwashed garment, freshly churned butter, collyrium ground on the same day, a stalk of *śara* grass with its tuft, two bundles of *darbha* grass (one with and one without a tuft), and a razor.
6.2.1.7. Having entered this enclosed space, he anoints her right armpit with the formula, “May the waters moisten you for life, for long life, and for splendor.
6.2.1.8. With the formula, “O herb, protect her,” he places three tufts of *darbha* grass with their points directed eastward upon it. 6.2.1.9.
With the formula, “O axe, do not harm her,” and with the formula, “O god-famed one, shave these [hair],” he shaves her hair using an axe.
6.2.1.10. With the words, “May I attain prosperity in the future” (ŚB 1.2.1d), he touches the [hair] on the upper side; in this very same manner, he shaves the hair on the upper wing. 6.2.1.11.
Having been previously shaved, he makes it emit a flow of fragrance.
6.2.1.12. He causes water to be poured over it with the words, “May the waters, our mothers, purify us” (ŚB 1.2.1f1).

6.2.1.13. With the words, "May those whose essence is clarified butter purify us with clarified butter," he sprinkles himself with water; and with the words, "May they carry away all our impurity," [he sprinkles]. 6.2.1.14. He looks at the flowing waters and, with the words, "From them, pure and purified, I emerge," he steps out toward the north.
6.2.1.14. With the words, "Thou art the body of Soma; protect my body," he puts on an unwashed garment.
6.2.1.15. With the mantra, “Thou art the milk of the great ones; thou art the bestower of luster; bestow luster upon me,” he anoints himself with fresh butter following the direction of hair growth.

6.2.1.16. With the mantra, “Thou art the pupil of Vṛtra; thou art the protector of the eye; protect my eye,” he applies collyrium with a stalk of *śara* grass together with its tuft, three times on the right eye and twice on the left.
6.2.1.17. He throws away the stalk toward the south with the mantra, “Do not perish,” for so says the Brāhmaṇa. [He does this] with twenty-one bunches of *darbha* grass.

6.2.1.18. He purifies him with seven [verses] beginning, "May Citpati purify you; may Vākpati purify you," and with seven [verses] beginning, "May the god Savitṛ purify you with an unbroken filter, with the rays of the sun, O Vasu. 6.2.1.19.

With all seven [verses] beginning, "O Lord of the filter, by your filter, for whatever purpose I purify myself, may I be able to accomplish that," he should purify the wife of the one who has already fathered a son.

6.2.1.20. With the words, “Let the wife of the Brahman go forward” (3.5.6b), he causes her to enter the hall by the western door with the verse: “May she sit upon the altar with a leaf; then may I, following my desire, enter here into my own world. 6.2.1.21. Having entered and standing behind the Gārhapatya fire, he turns toward the east and sits down. With the words, “I bind you with a bond of peace” (3.5.6a), he girds her with the cord, saying: “I bind you with milk and clarified butter; I bind you with waters and plants; I bind you today with offspring. May she be consecrated; may we win strength.”
6.2.1.22. With the verse, "May we have good offspring through thee" (3.5.6d), he makes her recite this secret formula (*upaniṣad*): "A good wife, invincible. 6.2.1.23.
With the words, "Thou art the protection of Viṣṇu" (1.2.2g), he covers her with a garment, saying: "Protection for the sacrificer’s wife; grant me protection. 6.2.1.24.
With the words, "O Heaven and Earth, may you two cover her," he places the prepared *kurīra* (head-net) upon her.
6.2.1.25. With the words, “Protect me from the gaze of the constellations” (ŚB 1.2.2h), he gazes at the *atīkāśas* (openings) of the *kurīra*.
6.2.1.26. With the words, “Thou art the womb of Indra; do not harm me” (ŚB 1.2.2i), he fastens a *niṣkūjanī* (a silencing ring) to its *sic* (the fringe).
6.2.1.27. With the words, “For the sake of cultivation, for good crops” (ŚB 1.2.2k), he draws three lines to the west of the *gārhapatya* fire.
6.2.1.28. With the formula, "For the plants with beautiful berries, thee," he sews the right wing of this [bird-shaped vessel].

6.2.1.29. With the formula, "Thou art praised, the giver of people; together with the draught, protect me," he places an empty cup upon it. 6.2.1.30. There are rice and barley, a drop of clarified butter, and a drop of water; from here, he warms his hands over the fire.

6.2.1.31. Having recited three times, "I enter the consecration (*dīkṣā*); truth, my own self, faith, the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), food, imperishability, and the world of Brahman; through breath, through truth, the consecration," he dips his fingers into the cup (*camasa*), saying: "Svāhā! To the sacrifice with the mind! Svāhā! From heaven and earth! Svāhā! From the wide atmosphere! (cf. 1.2.2n). 6.2.1.32. Having dipped all [the fingers], he draws up four [sips] with the formula: "From the wind, I undertake the sacrifice" (1.2.2n, last). 6.2.1.33. They remain restrained in speech until the invitation (*upahava*).
6.2.1.34. "O householder, let your wife seek permission," says the Adhvaryu. 6.2.1.35. Having said, "Permission is granted," he releases his speech. 6.2.1.E. While rising, he issues the command.

6.2.2.1. Rising, he issues the command: "O Soma-seller, purify the Soma! Let a Brāhmaṇa sit to the south at the edge of the water! O Subrahmaṇya, lead forth the Soma-carrying horse! The Pratiprasthātṛ unties the bound [animal]; prepare the articles for the purchase of the King (Soma)!
6.2.2.2. They do these things.

6.2.2.3. He pours the rice grains into the vessel for the scrapings (*niṣkāsa-bhājana*) which he uses when preparing the *caru*. 6.2.2.4. When this [milk] has been boiled, he pours clarified butter (*ājya*) into it with which he is about to proceed. 6.2.2.5.
Having poured that back into the butter-pot (*ājyasthālī*), he performs the *stambayajus* rite, encloses the altar (*vedi*), and mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
6.2.2.6. Having been impelled, he performs the second tracing around.

6.2.2.7. Having leveled the ground and propped it up, he issues the command: "Set down the sprinkling waters; place the fuel and the sacrificial grass nearby; cleanse the dipping-spoon and the offering-spoons; come forth with the clarified butter. 6.2.2.8. They do these things.

6.2.2.9. Having wiped the *sruc* ladles, he takes up the clarified butter; all six [ladles] are filled with portions. 6.2.2.10. He sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmābarhis*), he sprinkles the altar (*vedi*), and he sprinkles the items placed nearby. 6.2.2.11.
Having poured out the remaining water, he takes up the *prastara* bundle.
6.2.2.12. He strews the sacrificial grass (barhis). 6.2.2.13. Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (paridhi).
6.2.2.14. He places two fuel-sticks (samidh) upon the fire.
6.2.2.15. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*), he yokes the fire.

6.2.2.16. Having returned, he places the *tiraścī* [ladle] down; upon the two *tiraścī* [ladles], the *prastara* [bunch of grass]; upon the *prastara*, the *juhū* [ladle]; and the other two [ladles, *upabhṛt* and *dhruvā*], upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). 6.2.2.17. When they have been placed together, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite the formulas for the *apānagraha* cups and the *pṛśni* [cups].
6.2.2.13. Having touched [the fire] while reciting, "The firm ones have sat down... for me, O Agni" (*dhruvā asadan yan me agne*), he recites the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula.
6.2.2.14. He pronounces the invitatory verses (*anuvāka*) for the fire being kindled.
6.2.2.15. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* ladle, he says: "O *Āgnīdh*, cleanse the fire three times each! [N1,61a1]
6.2.2.16. Having stepped across without letting the two *sruk* ladles touch each other, having anointed the *dhruvā* and set it down, he chooses the *pravara*.
6.2.2.17. The *hotṛ* sits down.
6.2.2.18. Being impelled, he takes up the two *sruk* ladles.
6.2.2.19. He performs the *prayāja* offerings.
6.2.2.20. Having performed the *prayāja* offerings and having stepped across, he pours clarified butter over the *dhruvā* ladle five times, and then over the oblation and the *upabhṛt* ladle.
6.2.2.21. Disregarding the two *ājyabhāga* portions, he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Pathyā Svasti," while taking four portions of clarified butter.
6.2.2.22. He says, “O, cause it to be heard! and then, “Sacrifice for the path-leading well-being (pathyāṃ svastim).
6.2.2.23. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering in the eastern half [of the fire].
6.2.2.24. He says, “Recite the invitatory verse for Agni,” while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
6.2.2.25. He says, "O, cause [him] to hear!"—"Sacrifice to Agni!
6.2.2.26. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers [the oblation] in the southern half.
6.2.2.27. He says, "Recite for Soma! while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
6.2.2.28. He says, "O, cause [the Hotṛ] to hear," and then, "Sacrifice to Soma.
6.2.2.29. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers in the rear half [of the fire].
6.2.2.30. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Savitṛ," while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
6.2.2.31. "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard!"—thus he says; "Sacrifice to Savitṛ!"—thus [he says]. 6.2.2.32.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers [the oblation] in the northern half [of the fire]. 6.2.2.33.
"Recite for Aditi!"—thus he says, while spreading [ghee] underneath and cutting off [portions], he cuts off portions of the rice-pap from both the rear and the front.
6.2.2.34. He pours clarified butter over it and anoints it back. 6.2.2.35. He says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard!"—"Sacrifice to Aditi!
6.2.2.36. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering in the middle.
6.2.2.37. "Recite for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt," he says, while spreading [the butter] five times. 6.2.2.38.
He takes a portion from the northern half of the *caru* with the stirring-spoon once.
6.2.2.39. Having taken that portion, he hands the two spoons, one below the other, to the Āgnīdhra.
6.2.2.40. He pours clarified butter over [the portion] twice; he does not smear it back [onto the cake]; it is an eightfold-portioned *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
6.2.2.41. He says, "O, cause [the fire] to hear! and "Sacrifice to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt! 6.2.2.42.
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering on the northern half, passing beyond the previous offerings.

6.2.2.43. He causes the fires to burn intensely; he does not throw the stirring-ladle (mekṣaṇa) into the fire. 6.2.2.44. Having stepped across and placed the two offering-spoons (srucau) in their respective places, he cuts off the portion for the Prāśitra-eating.
6.2.2.45. Having touched water, he spreads under the Iḍā-portion nine times.
6.2.2.46. He cuts off twice and pours clarified butter over it once; this is the twelve-fold portion (*dvādaśāvadāna*) for the *iḍā*. 6.2.2.47.
When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [the portions] for the *agnīdh*. 6.2.2.48. They consume [the portions] and perform the purification (*mārjana*); they carry [the *iḍā*] around.
6.2.2.49. When the *prāśitra* has been consumed by the Brahman priest, he offers the oblation of the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula along with the *santati* (connecting) verses.
6.2.2.50. With the words, “O Brahman, we shall set forth,” he performs the *anūyāja* offerings.
6.2.2.51. Having returned, he separates the two offering-spoons (*sruc*) with the two *vājavatī* verses.

6.2.2.52. He strews the *prastara* and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) together with the *śaṃyu*-formula. 6.2.2.53. He takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter and offers them with the mantra: "The sage of the sacrifice spreads the path, svāhā!—on the back of the earth, above the luminous realm of heaven, by which you carry the oblation as a messenger from here, O wise one, being immortal and most gracious, svāhā! 6.2.2.54. He takes another four spoonfuls of clarified butter.

6.2.2.55. Upon that [spot], having tied a piece of gold with a blade of *darbha* grass while reciting, "This, O bright one, is thy body" (1.2.4a), he places it down with the words, "Be united with it; go to radiance. 6.2.2.56. With the formula, "Thou art swift" (1.2.4b,c), he offers it, saying: "Sustained by the mind, beloved by Viṣṇu—may I obtain the control of speech at the impulse of thee, whose impulse is true; Svāhā! 6.2.2.57. He takes another fourfold portion of clarified butter, saying: "Thou art bright, thou art immortal, the oblation for the All-gods" (1.2.4d).
6.2.2.E. While rising, he issues the command:

6.2.3.1. While rising, he issues the command: "Bring the wooden sword (sphya), the water-vessel, and the foot-washing stone! Come, O sacrificer! Let them lead the wife forward! Open the eastern door!"—thus.
6.2.3.2. The doors are closed.

6.2.3.3. At the time when they proceed with the *prāyaṇīya* offering, the *agnīdh* pours the *praṇītā* water within the altar (*antarvedi*). Having washed the *caru*-pot and the vessel for the scrapings, having poured the rice grains into it, and having bound the *veda*, the stirring-spoon (*mekṣaṇa*), and the sacrificial grass together, he wraps them around the central king-post of the shed and places them there.
6.2.3.4. Having gone out from the eastern door of the hall, he holds up a piece of gold.
6.2.3.5. They look through its opening with the verse: "I have mounted the eye of the sun, O Agni, shining with wisdom" (1.2.4e). 6.2.3.6.

He consecrates the cow intended for the purchase of the King Soma with the formulas: "Thou art thought, thou art mind" (1.2.4f,g), and "Thou art intelligence, thou art the sacrificial fee—become well-disposed toward us.
6.2.3.7. With the formula, "May Mitra bind thee by the foot" (1.2.4h,i,k), he binds her by the foot with a *yajus* formula, saying: "May Pūṣan protect the paths; for Indra, the overseer."
6.2.3.8. Reciting, “May your mother approve of you” (1.2.4l,m), he follows her with the words, “May your father approve, may your brother; [I offer] Soma for Indra. 6.2.3.9.
Reciting, “May Rudra turn you back” (1.2.4n,o), he walks around her from the north-east, saying, “[Go] by the path of Mitra for well-being, together with wealth.
6.2.3.10. Standing behind her, he says, “Make her step forward toward the east and the north.”

6.2.3.11. Over her [footprint], he strides six steps following along the right thigh with the formula, "Thou art wealthy (vasvī)," "Thou art Rudrā," "Thou art Aditi," "Thou art Ādityā," and "Thou art Candrā. 6.2.3.12.
With the formula, "May Bṛhaspati cause thee to rejoice in happiness," he takes hold of the seventh footprint.
6.2.3.13. With the formula, "May Rudra together with the Vasus look upon thee," he covers [the footprint].

6.2.3.14. With the words, "I sprinkle you on the head of the earth" (TS 1.2.5.c), having placed gold upon the footprint, he makes an offering with the formula: "On the place of sacrifice, on the footprint of Iḍā, rich in ghee, svāhā! 6.2.3.15. With the words, "The *rakṣas* is encircled; the enemies are encircled" (TS 1.2.5.d,e), he draws a line around the gold at the footprint with the wooden sword (*sphya*), saying: "Here I cut off the neck of the *rakṣas*. 6.2.3.16. With the words, "May wealth be with us" (TS 1.2.5.f1), the Adhvaryu, having dug a hole as deep as a cow's hoofprint with a black antelope horn, pours the dust from the footprint into it.

6.2.3.16. With the words, “In thee be wealth” (1.2.5f2), he hands it to the sacrificer. 6.2.3.17. With the words, “In thee be wealth; may there be wealth for us both” (1.2.5f3+?), the sacrificer hands it to the wife. 6.2.3.18.

With the words, “O goddess, look upon the goddess Urvaśī” (1.2.5g,h), he causes the wife to gaze at the cow used for purchasing the Soma. With the words, “May I, accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, consort with thee; may I obtain a hero in thy sight, O goddess” (1.2.5i), [he does so].
6.2.3.19. With the words, “May I not be separated from the abundance of wealth,” the sacrificer [says], “May the abundance of wealth not be separated from me. 6.2.3.20.
With the verse, “Make the earth swell” (TS 2.4.8.2f), he pours out a vessel of water into that well with the words, “Break open this [earth]; release the heavenly skin-bag. 6.2.3.21.
The wife returns, treading upon the footprint.
6.2.3.22. It is measured out by the king.
6.2.4 (6.3.1 Cal) [The guest-offering].
6.2.4.1. It is measured out by the king.
6.2.4.2. On a red hide, a fourfold garment with its fringes directed toward the north is spread out.
6.2.4.3. At the edge of the water, a Brāhmaṇa sits to the south.

6.2.4.4. Having touched water and performed the ritual purification (*mārjana*), and having taken the *upāṃśu* cup, he approaches with the *Chandomas*, saying: "This is your Gāyatra portion. Then the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer address the King Soma: "Tell this to Soma for me: 'This is your Triṣṭubh portion'; tell this to Soma for me: 'This is your Jagatī portion'; tell this to King Soma for me: 'Go to the world, the sovereignty of the Chandomas.'"

6.2.4.5. Having arrived, he touches it with the formula, “May your stalk be joined with my stalk” (1.2.6a), and [continues] with, “Joint by joint, your fragrance and clarity are the draught” (1.2.6a). Then, 6.2.4.6. with the *aticchandas* verse, “To that god Savitṛ... (1.2.6b), he measures out the King [Soma] one by one, omitting each time [the first part], five times with the sacrificial formula (*yajus*), “I praise the seer-minded one... through grace for the sake of light” (1.2.6b), and five times silently. 6.2.4.7.
With the formula, “For the subjects, thee” (1.2.6c1), he gathers the stalk together; they desire the stalk to be placed upon the skin.
6.2.4.8. With the words, “For out-breath thee,” he ties the two ends together. 6.2.4.9. With the words, “For diffused breath thee,” he fastens it with a cord.
6.2.4.10. Having untied it with the words, “Do thou breathe after the offspring,” and having placed the *upāṃśu* cup [within], he breathes after it.
6.2.4.11. Having bound it with the Soma-turban while reciting, "May the subjects breathe after you" (TS 1.2.6.3), he places the King (Soma) right there upon the hide.
6.2.4.12. Then the Soma-seller takes it himself. 6.2.4.13. As he is taking it, he pours water from a water-pot over his feet.

6.2.4.14. Having risen from the well with the words, “I purchase your *soma*,” the *adhvaryu* mutters the formula for the purchase: “Full of vigor, full of milk, full of strength, overcoming the enemy.

6.2.4.15. “O seller of *soma*, is your *soma* for sale? “It is for sale,” he replies. 6.2.4.16. “I shall purchase it from you with a cow,” he says; “I shall purchase it from you with a small coin (*kalā*),” he says to him in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
6.2.4.17. “Soma the King deserves more than this,” says the Soma-seller.

6.2.4.18. “Soma the King deserves even more than this,” says the Adhvaryu: “I shall buy you with the great majesty of the cow, with her froth. 6.2.4.19. “Soma the King deserves more than this,” says the Soma-seller. “Soma the King deserves even more than this,” says the Adhvaryu: “I shall buy you with the great majesty of the cow, with her foot.”

6.2.4.20. “King Soma deserves more than this,” says the Soma-seller. “King Soma indeed deserves more than this,” says the Adhvaryu. “But the greatness of the cow is great; I shall buy him from you for half of her. That was already settled. 6.2.4.21. “King Soma deserves more than this,” says the Soma-seller. “King Soma indeed deserves more than this,” says the Adhvaryu. “But the greatness of the cow is great,” he said, referring to half of the enjoyment.

6.2.4.22. “The milk of this [cow] is indeed: fresh milk, milk that has been heated, curdled milk, whey, curds, fresh butter, and clarified butter; offspring subsist upon these. “I shall purchase [the cow] from you,” [he says]. 6.4.2.23. “The King has been purchased,” says the Soma-seller. “Declare the birds! [he says].

6.2.4.24. He says to him, "This is the royal purchase-cow": "We shall protect those for you with another; this is the goat, this is the moon, this is the swelling one. Her son is this one who overcomes the yoke-pole; this is the protector of men, these two are a pair, this is the garment, this is the four-bowl measure, this is the butter-bowl, this is the tuft of *balbaja* grass—take her hand.
6.2.4.25. Then, with the words, "I buy your bright with the bright" (1.2.7a2), he places gold in his hand; with the words, "the moon with the moon, the immortal with the immortal," [he places it].
6.2.4.26. From the verse, “śaṃyak te goḥ,” the Adhvaryu takes up the King Soma.
6.2.4.27. With the words, “asme candrāṇi,” he wipes the gold. 6.2.4.28. With the words, “tapasas tanūr asi,” he touches the goat by its neck, saying, “prajāpate varṇa.”

6.2.4.29. With that [cow], turning toward himself, he drives away the Soma-seller with her turned away from him, saying: "With the last of thy cattle, I buy thee who art nourishing a thousandfold prosperity.
(1.2.7c2) 6.2.4.30. With "Thy kinship is with us" (1.2.7d), he turns back toward the sacrificer; with "May thy riches rest upon me," he turns toward himself.
6.2.4.31. Then he passes along behind her.
6.2.4.32. Then the Soma-seller receives them.

6.2.4.33. With the words, "Here I tie the necks of the biting serpents" (TS 6.1.10.4), he ties on a black tuft of wool; with the words, "He who hates us and whom we hate—here I seize his neck," he ties it. 6.2.4.34.
With the verse, "Light for us" (TS 1.2.7.e), he hands a white tuft of wool to the sacrificer.
6.2.4.35. "Upon the seller of Soma, darkness!"—with this, he pierces the seller of Soma with a black [antelope skin].
6.2.4.36. Right there, he sits down upon the hide.
6.2.4.37. While the sacrificer is within the sacrificial enclosure (antarvedi), the Adhvaryu brings him a drink.
6.2.4.38. He awaits the king: "O Mitra, come to us" (6.2.5).
(Cf. *Bśs* 6.15 in general) 6.2.5.1.
"O Mitra, come to us, bestowing good friendship" (1.2.7f).
6.2.5.2. With the words, “Enter the right thigh of Indra” (1.2.7g), he places him upon the right thigh with the words, “Desiring the desiring one; pleasant, the pleasant one. 6.2.5.3.

With the words, “The birds with beautiful wings approached Indra” (RV 10.113.4), he uncovers him with the verse: “The Priyamedha seers, imploring, say: ‘Dispel the darkness, fill our eyesight; release us like those bound and cast down’” (TB 2.5.8.3).

6.2.5.4. With the formula, “O Śvāna, Bhrāja” (1.2.71h), he points out the royal-purchase animals [to the dogs], saying: “O Aṅghāri, Baṃbhāri, Hasta, Suhasta, Kṛśānu! These are the Soma-purchasers; guard them; let no one deceive you. 6.2.5.5. Having taken up the King [Soma] with the formula, “Up with life, with good life” (1.2.8a), he rises, saying: “We have risen up with the sap of the plants, up with the vigor of Parjanya, up along with the immortals.”
6.2.5.6. At the southern edge of the altar, they place the Soma-cart facing eastward; he approaches the Soma-cart with the formula, “Follow the wide mid-region” (TS 1.2.8b).
6.2.5.7. With the formula, “Thou art the seat of Aditi” (TS 1.2.8c), he spreads a black antelope skin on the Soma-cart, with its neck toward the east and the hair side upward.
6.2.5.8. With the formula, “Sit on the seat of Aditi” (TS 1.2.8d), he places the King (Soma) upon the black antelope skin.

6.2.5.9. With the words, “The bull propped up the sky and the mid-region” (RV 8.41.10c), he worships the one standing nearby; then with, “He measured out the breadth of the earth; the sovereign sat down among all beings” (RV 8.41.10d-f). 6.2.5.10.

With the words, “All these are the ordinances of Varuṇa” (RV 1.2.8e2,f), he wraps the Soma-carrying cart around with a cloth, saying, “In the woods, in the mid-region... the Soma on the mountain” (RV 1.2.8e).

6.2.5.11. With the verse, “Upwards that Jātavedas... (1.2.8g), he fastens a black antelope skin, with its neck pointing upward and the hair on the outside, onto the post-base, saying, “The rays bear the god Sūrya so that all may see him” (1.2.8h). 6.2.5.12. With the formula, “O two oxen, come hither, you who bear the yoke,” (1.2.8h var.), he addresses the two draft-oxen: “Tearless, not slayers of heroes, impellers of sacred knowledge, protect the yoke-pole and the yoke. 6.2.5.13. With the formula, “Thou art the support of Varuṇa,” (1.2.8i), he touches the supporting beam.
6.2.5.14. Having yoked the ox and fastened the yoke-halter with the formula, “Thou art the supporting pillar of Varuṇa” (cf. 1.2.8k), he drives the peg into the ground. 6.2.5.15.
With the formula, “The noose of Varuṇa is cast off” (1.2.8l), he places it over the ox.
6.2.5.16. In this very same manner, he yokes the second ox.
6.2.5.17. He fastens the cord either to the support-beam or to the sacrificial post. 6.2.5.18. Between the two *iṣe* formulas, the Subrahmaṇya priest stands holding branches of the *palāśa* tree.

6.2.5.19. Without climbing up, they turn around toward the south. [The Adhvaryu] says: "Recite for the Soma being carried forth!"—[the Subrahmaṇya replies: "O Subrahmaṇya, invoke the Subrahmaṇyā; wait for a moment, the sacrificer will follow with his invocation."

6.2.5.19. He calls out three times in a low voice, "Subrahmaṇyoṃ, Subrahmaṇyoṃ, Subrahmaṇyoṃ," while the sacrificer [recites] four times; the Subrahmaṇya priest calls out three times loudly. 6.2.5.20.
With the words, "Descend, O Lord of the World (bhuvaspate)," the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite, ending with, "May Viśvāvasu bestow all names."

6.2.5.21. At the point where [the text says], "Becoming a hawk, fly away" (ŚB 1.2.9b,c), when the Soma-carrying cart turns northward in front of the hall, the two of them touch the roof-covering, not the cord, [saying]: "In the house of the sacrificer, prepared by the gods... the sacrificer finds wealth. 6.2.5.22. Having run past, the Agnīdh stands firm with the fire-brand; the Pratiprasthātṛ [stands] with the cakes for the sacrificial offering.
6.2.5.23. With the formula, “Homage to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa” (TS 1.2.9d), the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite, “Praise the great god” (TS 1.2.9e).
6.2.5.24. With the formula, “Thou art the pillar of Varuṇa” (TS 1.2.9e), he props [the post].
6.2.5.25. With the formula, “Thou art the release of Varuṇa’s pillar” (TS 1.2.9f), he pulls out the pin (śamyā).
6.2.5.26. Reciting, "The noose of Varuṇa is released" (TS 1.2.9.g), he unyokes the ox from the side where he was approached.
6.2.5.27. One ox becomes unyoked, while the other remains unyoked. 6.2.5.28. Then he receives the guest-offering (ātithya).
6.2.5.29. While his wife has taken hold of him, he should say, with her permission: "O wife, give your consent. 6.2.5.30.
Having set out the sacrificial implements and having carried forward the water, he pours out the *ātithya* oblation [with the formula]: "Thee, belonging to the god...

6.2.6.1. "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan—[Savitṛ-mantra]—you are the guest-offering for Agni; I pour you out, acceptable to Viṣṇu. You are the guest-offering for Soma; I pour you out, acceptable to Viṣṇu. You are the guest-offering for the Guest; I pour you out, acceptable to Viṣṇu. For Agni, the giver of increase of wealth, I pour you out."

"I offer you, acceptable to Viṣṇu" (1.2.10a4 with addition); "I offer you, acceptable to the Śyena, the bearer of Soma, to Viṣṇu" (1.2.10a5 with addition)—with these words, he pours out five handfuls of rice. Once the pouring is completed, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses. Having released his speech at the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*), he unyokes the other ox and causes the King (Soma) to enter.

6.2.6.4. If it is a *pravargya*-rite, they lift up the *samrāj* first; if it is a *pravargya*-rite, the *samrāj* is placed on the throne-seat (*āsandi*) higher [than the *rājan*]. 6.2.6.5. With the verse, "Those abodes which are yours (1.2.10b)," he causes the *rājan* to enter; [he recites]: "With the oblation they sacrifice to all those [abodes] of yours = O Soma, [enter] the dwellings. 6.2.6.6. Once seated, he becomes the *samrāj*; then he sets down the *rājan* with the formula: "Thou art the seat of Aditi; sit upon the seat of Aditi (1.2.10c)."
6.2.6.7. Together with a black antelope skin, he sat down upon the throne-seat (āsandi).
6.2.6.8. With the words, “O you of firm vows,” he worships the one who has sat down, saying, “Varuṇa, the wise one, for sovereignty over the wives.
6.2.6.9. With the words, “You are Varuṇa, of firm vows,” he wraps both throne-seats with a cloth, saying, “You belong to Varuṇa; for Varuṇa, you!”

6.2.6.10. With the verse, "May there be welfare from the gods" (TS 1.2.10.e), he pours water from the water-vessel behind the royal throne-seat (*rājāsandi*), provided that the *pravargya* ceremony was performed for the previous *samrāj*. He says: "May we not be severed from the service of the gods.
6.2.6.11. He says: "May I not come between Agni and the King (Soma) and be harmed. 6.2.6.12. This guest-offering (*ātithya*) cake for Viṣṇu is being cooked on nine potsherds.

6.2.6.13. Its ritual materials are: a prastara of *aśvavāla* grass, a crosswise blade of sugarcane, enclosing sticks of *kārṣmarya* wood, and chips for the *raṇī*. 6.2.6.14. When this [milk] has been boiled, he carries away the *stambayajus*.
6.2.6.15. He encloses the altar (*vedi*).
6.2.6.16. He mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
6.2.6.17. Being impelled, he performs the subsequent tracing around (*parigrāha*).
6.2.6.18. Having leveled and propped it up, he issues the call.

6.2.6.19. "Set down the *prokṣaṇī* waters; set down the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmābarhis*); cleanse the *sruva* and the *sruk* ladles; gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter (*ājya*)"—thus they do this. 6.2.6.20. Having cleansed the *sruk* ladles, he takes all the portions of clarified butter in four scoops each; he sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass; he sprinkles the altar (*vedi*); he sprinkles what has been placed near. 6.2.6.21. [He sprinkles] the *vedim*, he sprinkles the *āsannam*.
6.2.6.22. Having poured out water, he takes up the *prastara* (grass-bundle).
6.2.6.23. He spreads the *barhis* (sacrificial grass). 6.2.6.24. Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) made of *kārṣmarya* wood.
6.2.6.25. He places two fuel-sticks on the fire. 6.2.6.26. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing-sticks, he yokes the fire.

6.2.6.27. Having returned, he places a crosswise twig of *ikṣu* grass; upon the two crosswise twigs, a *prastara* of horse-tail grass; upon the *prastara*, the *juhū* ladle; and the other two *barhis* blades upon the *prastara*.
6.2.6.28. When [the fire] is near, he recites the *apānagraha* verses and the *pṛśni* verses.

6.2.6.29. Having touched [the fire] together with the formula, "The steadfast ones have sat down; that which is mine, O Agni... (*dhruvā asadan yan me agne*), he recites the *saṃbhāra* formulas and the *caturhotṛ* formulas.
6.2.6.30. He proceeds with the fire produced by friction (*nirmanthya*).
6.2.6.31. He recites the invitatory verse for the fire being kindled.

6.2.6.32. He places the entire fuel-stick (*idhma*) onto the fire; he does not leave any fuel-stick remaining. 6.2.6.33. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*), he says: "O *Āgnīdh*, cleanse the fires three times each! Having crossed over without touching the two offering-ladles (*sruc*), having anointed the *dhruvā* ladle and set it down, he chooses the *pravara*.
6.2.6.34. The Hotṛ sits down.
6.2.6.35. Being impelled, he takes up the two offering-spoons and performs the *prayāja* offerings.
6.2.6.36. At the fourth [offering], he pours everything together from the *upabhṛt* spoon; he performs all the *prayāja* offerings from the *upabhṛt*.

6.2.6.38. Having performed the *prayāja* offerings and stepped across, he sprinkles the *dhruvā* ladle with clarified butter, but not the *upabhṛt* ladle; for that one remains empty. 6.2.6.39. He offers the two *ājyabhāga* portions; he sacrifices to Viṣṇu with the oblation; [four times]; he sacrifices to the *sviṣṭakṛt*. 6.2.6.40.
Having stepped across and placed the two ladles in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
6.2.6.41. Having touched water, he cuts off a portion of the *iḍā*.
6.2.6.42. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places it for the *agnīdh*.
6.2.6.43. They consume [the portions], they sprinkle themselves with water, and they carry [the *iḍā*] around.
6.2.6.44. When the *prāśitra* has been consumed by the Brahman priest, he offers the oblation of the *caturhotṛ* formula without regard for the continuity of the sequence.

6.2.6.45. Having replenished the *dhruvā* ladle, and having placed gold into the cup (*camasa*) while reciting the formula for the bestowing of the vow, "I take thee for Āpati" (TS 1.2.10f), he divides the *tānūnaptra* five times, reciting "I take thee for the protector" (TS 6.2.7).

6.2.7.1. “I take you for the troop; I take you for Tanūnapāt; I take you for Śākvara; I take you for the most powerful in strength. 6.2.7.2. Then the sacrificer smells [the vessel] three times, saying: “I offer you into Prajāpati, into the mind. 6.2.7.3. They carry away the Tanūnaptra [vessel]: the Brahman, the sacrificer, the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, the Pratiprasthātṛ, and the Āgnīdhra, with the formula: “You are unassailable, unassailable by others; the vigor of the gods, protecting from imprecation, not to be imprecated. (1.2.10.2g)
6.2.7.4. Then he causes the sacrificer to recite: "May the Lord of Consecration approve my consecration; may the Lord of Penance approve my penance. (1.2.10h1) 6.2.7.5.

"With this," he says, handing over the cup for the offering of the vow (*vrata*), "in the same manner, having heated [the water] in the afternoon, you shall hand over the vow. He hands it over to him accordingly. 6.2.7.6. "Which shall we do first? he asks: "Shall we cause the King [Soma] to swell? Or shall we lead him to the intermediate consecration (*avāntaradīkṣā*)? This is indeed a choice between alternatives.

6.2.7.7. With the words, “Thou art the fuel-stick of the intermediate consecration,” he takes up a fuel-stick. 6.2.7.8. Having sprinkled himself with water while reciting, “O Agni, Lord of Vows” (TS 1.2.11d + addition), he places the fuel-stick on the fire with the formula: “Thou art the lord of vows among vows; that body of mine which is here, let it be in thee; that body of thine which is here, let it be in me. O Lord of Vows, may the vows of us two who observe the vow be together; may our bodies be together. Svāhā! 6.2.7.9. He tightens his girdle more closely and makes his fists tighter.
6.2.7.10. He observes the heated vow (*taptavrata*). He purifies himself with the *madantī* waters. 6.2.7.11. He releases the previous vow-food (*vratana*).
6.2.7.12. With the words, "O Agni, that body of yours which is Rudra-like (1.2.11e)," he partakes of the vow-food, saying, "With that protect us; to that body of yours, svāhā!"
6.2.7.13. Having mounted these [fires], the fires themselves here, having touched the *madantī* waters, cause the King [Soma] to swell.

6.2.7.14. The Brahman and the Sacrificer [stand] to the south; the Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Pratiprasthātṛ, and Agnīdh [stand] to the north. Having loosened [the Soma stalks] and placed the *upāṃśu* vessel [down], they cause the King to swell with the formula: "O divine Soma, may each stalk of thine swell" (TS 1.2.11a,b + addition). [They continue: "For Indra, the winner of the single prize; may I attain the pressing; may there be well-being until the conclusion. 6.2.7.15. Having inspected their hands, they enter.
6.2.7.16. Having arrived and touched the *madantī* waters, he separates the two offering-spoons with the two *vājavatī* verses. 6.2.7.17. He anoints the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*).
6.2.7.18. He does not cause the announcement (*āśrāvaya*) for them.

6.2.7.19. He tears off a blade from the *prastara* (grass-bundle); he anoints it on its edges. 6.2.7.20. Upon that [blade], while reciting, "Desired wealth... (VS 1.2.11c var.), they conceal it at the southern hip with the formula, "In the impulse for Bhaga... homage to the earth. 6.2.7.21.

With the formula, "May I consort with thee, accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ" (VS 1.2.5h,i + addition), the Neṣṭṛ causes the wife to be concealed behind the *vedī* cloth, [reciting]: "O thou of heroic seed... [may I not be separated] from thee through the abundance of wealth; may I not be separated from thee through the abundance of wealth. (VS 1.2.5k,l).

6.2.7.22. [The Adhvaryu says: "The fires rejoice, 'O waters! [The Āgnīdhra responds: "They rejoice. He [the Adhvaryu] says: "Run hither with them. 6.2.7.23. He takes up the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*), and having passed over them, he hands them to the Āgnīdhra.
6.2.7.24. Having silently poured out the *praṇītā* water within the altar, he binds a handful of grass to the *prastara* and sets it down.
6.2.7.25. They cleanse the fires with the *madantī* waters.
6.2.7.26. The guest-offering (*ātithya*) is concluded.

6.3.1.1. Having shifted the two hearths (*akhara*) right here, he says: "If it is with the *pravargya*, having performed the *pravargya* rite, he issues the command: 'Set the oblation on the fire; set the boiling water on the fire. [N1,65a8] 6.3.1.2. Now, if it is without the *pravargya*, he issues the command in exactly this same way.
6.3.1.3. When the clarified butter has congealed, he performs the *stambayajus* rite; he encloses the altar (*vedi*); he mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
6.3.1.4. Once the impulse has been given, he performs the second tracing around.

6.3.1.5. Having leveled the ground and propped it up, he issues the command: "Set down the boiling water; place the fuel and the sacrificial grass nearby; cleanse the dipping-spoon and the two offering-spoons; come forth with the oblation! [x10] 6.3.1.6. They do this.

6.3.1.7. When the *sruva* is the third [among the ladles], he anoints the two *sruca*s and takes the clarified butter (*ājya*): he takes eight portions into the *juhū*, and four portions into the *upabhṛt*. 6.3.1.8.
At the time for the *dhruvā*, he lifts up the vessel of clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*).
6.3.1.9. He sprinkles the fuel-sticks (*idhma*) and the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). He sprinkles the altar (*vedi*). He sprinkles the articles that have been set down.

6.3.1.10. Having poured out the water, he takes the *prastara* [grass-bundle]. He spreads the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). 6.3.1.11. Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).
6.3.1.12. He places these very fuel-sticks made of *kārṣmarya* wood upon the fire.
6.3.1.13. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*), he yokes the fire.

6.3.1.14. Having returned, he places the crosswise stalks of sugarcane (*aikṣavī*) down; upon the two crosswise stalks, the *prastara* of horse-hair; upon the *prastara*, the *juhū* ladle; and upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the other [ladles]. 6.3.1.15. Having set them down and touched them all together with the formula, "The firm ones have sat down... that which is mine, O Agni" (cf. MS 1.1.12:8.3; KS 1.11:6; VS 2.6), he recites the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula.
6.3.1.16. He recites the invitatory verse for the fire as it is being kindled. 6.3.1.17. He recites three additional verses, or nine in a continuous sequence.
6.3.1.18. The Adhvaryu seeks to encompass those [verses] with the fuel-stick; he does not leave any fuel-stick remaining.

6.3.1.19. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* ladle, he says: "O *Āgnīdh*, cleanse the fires once each! 6.3.1.20. Having stood up, he should choose the *pravara*.
6.3.1.21. He says, "O, cause [the Āgnīdh] to announce," and "Sit down, O Hotṛ."
6.3.1.22. This alone is the *pravara* here; he does not choose the *ṛṣis*.
6.3.1.23. The *hotṛ* sits down. 6.3.1.24. Being impelled, he takes up the two offering-spoons (*srucau*).

6.3.1.25. Stepping across, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni. 6.3.1.26. He says: "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard! He sacrifices to Agni. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers half of what was drawn in eight portions.
6.3.1.27. He says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Soma. He says: "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard!"
6.3.1.28. While pouring [the butter] together, he says, “*Āśrāvaya*,” and then, “Sacrifice to Soma. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering.

6.3.1.29. He says, “Recite the invitatory verse for Viṣṇu. 6.3.1.30. While pouring [the butter] together, he says, “*O śrāvaya*,” and then, “Sacrifice to Viṣṇu. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers all of this.
6.3.1.31. Having stepped across and set down the two *sruva*-ladles in their respective places, and having touched the *madantī* water, they cause the King (Soma) to swell.

6.3.1.32. The Brahman and the Sacrificer [stand] to the south; the Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Pratiprasthātṛ, and Agnīdh [stand] to the north. Having untied [the Soma] and placed the *upāṃśu* cup [down], they cause the King to swell with the formula: "O divine Soma, may stalk after stalk of thine swell. Then, with the formula: "May I attain the pressing for Indra; may I reach the end in safety," they wipe their hands and rinse them. [Cf. 6.2.7.12]

6.3.1.34. Having come and touched the *madantī* waters, he separates the two offering-ladles (*srucau*) with the formula: "Here, as a sacrificer, may I follow after and conquer the victory of Agni, Soma, Viṣṇu, and the deities. With this, he moves the *juhū* ladle toward the east. 6.3.1.35. "Here, as a sacrificer, by means of Agni, Soma, and Viṣṇu, and by the deities, I drive away misfortune, evil, the rival, and death"—with this, he pushes the *upabhṛt* ladle toward the west.

6.3.1.36. He anoints the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*). He does not cause the announcement (*āśrāvaya*) for them. He pulls out the grass-bundle (*prastara*). He anoints it on its joints. 6.3.1.37. Upon it, with the verse, "Wished-for riches... (TS 1.2.11c), he hides it in the southern buttock [of the altar], saying, "At the impulse, to Bhaga—homage to the Earth! (TS 1.2.11d).

6.3.1.38. With the formula, “May I consort with thee, O Tvaṣṭṛ-matī” (TS 1.2.5h + addition), he causes the wife—who has been lost from view behind the garment—to recite the *nihnava* (formula of concealment): “O thou of heroic seed, in thy sight may I not be separated from the abundance of wealth; may the abundance of wealth not be separated from me. [cf. 6.2.7.18] [N1, 66a3] 6.3.1.39. Having placed the *prastara* (grass-bundle) in his left hand, he strikes at the *upasad* (oblation) from the butter-pot with the *sruva* spoon using the formula, “That body of thine, O Agni, which is iron-like” (TS 1.2.11f1), [and then] with the formula, “The most excellent one, thou art in the abyss” (TS 1.2.11f2). [Note: TS 1.2.11f contains three mantras in a condensed form.]
6.3.1.40. With the words, “I have warded off the fierce speech” (ŚB 1.2.11g1), he touches the southern enclosing-stick (*paridhi*).
6.3.1.41. With the words, “With that, protect us; to that of yours, *svāhā*” (the latter part of ŚB 1.2.11g1), he makes an offering.
6.3.1.42. With the words, “I have warded off the brilliant speech” (ŚB 1.2.11g2, without *svāhā*), he throws it away.

6.3.1.43. He follows with the mantra: "May Agni be in harmony with the earth"—"In harmony with the path of the oblation, you have stood firm like a spear; O sharp one, pierce him apart! Agni is your point, Soma is your barb, Viṣṇu is your socket; you are discharged by Rudra, your name is 'The Young. Homage be to you! Do not harm me! Discharged from here, go to him who hates us and whom we hate, with both [ends]—with this one and with that one."
6.3.1.44. [The Adhvaryu says: "O fires, rejoice, O waters! He replies, "They rejoice. [The Adhvaryu says: "Run hither with them. [See 6.2.7.19. 6.3.1.45.

He takes up the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*). Having pushed them aside, he hands them over to the Āgnīdhra. 6.3.1.46. Having silently poured out the *praṇītā* water within the altar, and having tied a blade of grass to the *prastara* bundle, he sets it down.
6.3.1.47. They purify the fires with the *madantī* waters.
6.3.1.48. This *upasad* rite is concluded.
6.3.1.49. With this very same [rite], he proceeds in the afternoon.
6.3.1.E. They transpose only the *ājya* [chants].
C83] 6.3.2.1. They transpose only the *ājya* [chants].
6.3.2.2. He takes four portions of ghee into the *juhū* ladle and eight portions into the *upabhṛt* ladle. 6.3.2.3. Having performed the ritual with that [ladle], they remain for this night.

6.3.2.4. They scout the eastern direction... either by means of the *makha* [formula] or by means of the *śroṇi* [formula]; at that time, they drive in a peg at the spot where the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) will stand.
6.3.2.5. In the morning, having released his speech with the *āditya* cup, he proceeds with the *rajāśayā* cup.
6.3.2.6. The beginning of that oblation is: “O Agni, that body of yours which lies in the dust” (1.2.11f2). It concludes with: “The most lofty, dwelling in the abyss” (cf.
6.3.1.28). 6.3.2.7. The beginning of the accompanying formula is: “In harmony with Vāyu, in the intermediate space. It concludes with: “In harmony with the path of Truth” (cf. 6.3.1.32).

6.3.2.8. Having performed the rite with that [cord], and having taken up the cord and the pegs, he strides five steps eastward. He drives a peg there; that marks the edge of the altar (vedi). 6.3.2.9. Fifteen steps to the south; he drives a peg there. 6.3.2.10.
Fifteen steps to the north; he drives a peg there.

6.3.2.11. From the first peg, he strides thirty-six steps toward the east. There he drives a peg; that is the location for the sacrificial post (yūpa). 6.3.2.12. Twelve steps to the south, there he drives a peg. Twelve steps to the north, there he drives a peg. 6.3.2.13.
From the northernmost peg, he strides three steps toward the west. There he drives a peg; that is the location for the pit (cātvāla).

6.3.2.14. He drives three pegs into the ground at a distance of one *prādeśa* each; that is the time for the northern [corner]. 6.3.2.15. He drives six pegs into the ground at a distance of one *prādeśa* each; that is the center of the *āgnīdhra* shed. 6.3.2.16.
That is the third [measurement] of the altar. From the peg marking the time for the sacrificial post (*yūpa*), he measures out the *uttaravedi* on all sides as ten paces to the west.

6.3.2.17. He strides five steps westward from the *uttaravedi*; there he drives in a peg. That is the center of the two *havirdhāna* sheds. 6.3.2.18. One step to the south; there he drives in a peg. That is the location for the *uparava* holes. 6.3.2.19.
From the first peg driven in, he strides five steps eastward; there he drives in a peg. That is the center of the *sadas*.
6.3.2.20. He drives in a single southern peg; that marks the spot for the Audumbarī post. 6.3.2.21.
At the time of the *uparava* holes, he performs the *staṃbayajus* rite. He encloses the altar (*vedi*) and mutters the *karaṇa* formula. 6.3.2.22.

With the words, "O men, having come here, prepare this altar," they level it, saying: "At the height of heaven, at the navel of the earth, so that this sacrificer may not come to harm—make this altar rich in Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, and the Viśve Devas; O makers of the altar, make it! Make it!"

6.3.2.23. “They prepare the altar. 6.3.2.24. He issues the call: “The wooden sword (śphya) and the water-vessel! “Bring the yoke-pin (śamyā)! Come, O Sacrificer! O Āgnīdhra, sit down upon the high altar (uttaravedi). [cf. 5.1.1.24] 6.3.2.25. Having dug up the area of the pit (cātvāla) with the wooden sword, he sprinkles it with the water-vessel, saying: “Make the earth swell! “Split open this celestial firmament; give us of the celestial water; as Lord, release the stream. [TS 1.4.8f]

6.3.2.26. He measures around with a *śamyā*. 6.3.2.27. Having placed the *śamyā* to the south pointing eastward, he marks it from the north with the wooden sword (*sphya*), saying, "Thou art my path to prosperity. To the west, [he places the *śamyā*] pointing northward, saying, "Thou art my path to refreshment. To the east, [he places it] pointing northward, saying, "Protect me from distress. To the north, [he places it] pointing eastward, saying, "Protect me from agitation."

6.3.2.28. With the formula, “O Agni Aṅgiras, look at the sky by name,” he strikes at the loose earth in the middle with the wooden sword (sphya). 6.3.2.29. With the formula, “He who is on this earth—come with life and by name,” he carries it away with the words, “That which you have placed... for you. 6.3.2.30. Having carried it to the east of the Āgnīdhra fire-shed, he places it upon the altar.

6.3.2.31. With the formula, “O Agni Aṅgiras,” he strikes a third time. With the words, “He who is on the third earth,” he takes it up; with the words, “Come with life...,” he carries it away; and with the words, “That which you have placed... for you,” he deposits it.
6.3.2.32. Having carried [the earth] to the Āgnīdhra fire-altar by the eastern way, he places it on the Uttaravedi.
6.3.2.33. He carries the fourth portion silently. 6.3.2.34. Having moistened it with water, he mixes it together, saying: "Thou art a lioness; thou art a buffalo-cow."
6.3.2.35 With the formula, "O wide one, spread yourself; may the lord of the sacrifice spread wide for you," they cause it to spread with the wooden sword (*sphya*).

6.3.2.36 With the formula, "You are firm, you are firm," he strikes it three times with the yoke-pin (*śamyā*). 6.3.2.37 Having made it a span (*prādeśa*) on all sides, well-proportioned, and four-cornered, he sprinkles it with water with the formula, "Be purified for the gods," and [again] with the formula, "Be beautified for the gods."
6.3.2.38. Having covered themselves from above with these very waters and having performed the ritual with the *rajāśayā* vessel, they remain overnight [cf.
6.3.2.39. In the morning, having released their speech by means of the sun, they perform the ritual with the *harāśayā* vessel.
6.3.2.40. The beginning of that oblation is: "O Agni, that body of yours which lies in the heat" (1.2.11f3).
6.3.2.41. It is completed with: "The highest, you stand in the abyss" [cf.
6.1.4.28]. 6.3.2.42. The beginning of the following mantra is: "Together with Sūrya by day."

6.3.2.43. "In harmony with the path of Truth"—thus it is established. [cf. 6.3.2.6] 6.3.2.44. Having performed the rite with that [verse], while stepping out, he says: "Hand over the half-fast-food. This very [formula] is reversed. 6.3.2.45. Then he performs the rite with the final Upasad.
6.3.2.46. He causes the *pravargya* vessel to be removed while it is covered.
6.3.2.47. Having offered the oblation to Sūrya, they kindle the fuel-stick (*idhma*) and prepare the supporting ladles (*upayamanī*), if the rite includes the *pravargya*.
6.3.2.49. Now, if the rite does not include the *pravargya*, they kindle the fuel-stick right here and [prepare] the supporting ladles. [cf. 5.1.4.40–41]

6.3.2.50. They prepare the materials for the *uttaravedi*. 6.3.3 (Cal 6.4.3) [N1,67a9; M179; T1,212] 6.3.3.1. The materials for the *uttaravedi* are: *guggulu* resin, fragrant reed-grass (*sugandhitejana*), tufts of white wool, enclosing sticks made of *pautudrava* wood, ... [lacuna], fivefold-drawn clarified butter, and fivefold-drawn clarified butter [cf. 5.1.2.1].

6.3.3.2. He divides the foot into three parts. 6.3.3.3. Right here he scatters one third over the fire; he places one third in the supporting ladles (*upayamanī*); and he sets aside one third for the purpose of anointing the axle. 6.3.3.4. When the fuel is aflame, he takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter. He offers that [as follows]: [cf. 5.1.2.2].

6.3.3.5. With the words, “Agni has looked along the forefront of the dawns” (VS 4.1.2k), he performs the *anukhyāti* (the lighting-up); [he recites] “He has stretched out along the days, svāhā! 6.3.3.6. Having offered [this], he should take five portions of clarified butter (*pañcagṛhīta*). 6.3.3.7. While lifting up the fuel-stick (*idhma*), they place the supporting ladles (*upayamanī*) [upon it] (cf. 5.1.2.7).
6.3.3.8. He says, "Recite for the fire as it is being carried forward," and [the Adhvaryu responds], "Run along with one wooden sword.
6.3.3.9. Scratching with the wooden sword, the one with the single wooden sword (ekasphya) runs along toward the high altar (uttaravedi).
6.3.3.10. With the verse, "The sage of the sacrifice spreads out the path" (TS 3.5.5f), the Adhvaryu causes the sacrificer to recite.

6.3.3.11 Having stepped over [the fire] with the mantra: “Upon the back of the Nāka, in the luminous realm of heaven, by which thou carriest the oblation, thou goest as a messenger from here, wise and most bountiful,” he sprinkles the northern navel [of the altar] with the formula: “May Indraghoṣa protect thee in the east with the Vasus; may Manojava protect thee in the south with the Pitṛs; may Pracetas protect thee in the west with the Rudras; may Viśvakarman protect thee in the north with the Ādityas; may Bṛhaspati protect thee from above with all the gods.”
6.3.3.12. Whatever remains of the sprinkling water, he pours it out to the south upon the track of the wooden sword (sphya) for the great oblation. [cf.
5.1.2.12] [N1,67b4] 6.3.3.13. He meditates upon whomsoever the sacrificer hates.

6.3.3.14. Having touched water and taken five portions of clarified butter, he throws gold into it and draws the line diagonally across the navel from north to south, saying: "Thou art a lioness, overcoming rivals, svāhā!"—thus on the right shoulder; "Thou art a lioness, winning good offspring, svāhā!"—thus on the left hip; "Thou art a lioness, winning abundance of wealth, svāhā!"—thus on the right hip; "Thou art a lioness, winning the Ādityas, svāhā!"—thus on the left shoulder; "Thou art a lioness, bring the gods for the god-loving sacrificer, svāhā!"—thus in the middle. [cf. 5.1.2.13]
