6.3.3.15. With the words, “For the beings, thee,” he lifts up the offering-spoon (*sruk*).

6.3.3.16. With the words, “Thou art the life of all; make firm the earth,” he places the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*), made of *pūtudru* wood. 6.3.3.17. With the words, “Thou art a steadfast dweller; make firm the intermediate space,” he places the southern enclosing-stick.

6.3.3.18. With the formula, “Thou art the consumer of the imperishable; make firm the sky,” he places the northern portion. 6.3.3.19. With the formulas, “Thou art the ash of Agni; thou art the soil of Agni,” he pours down the ritual materials (*saṃbhārān*). 6.3.3.20. He makes an oblation over them with the residue of the ghee, saying: “The gods found that which was hidden in the cave—the domestic animals of every form, though diverse in appearance, yet being many, they are of one form. May there be delight in me for those seven; *svāhā*!”
6.3.3.21. He pours out the supporting ladles (upayamanī). 6.3.3.22. He sets down the fire.
6.3.3.23. With the formula, "Thou art Prajāpati, Viśvakarman," he pays reverence to the fire that has been set down, saying, "May that [be] yonder sun; may this Agni be well-loved by the cattle."

6.3.3.24. He offers the *atimukti* oblations with the formula: “May Agni, knowing, lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it; announce the sacrifice to the gods; further and further extend the lord of the sacrifice—*svāhā*. May Vāyu, knowing, lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it... extend the lord of the sacrifice—*svāhā*. May Sūrya, knowing, lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it... extend the lord of the sacrifice—*svāhā*. May the Sacrifice, knowing, lead the sacrifice; may those who destroy the sacrifice not find it; announce the sacrifice to the gods; further and further extend the lord of the sacrifice—*svāhā*. [N1,68a1]
6.3.3.25. Having descended and taking up the wooden sword (*sphya*), he says: "Step aside, lest I enclose you; O Brahman, I shall perform the northern enclosure. 6.3.3.26.
To the south of the great altar (*mahāvedi*), the Brahman priest sits down. [cf. 5.1.2.31] 6.3.3.27.
Being impelled, he performs the northern enclosure. [cf. 5.1.2.32]

6.3.3.28. Having leveled [the ground] and having propped [the posts] with the front part [of the yoke], while standing to the east of the hall, he issues the command: “Place the sprinkling waters; set down the fuel and the sacrificial grass.
6.3.3.29. They place the sprinkling waters for him; he sets down the fuel and the sacrificial grass. 6.3.3.30.
He sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass; he sprinkles the altar; he sprinkles what has been placed [on the altar]; he sprinkles the bundle of grass.

6.3.3.31. Pouring out what remains of the *prokṣaṇī* waters, while handing them to the *pratiprasthātṛ*, he says: "Sprinkle the fuel-wood with this. 6.3.3.32. With that [water], he sprinkles the fuel-wood. 6.3.3.33. He takes up this piece of wood from the fuel-pile.
6.3.3.34. He places it to the north of the Āhavanīya fire; this serves as the fuel for the Agniṣomīya animal sacrifice.
Taking this bundle of grass, he goes toward the Uttaravedi, spreading it along the Pṛṣṭhyā line. From here on, they proceed to the two Havirdhāna sheds.

From here on, they turn them around at the two Havirdhāna sheds themselves: the southern one to the south, and the northern one to the north. They do not cross over the *pṛṣṭhyā* cord. 6.3.4.2. They place them in front of the hall so that they are visible; they leave them tied up.
6.3.4.3. He cleanses the forehead-band and fastens it back on; he removes the third roof-covering; they enclose the shed. 6.3.4.4.
When it has been thus prepared, the Adhvaryu enters the hall and takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter.
6.3.4.5. He offers that in the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra: “They harness the mind and they harness the thoughts, svāhā! and with “The praise of the sage is unharmed, svāhā! (RV 1.2.13a).
6.3.4.6. Having taken up the *prokṣaṇī* sprinkling waters, he goes out, saying: “O you two belonging to Viṣṇu, be purified for Viṣṇu,” and, “O you two who hear the gods, announce among the gods.

6.3.4.7. He issues the call: “The *sruva*-ladle and the *sruc*-ladle! and, “Bring the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the clarified butter (*ājya*), and the *upāṃśu* cup; come, O sacrificer! Let them lead the wife here! 6.3.4.8. The *neṣṭṛ* leads the wives. Having brought them out through the southern door, they walk along the south of the *ānvāhāryapacana* fire, carrying their feet [in the prescribed manner].
6.3.4.9. When she has arrived, the *adhvaryu* takes four spoonfuls [of ghee] and offers it with:

6.3.4.10. “*Idaṃ viṣṇur vicakrame (1.2.13e svāhā)*”—having placed a piece of gold on the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart—he pours the residue from the ladle onto the footprint with: “*Tredhā nidadhe padam = pāṃsure svāhā*. 6.3.4.11. With the words, “*Ā no vīro jāyatāṃ karmaṇya (1.2.13d)*,” the wife anoints the axle with her hand extended toward the east over the footprint, saying, “*Yaṃ sa . . . nām asad vaśī*. She anoints silently from the south.
6.3.4.12. Right here he shifts the *sruva*-ladle, the *sruk*-ladle, the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the clarified butter (*ājya*), and the *upāṃśu* cup.
6.3.4.13. The *neṣṭṛ* leads the wife along the opposite path to the *pratiprasthātṛ*. Having caused her to enter by the southern door, he makes her exit by the northern one.
6.3.4.14. When she has arrived, the *pratiprasthātṛ* takes four portions [of clarified butter] and offers them.

6.3.4.15. Having placed a piece of gold on the southern track of the northern *havirdhāna* cart with the mantra, “*Irāvatī dhenumatī hi bhūtaḥ svāhā*,” he pours the remnants of the oblation (*saṃsrāva*) onto the footprint with the mantra, “*Śūyavasinīmayūkhaiḥ svāhā*.

6.3.4.16. With the mantra, “*Ā no vīro jāyatāṃ karmaṇyaḥ*,” the wife anoints the axle with her hand extended forward over the footprint, saying, “*Yaṃ sarve ’vaśī*. She anoints it silently from the north. 6.3.4.17. The wife returns.
6.3.4.18. He says, "Recite for the two *havirdhāna* carts as they are being moved forward.

6.3.4.19. He causes [the Adhvaryu] to recite, "O God, speak auspiciously for our dwellings," provided that he emits a sound; and if he does not, [he causes him to recite], "Speak food; speak vigor. 6.3.4.20. He follows with the consecration formula: "Go forward, fashioning the sacrifice; lead the sacrifice upward; do not falter."
6.3.4.21. Having circumambulated from the east with the verse, “May you two rejoice here on the summit of the earth” (1.2.13g2), they restrain [the chariot] when the axle-nave is in its proper place.

6.3.4.22. With the verse containing a word of blessing, “O Viṣṇu, whether from heaven or from the earth” (1.2.13h), the Adhvaryu drives in the stakes for the southern *havirdhāna* cart with the formula, “O great Viṣṇu, or from the left” (*maho viṣṇav uta vā savyād*). With the verse, “I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu” (1.2.13i), the Pratiprasthātṛ [drives in the stakes] for the northern [cart] with the formula, “He who [measured] the earthly realms... unto his glory” (*yaḥ pārthivāni... rugāya*).

6.3.4.23. With the formula, "Thou art the forehead of Viṣṇu," he touches the front beam (rarāṭīya); with "Thou art the back of Viṣṇu," the middle roof-panel; with "Ye two are the corners of Viṣṇu's loincloth," the two roof-panels on both sides; and with "Thou art the needle of Viṣṇu," [the cord]. 6.3.4.25. The Adhvaryu sews the southern door-posts, and the Pratiprasthātṛ the northern one, with the formula, "Thou art the firm foundation of Viṣṇu."

6.3.4.26. Having sewn [the two carts] at a distance of one cubit (*aratni*), they loosen the knots while making knots as they sew, and they touch the prepared *havirdhāna* (soma-cart) with the formula: "Thou art Vaiṣṇava; for Viṣṇu thee. [? 6.3.4.E.
"Of the god thee... (VS 1.2.13o). ||15||

With the words, “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...,” he takes up the spade (*abhri*) with the formula: “I take thee with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan; thou art a spade, thou art a woman. 6.3.5.2.
With the words, “The *rakṣas* is encircled, the enemies are encircled,” he traces a circle around the pit for the *audumbarī* post with the formula: “Here I cut off the *rakṣas*.”
6.3.5.3. He says, "O *prastotṛ*, come here, dig this!
6.3.5.4. With the words, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ," he takes up the spade (*abhri*), saying, "I take thee of the Aśvins; thou art a spade, thou art a woman. 6.3.5.5.
With the words, "The *rakṣas* is encircled, the enemies are encircled," he draws a line around the place for the *uparava* holes, saying, "Here I cut off the *rakṣas*."

6.3.5.6. Then he traces around them individually with the formula: "I trace around the Rakṣas-slayers, the spell-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu. To the south, he traces around the easternmost one with: "I trace around the Rakṣas-slayers, the spell-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu."

6.3.5.7. With the formula, "I mark around that which is to the west of it, the slayer of demons, the destroyer of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu," he marks around that which is to the north of it with the formula, "I mark around that which is to the north of it, the slayer of demons, the destroyer of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. To the one who is at the northernmost part, he says, "O Unnetṛ! Dig these, without breaking them, making them level at the height of an arm. 6.3.5.8.
With the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ," he takes up the spade, saying, "With the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee; thou art a spade, thou art a woman."

6.3.5.9. With the words, “The *rakṣas* is encircled; the enemies are encircled,” he traces around the pit for the sacrificial post (*yūpāvaṭa*), saying, “Here I cut off the neck of the neck-gripping *rakṣas*.
6.3.5.10. He says, “O *Śubrahmaṇya*, dig this [pit] to the depth of the lower stone (*upara*).

6.3.5.11. Having given the command, “Bring the dug-out pit for the *audumbarī* post, the *audumbarī* post placed therein, the *prokṣaṇī* waters containing barley, the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the clarified butter (*ājya*), and the *upāṃśu* cup; come, O sacrificer!”—he continues.

6.3.5.12. With the formula, “For heaven thee, for the intermediate region thee, for the earth thee,” he sprinkles the Audumbarī post. 6.3.5.13. With the formula, “May the world, the seat of the fathers, be purified,” he pours water into the hole for the Audumbarī post.
6.3.5.14. With the formula, “Thou art barley; bar away from us our enemies,” he scatters barley grains, adding, “Bar away our adversaries.”
6.3.5.15 With the formula, “Thou art the seat of the fathers” (TS 1.3.1.g), he spreads the sacrificial grass with its tips pointing in all directions.

6.3.5.16 With the formula, “Svāhā to the fathers,” having placed a piece of gold underneath, he makes an offering over it with clarified butter. 6.3.5.17 He says, “O Udgātṛ, do what is your duty. The Udgātṛ performs whatever task is his duty regarding the Audumbarī post.

6.3.5.18. With the words, “Prop up the sky (1.3.1h),” he raises it; with the words, “Fill the mid-region, make firm the earth,” [he does so]. 6.3.5.19. With the words, “May Dyutāna Māruta set thee up (1.3.1i),” he sets it up; with the words, “By the steadfast law of Mitra and Varuṇa,” [he does so]. 6.3.5.20.

With the words, “Favoring the Brahman, favoring the Kṣatra (1.3.1k),” he piles it around with the wooden pin; with the words, “I pile thee around, bestowing good offspring and bestowing the increase of wealth,” [he does so].

6.3.5.21. With the words, “Make firm the *brahman*, make firm the *kṣatra*,” he makes it firm with the staff of the consecrated; with the words, “Make firm the progeny, make firm the wealth, make firm the increase of wealth, make firm the kinsmen for the sacrificer.
6.3.5.22. With the words, “Make the earth swell,” he pours out a vessel of water; with the words, “Break the skin-bag. 6.3.5.23. With the words, “For food, thee,” he places gold upon its prongs.
6.3.5.E. “With ghee, O Heaven and Earth...
Reciting, “With ghee, O Heaven and Earth, fill yourselves full” (1.3.1m), he offers an oblation into the Audumbarī post. He pours out the remainder until the very end. [N1,69b3]
6.3.6.2. With the formula, “Thou art for Indra” (cf. 1.3.1n), he places the southern roof-covering with the words, “The shade of all people.
6.3.6.3. They make the northern roof-coverings higher than the southern ones; they make them overlapping. 6.3.6.4.

They extend the *sadas* shed toward the north with the verse, “O lover of songs, may the songs encompass thee” (1.3.1o); he piles it up on both sides with the words, “May these be, may they be increased on every side, the delights.”

6.3.6.5. With the formula, "Thou art Indra’s seam," the Adhvaryu sews the eastern door; with "Thou art Indra’s firm [point]," the Pratiprasthātṛ sews the western one. 6.3.6.6. Having sewn them to the measure of an aratni, they loosen the knots; sewing while forming knots, they proceed. 6.3.6.7.
With the formula, "Thou belongest to Indra; for Indra thee," they both touch the prepared Sadas.
6.3.6.8. He approaches the excavated *uparava* pits. 6.3.6.9. Their materials consist of six pegs and two wooden boards.
6.3.6.10. He issues the call: "The sprinkling waters contain barley; bring the sacrificial grass, the clarified butter, and the vessel for the *upāṃśu* draught; come, O sacrificer!"

6.3.6.11. Taking one of these very stakes, he digs the *uparava* pits—which were already dug—each one with the formula: "I dig you, the Rakṣas-slayers, the pit-fall slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu" (TS 1.3.2a). He first digs the one in the south-eastern corner. 6.3.6.12. With the formula:
"Here I root out that pitfall for you" (TS 1.3.2b), he throws up the earth, saying: "That which a kinsman or a stranger has buried against us."

6.3.6.13. With the words, "I make him lower than this," he presses down with his two thumbs from the south, behind the *uparava* pits, saying: "He who is our equal, or he who is not our equal, who acts as an enemy—he is pressed down by the *gāyatrī* metre; the secret spell (*valaga*) is crushed. 6.3.6.14. With the words, "I dig the Rakṣas-slaying, spell-destroying [pits] belonging to Viṣṇu," he digs that which is further away from that [first pit].
6.3.6.15. With the words, "This I dig up from you, that *valaga*," he scatters sand. With the words, "That which our rival or our non-rival has buried," (ibid.

b2 with variant), and "This I make lower," he presses down with his two thumbs to the south and behind the *uparava* pits, saying, "The *valaga* belonging to him who is our kinsman or who is not our kinsman and acts as an enemy, is pressed down by the *jagatī* metre."
6.3.6.16. With the words, “I dig the slayers of Rakṣases, the slayers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu,” he digs the one furthest to the north.

6.4.1.17. With the words, “Here I dig up that secret spell which my rival has buried against us,” he throws up the loose earth. With the words, “This I make lower than him who is not our rival,” he presses down with his two thumbs from the south and behind the *uparava* holes.
6.3.6.19. “Whatever rival of ours, or whoever who is not our rival, acts with hostility—by means of the *anuṣṭubh* metre, that secret spell (*valaga*) is crushed.

6.3.6.20. Having poured those [substances] together and having transferred them to the south of the altar, and having touched water, the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer both touch the two front portions [of the mound], saying, “May we proceed quickly (*śīvahi*). The Adhvaryu stands to the south and the sacrificer to the north.

6.3.6.21. “O Adhvaryu, what is here?”—thus the sacrificer asks first. “Auspiciousness,” he says. “May that be for us both together,” says the sacrificer. “What is here? the Adhvaryu asks. “Auspiciousness,” he says. “May that be for us both together.”

6.3.6.22. With the words, “May we two attain prosperity,” they both touch the two southern halves. The Adhvaryu asks, “Sacrificer, what is there? He replies, “Auspiciousness. “May that be common to us both. The Sacrificer asks, “Adhvaryu, what is there? He replies, “Auspiciousness. “May that be common to us both. 6.3.6.23. With the words, “May we two attain tranquility,” they both touch the two western halves. The Sacrificer asks, “Adhvaryu, what is there? He replies, “Auspiciousness. “May that be common to us both.”

6.3.6.24. [The Adhvaryu says] "Sacrifice... [and so on]. When the Adhvaryu says "Auspiciousness," he [the Sacrificer] says, "May that be ours together. 6.3.6.25. Saying "Let us rise up," they both touch the two northern [sacrificial posts]. The Adhvaryu asks, "Sacrificer, what is here? He replies, "Auspiciousness. "May that be ours together," he says. The Sacrificer asks, "Adhvaryu, what is here? He replies, "Auspiciousness. "May that be ours together," he says.

6.3.6.26. Then he touches each of these intermediate [stones] one by one: with the formula, “Thou art Virāj, the subduer of the seven,” he touches the one in the eastern part on the south; with “Thou art Śarāj, the slayer of rivals,” the one immediately following it; with “Thou art Śvarāj, the slayer of the malicious,” the one immediately north of that; and with “Thou art Viśvārāj, the slayer of all destructive spirits,” the one furthest to the north of all.
6.3.6.27. With the formula, "I sprinkle you, the slayers of Rakṣases, the destroyers of magical spells, belonging to Viṣṇu," he sprinkles all of them together. ||17||

He sprinkles all of these together. 6.3.7.2. With the formula, “I pour down the Rakṣas-slayers, the spell-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu” (TS 1.3.2.h), he pours water on the easternmost [post] from the south. In the same way for each one.
6.3.7.3. With the words, “You are barley; keep hatred away from us,” he scatters barley grains, saying, “Keep enemies away.

6.3.7.4. In this very same way—repeating for each one—he spreads sacrificial grass with its tips pointing in all directions, saying, “I spread you, the slayers of Rākṣasas, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu.”

6.3.7.5. Upon that very same single [spot], in this manner, upon that very same single [spot], in this manner, upon that very same single [spot], he makes an offering over it with another [substance], having placed a piece of gold in between, while reciting: “I offer the slayers of demons, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu; svāhā! (1.3.2l + svāhā). 6.3.7.6. With the formula, “I set down the two slayers of demons, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu (1.3.2m),” he places the two pressing-boards facing eastward upon these [spots]. He fixes them with two pegs in front, two behind, and two in the middle.
6.3.7.7. With the formula, “The two Rakṣas-slayers, the two Valaga-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu—I sprinkle around with this loose earth” (1.3.2n), he sprinkles around with the loose earth (*purīṣa*).

6.3.7.8. With the formula, “The two Rakṣas-slayers, the two Valaga-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu—I strew around with this sacrificial grass” (1.3.2o), he strews the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) both toward [the altar] and all around it.
6.3.7.9. With the formula, “The two Rakṣas-slayers, the two Valaga-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu” (1.3.2p), he covers [the altar].
6.3.7.10. With the formula, “I spread over [the stone] that which slays the Rākṣasas, destroys the secret spells (valaga), belongs to Viṣṇu,” he spreads the pressing-skin over these two stones.

6.3.7.11. Then, with the formula, “Thou art great, O great pressing-stone,” he causes it to sound by striking it with the staff of the consecrated sacrificer between the two *iṣe* blades, saying, “Speak a great sound for Indra; speak a sound that slays the Rākṣasas, destroys the secret spells, and belongs to Viṣṇu. (1.3.2q with addition)
6.3.7.12. At this time, the Pratiprasthātṛ, having prepared a four-cornered, eastward-facing mound to the east of the support of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, strews it around with sand.
6.3.7.13. He issues the command: "The wooden sword (*sphya*), the water-vessel—bring the loose earth and the sand, O Sacrificer!
6.3.7.14. They bring the loose earth from the *cātvāla*. Wherever they find sand, they take it; then, having dug up the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth and leveled it, he sprinkles it with water.
6.3.7.15. Having leveled the soil, he pours down loose earth and sprinkles it with water. He pours down sand, levels it, and sprinkles it with water. 6.3.7.16.
In this very same manner he prepares the *dhiṣṇya* hearth for the Hotṛ; likewise for the Maitrāvaruṇa, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the Potṛ, the Neṣṭṛ, and the Acchāvāka; and likewise the Mārjālīya hearth.

6.3.7.17. Then he causes them to stand in their respective places one by one: [he addresses] the *dhiṣṇya* of the Āgnīdhra with, “Thou art the pervasive one, O Pravāhaṇa” (1.3.3a), and with, “With thy fierce aspect, O Agni, protect me; fill me; do not harm me” (1.3.3r); [he addresses] the *dhiṣṇya* of the Hotṛ with, “Thou art the bearer, the carrier of oblations” (1.3.3b); [he addresses] that of the Maitrāvaruṇa with, “Thou art the invigorating one, the wise” (1.3.3c); [he addresses] that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with, “Thou art Tutha, the all-knowing” (1.3.3d). [N1,71a1]

[The Adhvaryu addresses the respective priests: to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with, "Thou art the eager one (*uśij*), the sage (*kavi*)" (1.3.3e); to the Potṛ with, "Thou art the swift one (*aṅghāri*), the son of Bamba (*bambhāri*)" (1.3.3f); to the Neṣṭṛ with, "Thou art the seeker of aid (*avasyu*), the worshipful one (*duvasvant*)" (1.3.3g); and to the Mārjālīya fire with, "Thou art the purifier (*śundhyu*), O Mārjālīya" (1.3.3h). With the formula, "With thy fierce aspect (*raudra-anīka*), protect me, O Agni; carry me across; do not harm me" (1.3.3r), he applies the "aspect" (*anīka*) to all of them.
6.4.1 (Cal 6.6.1). They disperse to run [to their respective places]. In the afternoon, having been washed, they assemble.

6.4.1.2. The Pratiprasthātṛ, having gone between the *cātvāla* and the *utkara*, takes the *vasatīvarī* waters with a jar covered by a bunch of grass (*kūrca*), standing against the current of flowing waters at the junction of shadow and sunlight.

[cf. 6.4.2] 6.4.1.3. If they do not flow, he should take them after stirring them up. If there should be no shadow, he should create his own shadow, [saying]: “These waters are rich in oblation; may the sun be rich in oblation” (TS 1.3.12a).

6.4.1.4. Having brought them back in the manner described, he places them behind the *gārhapatya* fire with the formula: "In the seat of Agni, whose house is unassailable, I place you; for the sake of bliss, O blissful ones, bestow bliss upon me. (ŚB 1.3.12.1b)

6.4.1.5. When he has arrived, he issues the directions: "Strew the sacrificial grass! Restrain the vow! Call the *apivrata* [priests]! O *Āgnīdh*, place the clarified butter on the fire! O *Pratiprasthātṛ*, cleanse the offering-spoons and take up the portions of clarified butter! O *Unnetṛ*, pour together the Soma in the *droṇakalaśa* vessel with the *daśāpavitra* filter! Let them bring the wife; let the carts follow behind. 6.4.1.6. They do this: the *Pratiprasthātṛ* cleanses the offering-spoons and takes up the portions of clarified butter, including the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*).

6.4.1.7. Having taken the well-known portions from the *juhū* and *upabhṛt* ladles, he spreads a base layer for the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) with the formula, “Thou art the milk of the great ones” (3.2.6a1), and a second time with, “The body of all the gods,” and [a third time] with, “May I succeed today in taking the draught of the speckled ones” (ibid.
a2). 6.4.1.8. He pours curds into the *sruc* ladle across the strainer with the formula, “Thou art the draught of the speckled ones” (ibid.
a3). 6.4.1.9. He pours clarified butter over it from above with the formula, “Thou art the heart of Viṣṇu; one [portion], food” (ibid. a4, a5).
6.4.1.10. With the words, “May Viṣṇu stride along you,” he makes the second [offering]. 6.4.1.11. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite, “May prosperity increase through curds and ghee” (ibid.

a6). 6.4.1.12. With the words, “Of that which has been offered and consumed, [may there be] invincibility” (ibid. a7–b), at the time for the *dhruvā* ladle, he lifts up the vessels containing the clarified butter.
6.4.1.13. They kindle the sacrificial fuel and prepare the supporting ladles.
6.4.1.14. He leads the wife out after the rice-grains with the formula: "Come up after me. [N1,71a9]

6.4.1.15. The Adhvaryu causes the sacrificer and his wife to stand near the *prajahita* (the discarded fire) with the formula: "In harmony with all the gods worthy of sacrifice, breaking forth with those already born and those yet to be born, place the sacrificer in the world of heaven! Do not abandon this oblation for which we approach you. Seize him as he rises; do not exclude the sharer from his share! Where the worlds of the Seven Seers, the doers of good deeds, are, there place this sacrifice and the sacrificer. Both of you, take hold of him!"
"Exert yourselves together upon the common path; whatever merit has been performed by you and offered into the fire—for the protection of that, O husband and wife, exert yourselves together.
(6.4.1.16) Having returned, they sit down behind the *gārhapatya* fire facing east; either the *brahmán*, the sacrificer, or the king places the *rājā* (Soma) in his lap.
(6.4.1.16) The *adhvaryu* takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter in the *pracaraṇī* ladle.

6.4.1.17. He offers that [libation] while the Vaisarjana formulas are being recited, beginning with: “O Soma, you who ward off those who harm our bodies (1.3.4a)... and ending with: “...you are the wide-extending protector against hatred caused by others;

svāhā! 6.4.1.18. With the formula: “May the swift one, enjoying the clarified butter, partake of it; svāhā! (1.3.4b),” he offers the *aptu* offering with the *sruva* ladle. 6.4.1.19. As he lifts up the fuel-stick (*idhma*), they place the supporting ladles (*upayamanī*) beneath it.
6.4.1.E. "He bestows Soma. ||19||
“Bring hither the Soma-pressing stones, the Vāyavya cups, the Droṇakalaśa, and the Vasatīvarī waters! Recite for Agni and Soma as they are being led forth!”—thus he says.
6.4.2.2. With the verse, “May this Agni create wide space for us” (1.3.4c), they proceed with Agni at their head, [reciting] “May he go before our enemies in the winning of booty.”
6.4.2.3. They go to the *āgnīdhra* hearth. 6.4.2.4. He pours out the supporting ashes; he places the fire down. The *adhvaryu* takes four spoonfuls into the *pracaraṇī* ladle. 6.4.2.5.

He offers that with the verse containing the word "lead," beginning "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth" (RV 1.1.14i), at the *āgnīdhra* altar, ending with "O God, may we worship all [the gods]" (RV 1.1.14j).

6.4.2.6. Right here they set down the *droṇakalaśa* and the *vasatīvarī* waters. 6.4.2.7. They pass by with the King Soma and the clarified butter. Having run past, the *adhvaryu* sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmābarhis*). He sprinkles the altar; he sprinkles what has been placed [thereon]. [cf. 5.1.3.1] 6.4.2.8. Having poured out the water, he takes the *prastara* bundle. He spreads the sacrificial grass. [cf. 5.1.3.2]
6.4.2.9. Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), these very ones made of *kārṣmarya* wood.
(C90) [cf. 5.1.3.3] 6.4.2.10. He places two fuel-sticks (*samidh*) upon the enclosing sticks; having caused [the fire] to spread over them, he fans the fire. 6.4.2.11.
With the words, “O Viṣṇu, stride out widely,” he offers a spoonful (*sruvāhuti*). [He says: “For a wide dwelling... [protect] the lord of the sacrifice, svāhā! (TS 1.3.4d + svāhā).

6.4.2.12. Having stepped forward, he places a stalk of sugarcane crosswise; upon the two crosswise stalks, he places the *prastara* of *aśvavāla* grass; upon the *prastara*, the *juhū* ladle; and upon the *akhara* (the pit), the other [ladles]. 6.4.2.13. Having set them down and touched them together with the formula, "The *dhruvā*s have sat down, which for me, O Agni... (*dhruvā asadan yan ma agne*), he recites the *daśahotṛ* formula. [cf. 5.1.3.6]

6.4.2.14. Having touched water, he causes the King (Soma) to enter toward the southern *havirdhāna* cart with the verse: “Soma goes forth, the knower of the way; he goes to the appointed place of the gods to sit upon the womb of Truth” (1.3.4e).
6.4.2.15. With the formula, “Thou art the seat of Aditi; sit on the seat of Aditi” (1.3.4g), he places the King upon the *kavandha* together with the black antelope skin.
6.4.2.16. He hands him over with the words, “This is your Soma, O God Savitṛ” (1.3.4h), and adds, “Guard him; let him not deceive you.”

6.4.2.17. Having handed [the Soma] over with the words, “O divine Soma, you have approached the gods” (cf. 1.3.4i), he worships it, saying, “Now I, a human, having conquered by the thousand, approach humans with the gift; I turn back with prosperity. 6.4.2.18. He turns back toward the north and makes an añjali gesture, saying, “Homage to the gods” (1.3.4k) and “Svadhā to the ancestors.
6.4.2.19. Bending his right knee, he steps out, saying, “Today I am released from the bonds of Varuṇa” (cf. 1.3.4l1).
6.4.2.20. He gazes upward with the words, “The light is to be looked upon from above. 6.4.2.21. He looks beyond the Āhavanīya fire with the words, “The Vaiśvānara light.
6.4.2.22. With the words, “Thou art the kindling-stick of Agni,” he takes up a fuel-stick.

6.4.2.23. Having performed the purification with the mantra, "O Agni, Lord of Vows" (VS 1.3.4m–o), they place a fuel-stick on the fire with the mantra: "Thou art the Lord of Vows among vows; that body of mine which was in thee, let it be here in me; this body of thine which was in me, let it be there in thee. O Lord of Vows, as our vows were according to their respective places, so let our bodies be according to their respective places—svāhā! (VS 1.3.4m–o).

6.4.2.24. They bring the *vasatīvarī* waters for him. Having placed them on the southern hip of the high altar (*uttaravedi*), while they are uncovered, he releases his fingers as if touching *manas*.

6.4.2.25. With the formula, "Svāhā! I release the sacrifice with the mind; Svāhā! [from] heaven and earth... from the intermediate space; Svāhā! I release the sacrifice upon the sacrifice," he lifts up his fingers. 6.4.2.26. Having carried the *vasatīvarī* waters back along the path by which they came, he sets them down behind the *gārhapatya* fire.
6.4.2.27. In those very same [vessels], the Neṣṭṛ priest dismisses the wife in this very manner.
6.4.2.28. Either before the initiation or once the King Soma has been purchased, they cut down the sacrificial post (yūpa).
6.4.2.E. Having melted the clarified butter over the Gārhapatya fire and purified it, [he proceeds].

Having melted the clarified butter over the *gārhapatya* fire, purified it, and cleansed both the *sruva* and the *sruk* ladles, he goes forward to the east and takes four portions of butter for the *āhavanīya* fire.

6.4.3.2. He offers that with the formula, “O Viṣṇu, stride out widely, svāhā! Having placed a kindling stick on the *āhavanīya*, he offers the oblation for the sacrificial post (*yūpāhuti*) with the formula, “Make wide room for our dwelling; spread the clarified butter, svāhā! [72b]
6.4.3.3. Having taken the *sruva* ladle, the clarified butter, the *upāṃśu* cup, the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), and the axe, he goes out [cf.

5.1.1.4ff.]. 6.4.3.4. He pays reverence to that half of the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) which he has chosen, saying: "I have passed beyond others, not others—for the sacrifice to the gods" (TS 1.3.5.1a). 6.4.3.5.
Saying, "May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey" (TS 1.3.5d), he anoints it with clarified butter after interposing a piece of gold [see scholium no. 5, p. 4f.; cf. 5.1.1.6].
6.4.3.6. With the words, "O herb, protect him," he encloses it with sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
6.4.3.7. With the words, "O axe, do not harm him," he strikes it with the axe.
6.4.3.8. He ties up and sets aside the first splinter that falls away.
6.4.3.9. He cuts [the branch] so that it does not get caught on the axle. He causes it to be carried forward, either eastward or northward.

6.4.3.10. He consecrates it with the mantra: “Do not scratch the sky with your top; do not harm the intermediate space with your middle; be united with the earth” (cf. no. 6). 6.4.3.11. Having cast gold [into the fire], he offers an oblation upon the stump with the mantra: “O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred branches, svāhā! (cf. no. 7).
6.4.3.12. With the mantra, "May we rise up with a thousand branches" (TS 1.3.5h2), he touches himself. 6.4.3.13.
Having touched water, he sharpens the axe along the grain with the mantra, "As this axe whets itself upon thee... and continues, "...he has led it forward for great good fortune. 6.4.3.14.
With the mantra, "Unbroken is the wealth of heroic sons" (TS 1.3.5i), he trims the yoke-pin; in the same manner, he trims the yoke-pin of the northern shoulder.
6.4.3.15. He brings these three [objects], each four finger-breadths wide.

6.4.3.16. They fashion the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) so that it has eight corners. Once the post has been fashioned with eight corners, the *caṣāla* (top-ring) has been prepared, and it has been washed and placed to the east of the sacrificial pit (*yūpāvaṭa*).

[cf. 5.1.3.10] 6.4.3.17. Walking around it together with two splinters (*śakala*), he issues the command: "Bring the sprinkling waters containing barley, the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the clarified butter (*ājya*), and the vessel for the *upāṃśu* libation; come, O sacrificer! [5.1.3.11]

6.4.3.18. He sprinkles the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) with the formula, “For the earth thee! For the intermediate space thee! For the sky thee! (cf. 1.3.1), and [he adds], “May the world, the seat of the fathers, be purified. 6.4.3.19.

He pours water into the hole for the sacrificial post with the formula, “Thou art barley; keep away from us our enemies” (1.3.1). 6.4.3.20. He scatters barley grains [into the hole] with the formula, “Keep away the hostile ones” (1.3.1).

6.4.3.21. With the formula, “Thou art the seat of the fathers” (VS 1.3.1 + *pitṛbhyaḥ svāhā*), he spreads out sacrificial grass (*barhis*) with its tips pointing in all directions, saying, “To the fathers, svāhā! 6.4.3.22. Having placed gold underneath, he makes an offering of clarified butter while reciting, “Thou art easy of access, the first-goer” (VS 1.3.6e). Then, having said, “The tree of the fathers shall stand upon thee; may they know him,” he places a chip of the sacrificial post (*yūpaśakala*) face upwards. 6.4.3.23. He says, “Recite for the sacrificial post as it is being anointed! (cf. ZB 3.7.1.10; ApŚS 7.10.1; MānŚS 1.2.2.12).

6.4.3.24. Moving around the top of the sacrificial post, he says, "May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey" (cf. 1.3.5d; 1.3.6f), and having pulled off the *caṣāla* (the wooden ring) and placed it between himself and the post, he anoints the top.
[No. 42] 6.4.3.25. Having anointed the *caṣāla* in the same manner, he fixes it on with the formula, "For the plants that bear good fruit" (1.3.6g).
6.4.3.26. In the same manner, he anoints the edge facing the fire (*agniṣṭhā-aśri*).
6.4.3.27. He touches it three times at the height of the navel.
6.4.3.28. He anoints it to the very end.
6.4.3.29. “Recite for the one being raised up!”—thus he says.
6.4.3.30. With the words, “Support the sky upward (RV 1.3.6h),” he raises [the post], and with the words, “Fill the intermediate space; make firm the earth with what is below. [No. 43] 6.4.3.31.

With the words, “Tread upon those who attack (RV 2.4.2.9),” he places [the base-ring] down, saying, “Let the enemies be beneath; stand like Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, conquering the waters and the fields. 6.4.3.32.

With two verses addressed to Viṣṇu, beginning with “We desire to go to those abodes of yours (RV 1.3.6i, k),” he prepares [the site], saying, “Where the many-horned cows are, there is the unwearied friend. [N1, 73a4]

6.4.3.33. When they join the corner facing the fire (agniṣṭhā-aśri) with the Āhavanīya fire, he then causes the top-ring (caṣāla) to be raised up with the verse, “That highest step of Viṣṇu” (1.3.6l), so that they see it as far as the phrase “stretched out” (rātatam).

6.4.3.34. With the formula, “Thee, the winner of the Brahman, the winner of the Kṣatra” (1.3.6m), he covers it around with loose earth (purīṣa), saying, “I cover thee, the winner of good offspring, the winner of the increase of wealth.”

6.4.3.35. “*Brahma dṛṃha kṣatram dṛṃha*” (VS 1.3.6)—with these words, he makes it firm with the consecrated’s staff (*dīkṣitadaṇḍa*). 6.4.3.36. “*Prajān dṛṃha rayim dṛṃha rāyas poṣam dṛṃha sajātān yajamānāya dṛṃha*”—with these words, he pours out the water-vessel. 6.4.3.37. “*Unnambhaya pṛthivīm bhinddhīdaṃ divyadṛtim*”—he pours out the vessel of water.
One should not release the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) before the encircling-rope (*parivyayaṇa*).
6.4.3.38. He says, "Recite for the one being girt about.
6.4.3.39. With the formula, "Thou art girt about" (ŚB 1.3.6.o), he girds it at the height of the navel with the formula, "The divine subjects and the human subjects [gird thee].
6.4.3.40. Having girt it three times, he causes the end to enter within.
6.4.3.41. He weaves the *aṇiman* and the *sthavimat* [strands].

6.4.3.42. With the formula, “Thou art the ridge of heaven” (ApŚS 7.11.19; ZB 3.7.1.22; VaitS 6.6; KātyŚS 6.3.17), he takes up the *svaru*. 6.4.3.43. With the formula, “I hide thee on the ridge of the intermediate space” (TS 1.3.6p), he hides it within the middle enclosing-stalk (*parivyaya*).
6.4.3.44. He releases the sacrificial post (yūpa) at its very end.
6.4.3.45. With the formula, “For food, thee” (TS 1.3.7a), he takes two blades of sacrificial grass (barhis).

6.4.3.46. With the formulas, “Born from Prajāpati, svāhā” and “The offspring born, may they grant permission, svāhā; this animal, the oblation, svāhā” (TS 3.1.4a, b—both with *svāhā*), he offers the introductory oblations (*upākaraṇīya*).

6.4.3.47. With the formula, “Thou art the sacrificial cord” (1.3.7b–g), he dedicates the animal facing westward from the east, with the formula, “Come hither, O gods; I dedicate thee, acceptable to Agni and Soma” (the final mantra, cf. ŚāṅkhŚS p. 70). 6.4.3.48.
Having placed two known blades of *barhis* grass aside, he takes a wooden chip with the formula, “Thou art the birthplace of Agni” (1.3.7h).

6.4.3.49. With the formula, “Ye two are the testicles” (ibid. i), he takes the lower fire-drill (*adharāraṇi*), and with the formula, “Thou art the male... the sound” (ibid. k), he takes the upper fire-drill (*uttarāraṇi*).

6.4.3.50. He anoints with the formula, “Anointed with ghee,” and he places [the kindling wood] with the formula, “O you two, bestow virility. 6.4.3.51. With the formulas, “Be born after the Gāyatrī metre,” “Be born after the Triṣṭubh metre,” and “Be born after the Jagatī metre,” he turns himself toward [the fire]. 6.4.3.52.
He says, “Recite for the fire being churned!”
6.4.3.53. They churn the fire. 6.4.3.54. He says: "Recite for the one born; recite for the one being hurled. 6.4.3.55.
He hurls [the fire] with the words: "Be of one mind with us," and "With a peaceful dwelling, today for us."
6.4.3.56. Having offered [the grass-bundle] with the formula, "Fire moves, having entered into fire, svāhā," he makes an additional offering with the formula, "The portion of the Ṛṣis, svāhā.

6.4.3.57. Having touched water, he takes up the cord with his hand turned upward, using the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...; I take thee with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan. [Note: The mantra in 1.3.8a is simply "I take thee" (ādade); is this a simplified form of the mantra?]

6.4.3.58. With the formula, “I seize thee, the oblation for the gods, with the noose of Ṛta” (TS 1.3.8b), he passes the cord diagonally around the horn of the animal. Why are there two instances of *tvā*? 6.4.3.59. With the formula, “Be bold against men” (TS 1.3.8c), he binds [the animal].

6.4.3.60. They bring for him the sprinkling waters in a vessel or a wooden cup. He sprinkles [the animal] with the formula, “From the waters, from the plants, I sprinkle thee” (TS 1.3.8e), and [he adds], “Acceptable to Agni and Soma” (TS 1.3.8d).
6.4.3.61. With the words, “Thou art the drinker of waters” (VS 1.3.8e,f), he causes [the animal] to drink, saying, “Even though licked by a dog, may it find pleasure in this.

6.4.3.62. If it should not drink, or if it should die, one should whisper into its right ear: “Thou art not slain; living, thou goest by the paths leading to heaven. Mayst thou pierce through with those already born and those yet to be born; place the sacrificer in the world of heaven. Do not abandon this oblation which we approach. Thus, it invariably drinks. 6.4.3.63. Having sprinkled the chest, he sprinkles the back.
6.4.3.64. Having caused [the Soma] to be drunk, having sprinkled [it], and having set down the vessel, he recites the invitatory verse for Agni as he is being kindled.

6.4.3.65. [He recites] seventeen [verses] beginning with "Sāvitrī... ending with "svāhā. 6.4.3.66. When the *sāmidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* spoon, he says: "O Āgnīdh, cleanse the fires three times each!"

6.4.3.67. Having stepped across without letting the two *sruks* touch each other, he anoints the animal with the *juhū* while reciting: “May your breath go with the wind; may your limbs unite with those worthy of sacrifice, and may the lord of the sacrifice unite with his blessing. 6.4.3.68. Having anointed the *dhruvā*, he sets it down in its place. Having set down the two *sruks* and the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) in their respective places, standing to the north, he chooses the *pravara*.
6.4.3.69. He causes the announcement to be made. He says: “O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce! (*o śrāvaya*).

6.4.3.70. “Agni, the divine Hotṛ, has sacrificed to the gods, he who is wise and observant; like Manu, he has brought [the sacrifice] to its place. O Brahman, speak and let him carry [the offering]... (6) ...“He is the one who brings this and that”—thus he chooses the Hotṛ.

6.4.3.71. “What is your name?”—thus he asks him. He announces his name, saying, “So-and-so, the human. 6.4.3.72. He throws a wood-shaving into the Āhavanīya fire so that the Hotṛ’s name is established.
6.4.3.73. He says, "O, cause [the Agnīdh] to announce! [The Agnīdh] says, "O, announce! 6.4.3.74.

"[Agni is indeed the leader of the divine clans, and the sacrificer is the leader of human beings. May their household-fire shine brightly for a hundred winters, O Vāyu! May you two, though not mingling your bodies, mingle your gifts. 6.4.3.75. At this time, he hands the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa.

6.4.4 (Cal 6.7.2) [N1,74a2; M190; C90] [cf. 5.2.2.1–19] 6.4.4.1. At this time, he hands the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa. [cf. 5.2.2.1] 6.4.4.2.
