6.4.4.3. The Hotṛ sits down. 6.4.4.4. Being impelled, he takes up the two offering-spoons.
6.4.4.5. He performs the *prayāja* offerings; he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ," "Prompt for the *samidh*s," and "Prompt, prompt!"—thus he performs the eleven *prayāja* offerings.
6.4.4.6. Having brought half [of the butter] in the fourth [turning], they bring all [of it] in the eighth.
6.4.4.7. Having left the eleventh portion remaining in the *upabhṛt* ladle, he makes the offering in the *sruc* and then steps across.

6.4.4.8. With the words, “O Axe, [enter] the hand,” he joins the *svaru* and the axe crosswise; with the words, “...they have been anointed,” he anoints the *svaru* on the inside of the *sruc* and the axe on the outside.

6.4.4.9. With the words, “Protect the cattle,” he rubs the forehead of the animal with the sacrificial knife (*svadhiti*). He says, “May this lack of fortune be wiped away from you. 6.4.4.10. Handing the sacrificial knife to the slaughterer, he touches the animal while holding the *svaru* chip; then, having placed the two offering-ladles (*sruk*) in their proper places, he says, “Recite for the fire carried around.”

6.4.4.11. Having taken a firebrand from the Āhavanīya fire and having gone out between the Cātvāla pit and the Utkara mound, he performs the circumambulation three times by leaping, [reciting] "The wise receive him" (*prajānantaḥ pratigṛhṇanti*)—[with *svāhā* added to each mantra]. While carrying the firebrand in his hand, he runs around; he offers the five *apāvya* formulas: "To breath from the limbs, from the bodies, *svāhā*; to those over whom [he] has power, *svāhā*; to those who are in agreement with what is being bound, *svāhā*; to... [ye... *svāhā*.
"O forest-dwellers, being in agreement, svāhā! Releasing yourselves, O paths, svāhā!"—thus he says. (Sch No. 64) [N1, 74a9] 6.4.4.12.
Having said "O sacrificer," while the sacrificer has taken hold of him from behind, he offers the sixth oblation for the Hotṛ.
6.4.4.13. Having set down the firebrand, the Āgnīdhra runs back three times along the opposite path. (No. 65)

6.4.4.14. The Āgnīdhra takes up that very firebrand (*ulmuka*); the Adhvaryu takes two blades of sacrificial grass (*barhis*); and the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the two omentum-spits (*vapāśrapaṇī*). They proceed toward the north, with the firebrand leading. 6.4.4.15. Between the *cātvāla* pit and the rubbish heap (*utkara*), having called for the formal announcement (*āśrāvya*) and given the direction (*upapreṣya*), he says: "O Hotṛ, [announce] the oblations to the gods. 6.4.4.16.

With the formula, "O wealthy ones, enter the lord of the sacrifice with what is dear to him" (TS 1.3.8i=k), they touch the animal along with the two omentum-spits; and with the formula, "O wide atmosphere, place the lord of the sacrifice within."

6.4.4.17. With the mantra, “Protect him from contact with the earth” (TS 1.3.8.l), they strew sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and place the animal upon it, with its head toward the west and its feet toward the north, making it free from groaning.
6.4.4.18. He says, “Quiet it,” and [the slaughterer] reports, “It has been quieted.”

6.4.4.19. Therefore, [the text says], "The breath of the sacrificer is not different from the animal" (TS 3.1.4h). Thus, both the *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer turn away [from the animal], [reciting]: "May the sacrifice, going to the gods along the path of the gods, reach the abode of the living gods; may the desires of the sacrificer come true. 6.4.4.20.
Having returned, they look at the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*), [saying]: "May offspring [be here]" (TS 5.2.2.19). 6.4.5 (Caland 6.7.3) [N1,74b3; M190; C91] [cf. 5.2.3.1–20]
6.4.5.1. “In this world, may the subjects [prosper] with milk and ghee”—thus [he says]. [Cf. BŚS 3.7.4j, partially agreeing. 6.4.5.2.
Restraining their speech and not looking around, they sit. 6.4.5.3.

With the words, “When the animal has uttered a cry,” he offers a spoonful-oblation once the animal has been immolated, saying: “If the chest or the feet have been struck, may Agni release me from that sin, from all distress—svāhā!”
6.4.5.4. With the words, “O immolators, come hither,” they approach the animal with the two omentum-spits, saying, “The sacrifice has encompassed the lord of the sacrifice for the gods” (ibid.

k). 6.4.5.5. The nooses have been fastened around the necks; he loosens them with the *viśālā* verse, “May Aditi loosen this noose” (ibid. l), saying, “Homage to the animals, homage do I pay to the Lord of Animals; may the noose fall upon the enemy. 6.4.5.6. He fastens them upon a dry stump. The sacrificer meditates upon whomsoever he hates.
6.4.5.7. Having sprinkled water around [the fire], they return without looking back.
6.4.5.8. The Neṣṭṛ brings the wife together with the water for washing the feet (pānnejana) between the *cātvāla* pit and the rubbish heap (*utkara*).
6.4.5.9. With the words, "Homage to you, O Ātāna," he causes her to look up at the sun.
6.4.5.10. With the words, “Go forward, unhindered” (1.3.8n), he leads it toward the north with the words, “With the abundance of ghee and wealth.

6.4.5.11. Having arrived, he causes the vital breaths of the animal to swell by sprinkling them with water: with the formula, “May your speech swell” (1.3.9a), he swells the speech; with “May your breath swell,” the breath; with “May your eye swell,” the eye; and with “May your ear swell,” the ear.

6.4.5.11. With the words, “That pain which has gone to your vital breaths” (ibid. b1), he pours [the water] on the necks; he does not have [the sacrificer] recite here [the verse], “That [pain] which [has gone to] the eye...

may it be purified” (ibid. b2). 6.4.5.12. With the words, “May your navel swell” (1.3.9c1), [he pours it] on the navel; with “May your anus swell” (ibid. c2), on the anus; and with “May your penis swell,” on the penis.
6.4.5.13. Having placed the two words “*śuddhāś caritrāḥ*” (1.3.9d), he sprinkles [the water]. With the words “*śam adbhyaḥ śam oṣadhibhyaḥ*” (1.3.9e), [he says] “*śaṃ pṛthivyai śam ahobhyām*.

6.4.5.14. [The Adhvaryu] ... [reciting] “*āpo devīḥ śuddhāyuvaḥ*” (1.3.8o), he consecrates the poured-out waters with the mantra: “*śuddhā yūyaṃ ... bhūyāsma*” (1.3.8o). [cf. p. 109] 6.4.5.15. The wife returns, and [the Adhvaryu] says: “Make her like an animal tied up facing upward (*uttāna-paśu*).”
6.4.5.16. With the formula, "O herb, protect him," he covers the skin over the navel with the *barhis* grass on the right side.
6.4.5.17. With the formula, "O axe, do not harm him," he cuts across [the skin] with the axe.
6.4.5.18. Having cut off a thick portion of the *barhis*, he anoints both sides of the animal with it.
6.4.5.19. Having stepped out, he discards [the grass-blade] with the formula: "Thou art the portion of the Rakṣases; this I lead away... (TS 1.3.9.i,k). 6.4.5.20.
Having touched water, he extracts the omentum with the formula: "For strength, thee" (TS 1.3.9.l). [With the formula:
"With ghee, Heaven and Earth... (TS 1.3.9.m).
With the mantra, “O Heaven and Earth, cover yourselves with clarified butter” (1.3.9.2m), he covers the two omentum-spits. 6.4.6.2. He cuts [the omentum] without making it wide.
6.4.6.3. With the words, “Uninterrupted be the wealth with excellent heroes,” he trims [the hair].
6.4.6.4. With the words, “Be pure for the gods; be beautiful for the gods,” he pushes back the trimming with sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
6.4.6.5. Having sprinkled [him] with water from a vessel, he heats him over a firebrand with the words, “The demon is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away.”

6.4.6.6. Having drawn out the embers from the *śāmitra* fire with the formula, “Follow the wide mid-air” (TS 1.3.9.o), they return again, led by the firebrand (*ulmuka*), between the *cātvāla* pit and the rubbish heap (*utkara*).

6.4.6.7. They again take hold of the two omentum-spits (*vapāśrapaṇī*) with the formula, “Towards thee, O Agni, day by day” (TS 1.5.6.f–i). With these three *gāyatrī* verses, they approach the *āhavanīya* fire with the formula, “O thou who dwellest in the evening, for our well-being” (TS 1.5.6.2–3, f–i).
6.4.6.8. With the formula, “The demon is burnt away; the enemies are burnt away,” he heats [the omentum] on the outermost ember of the *āhavanīya* fire.
6.4.6.9. Having carried that [omentum] between the sacrificial post and the Āhavanīya fire, the Pratiprasthātṛ, having turned toward the north from the south, roasts the omentum.

6.4.6.10. For it, the Adhvaryu throws a blade of grass outside [the fire] with the formula, “O Vāyu, partake of the drops! He makes an offering upon it with a spoonful using the verse, “Thee indeed they have established as the bearer of oblations,” and with the formula, “O maker of the cooked, enjoy [it], svāhā! [cf. Śrautasūtra p. 114]
6.4.6.11. “Recite for the drops,” he says. When the Maitrāvaruṇa has recited this hymn of six verses, the Adhvaryu, taking up the call for the *svāhākṛti* offerings, steps across.

6.4.6.12. “O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to hear! he says. He gives the command for the *svāhākṛti* offerings. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 6.4.6.13. Having sprinkled the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) over it, he sprinkles the omentum (*vapā*).
6.4.6.14. He spreads clarified butter and a chip of gold beneath the omentum.

6.4.6.15. "Recite for the fat of the omentum of the goat being cut off for Agni and Soma," he says. With the *sruva* ladle... (as above, 6)... "Give the call! he says. "Prompt the offering of the fat of the omentum of the goat set forth for Agni and Soma, svāhā to the gods! [cf. 5.2.4.15–18]

6.4.6.19. Before the omentum, the Pratiprasthātṛ offers a spoonful with the formula: “O Jātavedas, go to the gods with the omentum, svāhā! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, the Adhvaryu [offers] with: “For you are the Hotṛ of the gods, svāhā! 6.4.6.20. With the formula:
“To the gods, svāhā,” he makes a subsequent offering with the spoon, saying: “Svāhā! Go to the Maruts of the upward sky! (cf. ŚB 1.3.10.2q).

6.4.6.21. He throws away the two omentum-spits in opposite directions: the wide one toward the east and the narrow one toward the west. He makes an offering over the omentum with the drippings from them.
6.4.6.22. Having proceeded with the offering of the omentum, they purify themselves at the *cātvāla* pit with the three verses beginning, "O Waters, you are indeed sources of bliss.
6.5.1.1. "O Agnīdh, pour out the sacrificial cake for the animal sacrifice.
[cf. 5.3.1.1] 6.5.1.2. He issues the command: "O Brahman, guard the speckled butter; O Pratiprasthātṛ, prepare the animal victim. 6.5.1.3. They perform this.

6.5.1.4. “O Agnīdh, pour out the sacrificial cake for the animal sacrifice (paśupuroḍāśa). Having said this, he places the two arms with the hands joined together, the left arm being extended across the left hip. 6.5.1.5. Having placed the left arm on one side, moving it singly, he sets down the right hip, the udder-like portion (adhyūdhnī), the omentum (piṣṇalī), and the large intestine (vaniṣṭhu). He says, “Place that; set the heart as the last among the parts that have been moved. This is the procedure for the portions already set forth (prasthitakarma). [Cf. 5.3.1.2–4]

6.5.1.6. Having performed the sprinkling, the Adhvaryu points out the fire-hearths that have not yet been strewn, standing to the north of the two *havirdhāna* carts and to the south of the *āgnīdhra*. He addresses the *āhavanīya* fire with: "Thou art the peaceful ruler, Kṛśānu"; the *āstāva* with: "Thou art the one to be praised, O Pavamāna"; the *cātvāla* pit with: "Thou art the swift one, possessed of clouds"; the animal-cooking hearth (*paśuśrapaṇa*) with: "Thou art the unpolished one, the preparer of oblations"; the *audumbarī* post with: "Thou art the abode of the seasons, the light of heaven"; and [the *brahmāsana*] with: "Thou art the light of Brahman."

"May we prosper in heaven"—at this point he addresses the Brahman's fire; "The unborn one-footed one is yours"—the Gārhapatya fire; "You are the serpent of the deep"—the Gārhapatya fire; "The abandoned one, you are the unborn one by name of the unborn"—the Anvāhāryapacana fire; "You are the robber Sagara"—wherever he stands and responds; "You are the sage of the fathers"—wherever he performs the Hāryojanī offerings; "You are the ocean, the upholder of laws"—wherever he performs the rite with the churning fire.
6.5.1.7. The *agnīdh* removes the animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*), having spread a base of clarified butter beneath it and poured butter over it.

[cf. 5.3.1.5] 6.5.1.8. While spreading the base of butter for two portions of it, he says: “O Pratiprasthātṛ, recite for the cake being cut off for Agni and Soma. [cf. 5.3.1.6] 6.5.1.9. He cuts off portions from both the rear and the front of the cake, and pours butter over them. [cf. 5.3.1.7]

6.5.1.10. He anoints [the spoon]. He takes a single portion from the northern half into the *upabhṛt* [ladle]. He pours clarified butter over it twice. He does not anoint it again. 6.5.1.11. Having joined [the two ladles], the Adhvaryu places them on the fire. He says, "O, cause [the Agnīdhra] to announce! and issues the command: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the *puroḍāśa* set forth for Agni and Soma. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. 6.5.1.12.
He says, "Recite the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) for Agni. 6.5.1.13.
While bringing together the portion for the *sviṣṭakṛt* of the *puroḍāśa*, he says, "O, cause [the Agnīdhra] to announce! and "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Agni!"
6.5.1.14. He makes the offering when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.
6.5.1.15. Having stepped across and placed the two ladles in their respective places, and having divided the portions and sprinkled them with clarified butter, he places the *iḍā* for the Hotṛ.
6.5.1.16. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places it for the Āgnīdhra.
6.5.1.17. They consume [the sacrificial food] and perform the ritual purification (mārjana).
6.5.1.18. Together with the vessel, he carries the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) around to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, along with water, for the Brahman priest.
6.5.1.19. The Brahman priest consumes it and performs the ritual purification.
6.5.1.20. He issues the command: "O Āgnīdh, come with the northern sacrificial grass," and "O Pratiprasthātṛ, perform the dialogue regarding the animal victim.
6.5.1.21. They do this.
6.5.1.22. "O Āgnīdh, having brought a branch of the *plakṣa* tree, place the leaf-buds upon it."

6.5.1.23. With the formula, "For the protection of the gods," the Pratiprasthātṛ draws out some of the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) with the dipping-spoon (sruva), saying, "The most brilliant of the brilliant.

6.5.1.24. Stepping aside and approaching with the offering-ladle (sruk), he asks, "Is the oblation cooked, O Śamitṛ? "It is cooked," he replies. [With the formula], "May Pūṣan protect me from the path of the gods," 6.5.1.25. Stepping aside once more, he asks, "Is the oblation cooked, O Śamitṛ? "It is cooked," he replies. [With the formula], "May Pūṣan protect me as the guardian of the cattle of the gods."
6.5.1.26. Having stepped aside, he asks, "O slaughterer, is the oblation cooked? "It is cooked," he replies. "May Pūṣan, the overlord, protect that for the gods. 6.5.1.27.
Before the pouring of the clarified butter, he touches the heart with the heart-spit.
6.5.1.28. He sets it down in its known place.

6.5.1.29. With the formula, "May your mind be united with my mind," he makes the heart the uppermost part and bastes it with speckled butter (pṛṣadājya), saying, "May the breath be united with the breath; may this oblation, pleasing to the gods and rich in ghee, be offered—svāhā! 6.5.1.30.
Having carried it between the sacrificial post (yūpa) and the Āhavanīya fire, he places it to the south.
6.5.1.31. While spreading [the butter] upon its four [parts], he says to the Pratiprasthātṛ, "Recite for the Manotā as the oblation is being cut off."

6.5.1.32. From the *juhū* and the *upabhṛt*, and from the *vasāhomīyā* vessel and the *iḍā* vessel, he cuts two portions of the heart into the *juhū*. He cuts two portions of the tongue; twice from the tongue, twice from the breast, twice from the flank, and twice from each of the kidneys. 6.5.1.33. Having separated the three parts, he divides the rectum into three. Having cut the middle section into two, he places it into the *juhū*.
6.5.1.34. He sets aside the largest portion for the *apaya* offerings.

6.5.1.35. He cuts portions twice from the *sviṣṭakṛt* portion with his left foreleg; he cuts twice from each of the two sides; and he cuts twice from the right hip, [then] from the *adhyūdhnī*, which is the last [portion]. He sprinkles it with broth. 6.5.1.36. Having placed the broth underneath, he covers it with fat; he pours clarified butter over it; and he anoints it back [with the fat]. 6.5.1.37.
From the animal, he cuts a large piece of flesh from the right foreleg.
6.5.1.38. He places that in the *upabhṛt* [ladle]. He places the small portion of the rectum in the *upabhṛt* itself. 6.5.1.39. He cuts off a large piece of flesh from the left buttock.
6.5.1.40. He places that in the *upabhṛt* itself and sprinkles it with broth.
6.5.1.41. Having placed it in the broth, he covers it with fat. He pours clarified butter over it twice; he does not baste it back. 6.5.1.42.
Having let the animal's fat-offering drip away, he pours clarified butter over it.
6.5.1.43. He throws the boneless parts into the *iḍā*-vessel and sprinkles them with broth.

6.5.1.44. With the formula, “The breath belongs to Indra” (ŚB 1.3.10.c,d), he touches the portion of the animal that has been cut off, saying, “May they rejoice in every limb. 6.5.1.45. With the formula, “Thou art glory” (ibid. f,g,h), he stirs the fat-oblation with the rib-bone, saying, “May Agni cause it to rise. 6.5.1.46. He stirs it three times with the formula, “Driving away hatred. While stirring, he meditates upon whatever the sacrificer hates, thinking, “Driving away hatred.”
6.5.1.44. He places them for the Pratiprasthātṛ. 6.5.1.E. He recites the Pañcahotṛ formula over the two *sruva*-ladles [cf. 5.3.1.11–45]. 6.5.2 (Cal 6.8.2) [N1,76b10; M192; T1,228; C91] [cf. 5.3.2]

6.5.2.1. He recites the *pañcahotṛ* formula over the two *sruva*-ladles. He passes them back [to the Āgnīdhra] (cf. 5.3.2.1). 6.5.2.2. Having placed the scrapings for the wife in a vessel, he causes her to hold it.
6.5.2.3. He says: "Recite the invitatory verse for the oblation of the goat for Agni and Soma" (cf. 5.3.2.2).
6.5.2.4. As the Adhvaryu rises, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes up the *vasā-homa* (the fat-offering).
[cf. ibid. 3] 6.5.2.5. He says, "O, cause to hear!"—he gives the command: "Prompt the offering of the goat's oblation for Agni and Soma. [cf. ibid. 4] 6.5.2.6.

At the half-verse, "Drink the ghee, O drinkers of ghee," the Pratiprasthātṛ offers the *vasā-homa*. With the formula, "The fat, the fat... svāhā to thee for the intermediate space," he leaves a remnant for the *dhṛk*-verses.
6.5.2.7. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, the Adhvaryu offers the oblation.
6.5.2.8. He says, "Recite for Vanaspati," while dipping the *pṛṣadājya* with the *sruva* spoon.
6.5.2.9. Having poured that into the *juhū* ladle, he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! and "Prompt for Vanaspati! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.

6.5.2.10. "Recite for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt," he says, while bringing together the Sviṣṭakṛt portion of the oblation. He says, "O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce! He issues the command, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. 6.5.2.11. Following the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he makes offerings to the quarters with: "To the quarter, svāhā! To the intermediate quarter, svāhā! To the sub-quarter, svāhā! To the further quarter, svāhā! To the upward quarter, svāhā! May the quarters be filled with ghee, svāhā! Homage to the quarters, homage to the quarters! [cf. 5.3.2.12] 6.5.2.12. Following the quarters, he offers the oblation of the Pañcahotṛ.

6.5.2.13. Having stepped across and set down the two *sruva*-ladles in their proper places, having sprinkled them with clarified butter, and having gone back westward, he offers the *iḍā* to the *hotṛ*. [He says: "Be exhilarated, O god; the *iḍā* has been invoked. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he gives it to the *maitrāvaruṇa*, the *agnīdh*, and the *brahman*. He pushes the breast [of the sacrificial cake] toward the *brahman*. [cf. 6.8.2.5] 6.5.2.14. They consume [the portions]. He performs the ritual purification (*mārjana*).

6.5.2.15. “O Āgnīdhra, bring the embers for the supplementary offerings (aupayaja)!”—saying this, he goes forth [with the command]: “O Upayaṣṭṛ, sit down; O Brahman, we shall set out; having placed the fuel-stick, O Āgnīdhra, cleanse the fire once, once! 6.5.2.16.

Having brought the embers for the supplementary offerings from the Āgnīdhra hearth, the Āgnīdhra pours them down upon the Hotṛ’s Dhiṣṇiya altar. The Upayaṣṭṛ sits down with the rectum (guda). 6.5.2.17.
He performs the after-offerings (anūyāja) with the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya), making the Upabhṛt itself the Upabhṛt [vessel], and the Juhū is that in which the speckled butter is contained.

6.5.2.18. He says, "O Śrāvaya," and "Prompt for the gods. He performs these after-offerings (*anūyāja*) with the formula, "Prompt! Prompt! 6.5.2.19. When he says, "O Maitrāvaruṇa, recite the offering prayer," then the *upayaj* priest performs the secondary offerings (*upayaj*). He cuts off a portion of the rectum (*guda*) without piercing it and without turning it over, saying: "Go to the ocean, svāhā! (TS 1.3.11a1).

6.5.2.20. With the words, “Go to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! (1.3.11.1a, end), he finally offers the entire rectum; with the words, “For the waters thee, for the plants! (1.3.11.1b). 6.5.2.21. He wipes his hands on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) while reciting over the vital breaths: “Bestow mind upon my heart” (1.3.11c). 6.5.2.22. The *upayaṣṭṛ* makes the sacrificer recite: “May I attain my body, my skin, my son, and my grandson” (1.3.11d).

6.5.2.23. Having performed the *anūyāja* offerings and having stepped around [the fire], he anoints the *svaru* with the formula: “The controller for the controller. 6.5.2.24. With the formula, “May there be support here,” he places it in the ladle with the words, “May there be separation here; may there be self-support here. 6.5.2.25. With the formula, “May your smoke go to heaven,” he offers it, saying: “May your flame go to the intermediate space; fill the earth with ashes, *svāhā*!”
6.7.2.26. Here, they throw the sacrificial post (yūpa) into the fire, if they intend to throw it in.

6.7.2.27. Having returned, he separates the two offering-ladles (srucau) with the two *vājavatī* verses. 6.7.2.28. Having gone outside, they perform the *saṃyāja* offerings for the wives with the *viṣkalā*. He sacrifices to Soma with clarified butter (*ājya*), to Tvaṣṭṛ with clarified butter, and to Rākā with clarified butter.
6.5.2.29. "Recite for the wives of the gods," he says, while spreading [the base] and cutting [the portions].
6.5.2.30. He cuts from both the rear and the front of the outstretched *viṣkalī*. 6.5.2.31. He pours clarified butter over it and anoints it back.
6.5.2.32. He says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard," and then, "Sacrifice to the wives of the gods. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 6.5.2.33.
He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Gṛhapati," while spreading [ghee] underneath and taking portions [of the oblation].
6.5.2.34. From the upper half of the lower rib, he cuts off a large piece of meat.
6.5.2.35. He pours clarified butter over it twice; he does not anoint it back. 6.5.2.36. He says, "O, cause [the Agnīdh] to announce," and "Sacrifice to Agni Gṛhapati.
6.5.2.37. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering on the northern half, passing beyond the previous offerings.

6.5.2.38. He places the *iḍā* on the upturned [hand], and for the *āgnīdhra* on the downward-turned [hand]. Having performed this up to the *śaṃyu*-formula, having offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation of clarified butter, and having gone forward to the east, he offers three *samiṣṭayajus* oblations with the formula: “Go to the sacrifice... in the wind” (VS 1.4.44g, omitting the first word). 6.5.2.39. With the formula, “This is thy seasonal womb,” he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling woods (*araṇī*).
Having offered the *phalīkaraṇa* oblation and having gone forward to the east, he offers the *taras* oblations. [Cf. 5.3.2.19–44]

6.5.3. He offers the *tarāṃsi* oblations with the formula, “Those gods who are destroyers of the sacrifice” (*ye devā yajñaghana*). He offers two spoonfuls (*sruvāhuti*) into the *gārhapatya* fire with the two mantras: “May Agni protect me from them; may we go to the world of the righteous, svāhā! Those gods who are stealers of the sacrifice who dwell upon the earth—may Agni protect me from them; may we go to the world of the righteous, svāhā! [The two mantras are condensed in 3.5.4a, and the word order differs from the *TS*.
It appears that “upon the earth” (*pṛthivyām adhi*) is missing from the first mantra in manuscript C.]

6.5.3.2. He takes four portions [of clarified butter]. He offers it with: “We have come... (as in 3.5.4b)... from heaven, svāhā! 6.5.3.3. With the two verses beginning, “Those gods who are slayers of the sacrifice” (cf. 3.5.4c), he offers two spoonfuls in the Āgnīdhra fire with: “Those who sit in the intermediate space, Vāyu is their leader... (as in 3.5.4c)... us, svāhā! Those gods who are stealers of the sacrifice, who sit in the intermediate space, Vāyu is my leader... (as in 3.5.4c)... us, svāhā! [The two mantras are condensed in 3.5.4c.]
6.5.3.4. He takes four portions. He offers it with: “O Savitṛ, those nights of thine, O thou who art in the realms, svāhā—svāhā.

6.5.3.5. With the words, “Those gods who are destroyers of the sacrifice” (cf. 3.5.4e), he offers two spoonfuls into the Āhavanīya fire: “Those gods who are destroyers of the sacrifice, who sit in heaven—may Sūrya protect me; may we be well-doers, svāhā! Those gods who are stealers of the sacrifice, who sit in heaven—may Sūrya protect me; may we be doers of good deeds, svāhā! [The two mantras are condensed in 3.5.4e; cf. the mantras labeled a and c above. [N1.78a1]
6.5.3.6. He takes four spoonfuls. He offers it with: “With that [which you gave] to Indra, place this [offering]—svāhā (3,5,4f + svāhā).

6.5.3.7. At the time for the *nipadas*, the Pratiprasthātṛ says, “Step aside,” [thinking]: “May I not pass over you; I shall carry around the *vasatīvarī* waters. 6.5.3.8. To the east of the two *havirdhāna* sheds and to the west of the *āhavanīya* fire, the sacrificer stands holding the King Soma. To the east of the hall and to the west of the *sadas*, the wife is seated.
6.5.3.9. To the west of the *gārhapatya* fire, the *vasatīvarī* waters have been set down. There, the *pratiprasthātṛ* takes them up with his left shoulder. 6.5.3.10.

Having carried them out by the eastern door to the south of the *gārhapatya*, and having brought them along the southern edge of the *sadas* to the southern end of the altar, he sets them down to the south of the sacrificial post, not touching it, with the formula: "You are the portion of Indra and Agni" (TS 1.3.12.c.1).

6.5.3.11. He takes them from there with his right shoulder. Having brought them back by the same way he came, he places them behind the Gārhapatya fire with the formula: "You are the portion of Mitra and Varuṇa. (1.3.12c2)

6.5.3.12. He takes them up from there with his right shoulder. Having carried them out by the eastern door to the north of the *gārhapatya* fire, south of the *sadas*, south of the *āgnīdhra*, and having gone to the north of the *āgnīdhrīya* fire, he brings them along the northern edge of the altar and places them to the north of the sacrificial post (*yūpa*), not touching it, with the formula: "You are the portions for the Viśve Devas. 6.5.3.13.
He takes them up from there with his left shoulder.

6.5.3.14. Having brought them back by the same way they were taken, he places them in the Āgnīdhra fire-shed with the formula: “Be watchful at the sacrifice” (TS 1.3.12d). 6.5.3.15. They remain together in the Āgnīdhra shed;

then he brings the King Soma, along with the Ādhavanīya and Pūtabhṛt jars. Their handles are covered with leather and washed clean. There are large enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*) made of *udumbara* wood that have been rubbed smooth; two fuel-sticks (*idhma*), one bundle of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), of which one consists of fifteen pieces of various kinds of wood: one piece from each of seven male trees and eight pieces from female trees. All of these have been thoroughly purified.

6.5.3.16. As he is sitting down, he gives the instruction: "Let her milk the *gharmaduh* cow for the *dadhigharma*; let her who is the *vratadhuk* of the sacrificer be for the *payasyā*, and let her who belongs to the wife be for the *āśira*.
6.5.3.17. Fifteen constellations lead the night.
7.1.1.1. Fifteen lunar mansions lead the night. 7.1.1.2. When the tenth one rises, the third part of the night has arrived. 7.1.1.3.
At that time, having risen and made silence, he causes the King to enter toward the southern *havirdhāna* shed.

7.1.1.4. Then he issues the command: "O Āgnīdhra, place the clarified butter on the fire; O Pratiprasthātṛ, wipe the offering-spoons, take the portions of clarified butter, and prepare the vessels; O Unnetṛ, having placed the pressing-stones, the Vāyu-vessels, and the woollen filters together in the *droṇakalaśa* jar, set them down in the two *havirdhāna* carts; and prepare the milk and the parched flour; O Āgnīdhra, pour out the *savanīya* oblations, all of which are for Indra, on eleven potsherds. 7.1.1.5. They do this. 7.1.1.6.
Having wiped the spoons, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the portions of clarified butter, including the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*), in the *āgnīdhra* shed.
7.1.1.7. Having run, he joins the vessels to the mound (khara) with the formula: “Agni is the deity; the Gāyatrī is the metre. 7.1.1.8.

On the eastern part of the southern half of the mound, he places the Upāṃśu vessel with the formula: “Thou art the vessel of the Upāṃśu. 7.1.1.9. With the formula: “Soma is the deity; the Triṣṭubh is the metre,” he places the Antaryāma vessel to the north of that [Upāṃśu vessel] with the formula: “Thou art the vessel of the Antaryāma.”
7.1.1.10. He places the Upāṃśusavana stone between [the other stones], touching them, facing south.

7.1.1.11. With the formula, “Indra is the deity; the Jagatī is the metre” (TS 3.1.6.3), he places the Aindravāyava vessel, containing the *parisraj* [garland], behind it without touching it, with the formula, “Thou art the vessel of Indra and Vāyu.

7.1.1.12. With the formula, “Bṛhaspati is the deity; the Anuṣṭubh is the metre” (TS 3.1.6.4), he places the Maitrāvaruṇa vessel, having two handles (*dvibhṛṣṭi*), behind that without touching it, with the formula, “Thou art the vessel of Mitra and Varuṇa.”

7.1.1.13. With the formula, “The Aśvins are the deity; the Paṅkti is the metre,” he places the Āśvina vessel, which is untouched by what follows it and shaped like a breast, with the words, “Thou art the vessel of the Aśvins.

7.1.1.14. With the formula, “Sūrya is the deity; the Bṛhatī is the metre,” he places the Śukra vessel made of Bilva wood to the south of that [Āśvina vessel], behind it, with the words, “Thou art the vessel of the Śukra.”

7.1.1.15. With the formula, “The moon is the deity; the *satobṛhatī* is the metre” (TS 3.1.6.c7), he places to the north of that the *manthin* cup made of *vaikaṅkata* wood with the formula, “Thou art the vessel of the *manthin*. 7.1.1.16. To the west of the two vessels for the *śukra* and *manthin*, he places the two *prasthitā* cups made of *aśvattha* wood, which have bases shaped like horse-hooves and openings on both sides, upon the *gṛtapātra* with the formula, “Ye are the vessels of the seasons.”

7.1.1.17. With the formula, “The Viśve Devās are the deity; the Uṣṇih is the metre,” he places the Āgrayaṇa vessel upon the front support of the southern Havirdhāna cart with the formula, “Thou art the vessel of the Āgrayaṇa. 7.1.1.18. With the formula, “Indra is the deity; the Kakubh is the metre,” he places the Ukthya vessel to the south of it with the formula, “Thou art the vessel of the Ukthas.
7.1.1.19. He sets down the resting vessel (upaśaya) beneath it.

7.1.1.20. To the north of this [Soma cart], he places the vessel for the Ādityas with the formula: “Thou art the vessel of the Ādityas. 7.1.1.21. They set down beside it the four-cornered Āditya-vessel made of Udumbara wood.

7.1.1.22. Having moved behind himself with the formula, “The earth is the deity; the Virāj is the metre,” he places the Dhruva-vessel on the unpounded ground to the east of the support of the northern Havirdhāna cart with the formula: “Thou art the vessel of the Dhruva.”
7.1.1.E. This is the action of setting forth (prasthitakarma).
bśs 7.2. 7.1.2.1. This is the action of setting forth (prasthitakarma).
7.1.2.2. When the clarified butter has been taken up, the Adhvaryu takes four portions with the *pracaraṇī* ladle. He offers it in the Āgnīdhra fire. 7.1.2.4.

Having mentally recited the *Pañcahotṛ* formula, he takes another four portions. 7.1.2.5. He offers it as a spoon-offering with the mantra: "From the mouth [of Agni], protect me from the spell; from every curse, svāhā! (TS 3.1.7.1).

7.1.2.6. They proceed with the clarified butter offerings. 7.1.2.7. Having hastened forward, the Adhvaryu sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass; he sprinkles the altar; he sprinkles what has been placed [upon it]. 7.1.2.8. Having poured out the water, he takes up the prastara-bunch.

7.1.2.9. He spreads the sacrificial grass (barhis). 7.1.2.10. Having stepped forward toward the east, he places the enclosing sticks (paridhi), which are made of udumbara wood and serve as the great enclosing sticks.
7.1.2.11. With their respective formulas (yajus), he places two fuel-sticks (samidh) upon the fire.
7.1.2.12. He causes the sacrificer to recite the *yajus* formulas.

7.1.2.13. He touches them with the *aupānuvākya* formulas: with "I yoke the earth for thee together with light" (3.1.6b1), he touches the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*); with "I yoke Vāyu for thee together with the intermediate space" (3.1.6b2), the southern one; with "I yoke speech for thee together with the sun" (3.1.6b3), the northern one.
7.1.2.14. He yokes the fire.

7.1.2.15. Having stepped forward, he places the *akhara* transversely; upon the *tiraścī* he places the *prastara*; upon the *prastara* the *juhū*; and the others upon the *akhara*. 7.1.2.16. Having set them down together and touched them all over with the formula, "The steadfast ones have sat down; that which is mine, O Agni... (cf. MS 1.1.12:8.3; KS 1.11:6; VS 2.6), he touches the ladles with the formula, "I yoke the three *vipṛc*s of the sun... (TS 3.1.6b4).

7.1.2.17. Having touched water, he touches the pressing-stones with the verse: “O dwellers of the waters (cf. BŚS 3.7.9.1b), embryos of Ṛta, guardians of the world, falcons, swift ones, peaks of the mountains, like protectors who have set out—by your voice call upon Indra; by your roar drive away diseases; you are harnessed, carry [the sacrifice]. 7.1.2.18.
Having stood up, he worships the King Soma with the formula: “For the heart thee,” and “With the mind thee—restrain [him], O Hotṛ.”

7.1.2.19. With the mantra, “O King Soma, come hither, descend” (ŚB 1.3.13c–f), he brings down the King [Soma] between the two pressing-boards, saying, “Do not fear; do not tremble as you descend. 7.1.2.20.
He places the King upon the pressing-skin over the pressing-stones. 7.1.2.21.
Having touched water, he takes this fuel-stick (*idhma*) consisting of fifteen pieces of wood from various trees, including a purified splinter.

7.1.2.22. Having untied it, sprinkled it with water, and poured clarified butter over it, while throwing it into the Āhavanīya fire, he says: "Recite for the gods who come in the morning"—if the *Sāman* is the *Rathantara*; "Recite for the gods who come in the morning"—if the *Sāman* is the *Bṛhat*; "Recite for the gods who come in the morning, for the gods who come in the morning"—if it is both *Sāmans*. 7.1.2.23. Having turned away, he mentally responds to three verses.

7.1.2.24. "They sit together; this is the *saṃsarpa* [chant]; 'Oṃ' is the response (*pratigara*) for this *ukthya*," so they say. 7.1.2.25. When he recognizes [the point] in the *prātaranuvāka* [with the verse]: "The Dawn has appeared, bright-hued; Agni has been established in his proper season; O wonder-workers, masters of wealth, your immortal chariot is yoked; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!"—then [he should respond].

7.1.2.26. Then the Adhvaryu takes four portions of clarified butter in the *pracaraṇī* ladle. He offers that with the formula: “May Agni hear my call with the kindling-stick, svāhā! (TS 1.3.13g). He makes an offering on the Āhavanīya fire with the *anuvitti* formula: “May the Waters hear my call, svāhā! (TS 1.3.13g). 7.1.2.27. Taking another four portions and seizing the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he stands up and issues the command. || 2 ||

7.1.3.1. Rising, he issues the command: "O Hotṛ, seek out water! O Camasādhvaryu of the Maitrāvaruṇa, come hither! O Ekadhanins, come hither! O Neṣṭṛ, lead up the wife! O Āgnīdh, establish yourself at the Cātvāla pit with the Hotṛ’s cup and the Vasatīvarī waters!"

7.1.3.2. [The Neṣṭṛ] leads [the wife] away. The Neṣṭṛ, together with the wife and the vessel for the foot-washing water, goes between the *cātvāla* pit and the rubbish heap (*utkara*), saying: "Go forth! Come up! O you two who belong to the *ṛta*, do not harm me" (TS 3.5.6f). They arrive at the flowing waters. 7.1.3.3. Having thrown a blade of sacrificial grass (*barhis*) into those waters, he makes an offering over them, saying: "O divine waters, O offspring of the waters, that wave which is your portion—*svāhā*" (TS 1.3.13h).
7.1.3.4. Saying, "Thou art a furrower" (TS 1.3.13i), he takes up the cup belonging to the Maitrāvaruṇa.
7.1.3.5. With the words, “*apāpām mṛdhram*,” he strikes the drops.
7.1.3.6. With the words, “*samudrasya vo 'kṣityā unnaye*” (VS 1.3.13k), he draws them up. 7.1.3.7. Following that, they draw up the *ekadhana* vessels with the words, “*indrāya va indrāya va*.”
7.1.3.8. With the words, “To the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas,” the Neṣṭṛ causes the wife to take up the foot-washing water (pānnejana).
7.1.3.9. With the words, “I take the foot-washing waters for you, O All-Gods (Viśve Devāḥ),” they come forward.

7.1.3.10. With the words, “Come forth! Arise! (with a variant reading), the Neṣṭṛ leads the wife out, saying: “May Agni lead you two along the lovely paths of Cosmic Order (Ṛta); Aditi by name shall lead your front; homage be to you; do not harm me.”
7.1.3.11. Having returned by the same way they came, he places them down behind the Gārhapatya fire.
7.1.3.12. The Adhvaryu approaches.
7.1.3.13. He touches the Hotṛ’s cup and the Vasatīvarī waters together at the Cātvāla pit.
7.1.3.14. He causes [the Soma] to flow from the *vasatīvarī* waters into the *hotṛ*’s cup.

7.1.3.15. He anoints that excess [Soma] across the filter with the *pracaraṇī* ladle, saying: "May light be united with light; may the oblation be united with the oblation; [unite] those who observe the vow with the well-prepared [oblations]. 7.1.3.16. They fill it up from the *maitrāvaruṇa*’s cup and from the *vasatīvarī* waters.

7.1.3.17. Whatever remains in the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup, they pour that into the *vasatīvarī* waters. Then, touching this full cup, they both recite: “You are bright, possessing bright luster; you are the bearers of the bright one. I take your cup, which is full of light. With the former [cup], they cause the *nigrābhya* waters to flow forward; with the latter, the *vasatīvarī* waters and the *ekadhana* waters.
7.1.3.18. “O Adhvaryu, have you drunk?”—thus the Hotṛ asks the Adhvaryu. 7.1.3.19.
“I have drunk it well, O most exalted one,” he replies as he hastens away with the residue of the libation.

7.1.3.20. If he does not ask, one should say, “Peace, O teacher. 7.1.3.21. With the verse, “O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles (1.3.13l+svāhā),” he offers the residue into the Āhavanīya fire; and with the verse, “Him whom you urge on in the contests for booty, he shall be the controller of eternal nourishments, svāhā,” he offers if it is an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
7.1.3.22. If it is an Ukthya sacrifice, he wipes [the residue] upon the enclosing stick (paridhi).

7.1.3.23. If, having offered the *atirātra* and wiped [the ladle] on the enclosing-stick (*paridhi*) while reciting the *yajus*, he enters [the hall], then, having placed the *pracaraṇī* on the pole, he draws the *dadhi-graha* for Prajāpati with a four-cornered *audumbara* Aditya-vessel across the strainers, [taking] from the curd, with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the luminous, for the luminous Prajāpati, for Dakṣa... for the Earth. 7.1.3.24. He supports [the vessel] with the formula: "O Indra, drive away the mind of the hater; drive away the one who seeks to harm; slay him! (TS 3.5.8b).

7.1.3.25. He rises with the formula, “For out-breathing thee” (3.5.8c1). He moves forward with, “For in-breathing thee” (3.5.8c2). With, “For diffused-breathing thee; for the existent thee—I offer thee, full of light, svāhā! svāhā! (3.5.8c3 + svāhā), he gives it to another. 7.1.3.26. Having set down the vessel in its proper place, while [the Adhvaryu] removes the third portion of the *vasatīvarī* waters with the verse, “May Agni protect us at the morning pressing” (3.1.9b), [the Pratiprasthātṛ] pours them into the other jar with, “Vaiśvānara by his greatness... may we be sharers in the draughts” (3.1.9d).

7.1.3.27. Following that, they bring the *ekadhana* waters, [saying]: "You are the *nigrābhya*s. 7.1.4.1. Over the *nigrābhya*s, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "You are the *nigrābhya*s, heard by the gods (3.1.8a); you are bright, bearers of brightness. Satisfy my life-span, satisfy my breath... satisfy [them]. Let not my troops thirst. (7.1.4.1) [N1,80a10; M198; T1,236; C95] 7.1.4.1. "You are the *nigrābhya*s, heard by the gods," thus he causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the *nigrābhya*s: "You are bright, bearers of brightness. Satisfy my life, satisfy my breath... satisfy [them]. Let not my groups thirst. (7.1.4.1) [N1,80a10; M198; T1,236; C95] 7.1.4.1. 7.1.4.2. Having poured [the grain] into the royal [mortar], he draws out half [of it].

7.1.4.3. With the formula, “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ” (cf. 1.4.1a, with variation; as shown in abbreviated form in the TS), he takes up the pressing-stone for the *upāṃśu* [cup]: “With the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee; thou art a pressing-stone, a performer of the sacrifice for the gods, deep... (4) a winner, full of vigor, and a subduer of enemies. [N1,80b2]

7.1.4.4. Having turned it upward and placed the *upāṃśu* cup upon it, he measures out from the King [Soma] five times with the formula, "For Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, thee," and five times silently: "For Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, thee; for Indra, the slayer of the adversary, thee; for Indra, the overcomer of the adversary, thee; for Indra, accompanied by the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas, the conqueror of Vṛtra, thee; for Indra, accompanied by Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, and the Viśve Devas, thee. He measures out from the King [Soma] five times with the *yajus* and five times silently.

7.1.4.5. With the mantra, “śvātrā stha vṛtraturaḥ” (1.4.1c), the sacrificer pours water from the *nigrābhya* vessels, saying, “... rādhogūrtā ... pibatu. 7.1.4.6. With the mantra, “yat te soma divi jyotiḥ” (1.4.1d), he touches it, saying, “yat pṛthivyāṃ yad urāv antarikṣe ... dātre voca. 7.1.4.7. With the mantra, “dhiṣaṇe vīḷū satī vīḷayethām” (1.4.1e), he touches the two boards across the hide, saying, “ūrjaṃ dadhāthāṃ ... mā mā hiṃsiṣṭam.”
7.1.4.8. With the mantra, "The Soma belongs to Indra; it has increased you by mind, O well-born ones (3.1.8b)," he satisfies the King [Soma] with water, [reciting] "Born from the Ṛta—[the Soma]."

7.1.4.9. With the formula, “Light is gold,” he mixes it with gold: “With that I mix thee; light is the waters—with them I mix thee; light is the meters—with them I mix thee; light is Indra and Agni—with them two I mix thee; light is heaven and earth—with them two I mix thee. Thou art cooked, thou art made cooked; for Indra thee, most beloved by Indra. 7.1.4.10. The Pratiprasthātṛ inserts six shoots between his fingers; he holds the Upāṃśu-vessel in his hands, two in each.

7.1.4.11. With the formula, “We [offer] you, O sinless one” (VS 7.9.1a, with variation), the Adhvaryu strikes three times without letting [the stones] touch one another, [saying]: “May Vāyu, sent forth by Indra and joined with him, be your sharer; may Mitra be your sharer; may Varuṇa be your sharer. 7.1.4.12. He presses eight times at first, not letting go of the pressing stone. The Pratiprasthātṛ gathers the stones together and takes up the first two stalks in the Upāṃśu cup.

7.1.4.13. He holds those two between his hands while reciting, "Flow for Vācaspati, O vigorous one" (1.4.2a1); the Adhvaryu pours [the juice] and settles [the stones]. 7.1.4.14. Without letting go of the pressing stone, he gathers it eleven times for the second time; meanwhile, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes up four stalks (*aṃśu*) in the Upāṃśu cup. 7.1.4.15.
He holds those two between his hands while reciting, "The bull, purified by the hands, with the two stalks of the bull" (1.4.1a2); the Adhvaryu pours [the juice] and settles [the stones].
7.1.4.16. Having performed this a third time without following the sequence, those two collect the pressing-stone itself twelve times.

7.1.4.17. The Pratiprasthātṛ takes up six stalks in the Upāṃśu cup. 7.1.4.18. The Adhvaryu holds those two between his fingers and pours [the juice] with the formula, "Thou art the god, the purifier of the gods; for those whose portion thou art, for them I take thee. He then sets them down.
7.1.4.19. From this [verse], "Thou art the one made by the dog" (ŚB 1.4.2b), the Adhvaryu takes up the cup with the words, "Make our offerings sweet.

7.1.4.20. He wipes it all around with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*) with the words, "May the mind purify thee" (ŚB 1.4.2c). He rises with the words, "Follow the wide mid-region" (ŚB 1.4.2f). 7.1.4.21. He proceeds to the north of the Hotṛ with the words, "For all thy powers, celestial and terrestrial" (ŚB 1.4.2d).
7.1.4.22. He offers with the formula: “*Śvāhā! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya!*” (TS 1.4.2.e).
7.1.4.23. With the formula: “*Thou art bhūḥ, the best of rays!*” (TS 3.2.10.2), he breathes over the offering, saying: “O protector of the breath, protect my breath! 7.1.4.24. With the formula:
“*To the gods who drink the rays of light, thee!*” (TS 1.4.2.f), he wipes his hand, turned forward, along the enclosing stick (*paridhi*).
7.1.4.25. Having approached the Hotṛ from the south, he pours the residue into the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the formula, “This is thy womb; for out-breathing thee” (1.4.2g). 7.1.4.26.
He sets down the vessel with the formula, “For out-breathing thee, for in-breathing thee” (1.1.6.1h).
7.1.4.27. The Pratiprasthātṛ inserts two stalks each into the King Soma.
7.2.1.1. They separate the King (Soma). He pours [the water] upon it; they press it. 7.2.1.2.

They approach the *nigrābhya* waters. Taking the King with his joined palms, the Adhvaryu pours him over the *nigrābhya* waters while reciting: "To the east, to the west, to the north, to the south"—and, "O Mother, flow forth for us," saying, "May those quarters support you."

7.2.1.3. This very [action] is the approach to the *nigrābha*; he pours [the water] down. They press [the Soma]. He pours down [the water], approaching the *nigrābha*, as they press; they approach the *nigrābha* as he pours it down, while they press. 7.2.1.4. With the fourth [verse], he collects [it]. 7.2.1.5. The *unnetṛ* brings that [Soma] into the other jar.
7.2.1.6. From this point on, they should not bring back the King (Soma).
7.2.1.7. Having poured out the *ekadhana* waters and having dripped them from the *vasatīvarī* waters, the *unnetṛ* pours them forth.
7.2.1.8. Having poured them forth with the mantra, “May you swell; may [the waters] meet you” (TS 3.2.5.k), they cause the King to swell with the mantra, “O Soma, [be] a gathering from all sides.”

7.2.1.9. With the formula, “May the waters be auspicious for you” (ŚB 4.2.7n with variation), he pours [the water] for a Kṣatriya; [he adds], “may they come to you—do thou take them. He pours [the water]. They press [the Soma]. They go to the *nigrābha* [formula]. He pours [the water]. They press [the Soma]. They go to the *nigrābha*. He pours [the water]. They press [the Soma]. They go to the *nigrābha*. He pours [the water]. They press [the Soma]. They go to the *nigrābha*. He pours [the water]. They press [the Soma]. He collects [the Soma] with the fourth [verse]. 7.2.1.11. The *unnetṛ* brings that [Soma] into the other jar. From this point on, they should not bring back the King [Soma].
7.2.1.12. Having poured out the *ekadhana* waters and having dripped them from the *vasatīvarī* waters, the *unnetṛ* pours them together.

7.2.1.13. Having poured them together with the verse, “Swell up; let [the waters] gather unto thee” (TS 3.2.5k), they cause the King [Soma] to swell with the verse, “O Soma, [be] a gathering-place from all sides.

7.2.1.14. With the verse, “May thy milks be auspicious” (TS 4.2.7n), he pours them together for the King belonging to the royal class (*rājanya*), using the formula, “And may they be auspicious; do thou hold [them].”
7.2.1.15. They press [the Soma]. They go to the *nigrābhya* waters. He pours [the water] in. They press. They go to the *nigrābha*. He pours in. They press.
They go to the *nigrābha*. He pours in. They press. They go to the *nigrābha*. He pours in. 7.2.1.16. They press. With the fourth [pressing], he collects [the Soma]; they do not cause it to swell.
7.2.1.17. Now, they indeed perform the *nigrābha* nine times; they collect [the water] three times; they cause it to swell twice; thus they make the King (Soma) well-milked. 7.2.1.18.

The *unnetṛ* leads him, together with the two *daśāpavitra* filters, into the western jar. 7.2.1.19. Having placed the pressing-stones with their faces turned toward one another, the *udgātṛ*s remove the dregs (*arjīṣa*) from them.
7.2.1.20. Upon these [vessels], they place the *droṇakalaśa*.
7.2.1.21. They wait for the rising sun with the *antaryāma* cup.

7.2.1.22. When the sun has risen, he issues the command: "Spread out the *daśāpavitra* filter with its fringes pointing northward; purify the *śukra* [cup] continuously; we shall draw the cups for the sacrificer."
7.2.1.23. They do this.
7.2.1.24. They spread out the woollen filter with its fringes pointing northward. 7.2.1.25. Above the *droṇakalaśa* jar, the *udaṅka* purifies itself among the *nigrābhya* waters.

7.2.1.26. Having taken the *nigrābhya* waters from another jar and having poured them continuously through the filter into the *droṇakalaśa*, the bright juice (*śukra*) flows clear; he takes the *antaryāma* cup. 7.2.1.27.
Into it he draws [the juice], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; O Maghavan, restrain within, protect the Soma, and rejoice!
(TS 1.4.3a,b). 7.2.1.28. He supports it, saying: "Thou art made ready by the dogs" (TS 1.4.3c1).
7.2.1.29. "Make our nourishments honey-sweet," he says.

7.2.1.30. He wipes [the vessel] all around with the *daśāpavitra* filter, saying, "May the mind purify you" (TS 1.4.3d). Then he rises up, saying, "Follow the wide mid-region" (TS 1.4.3e). 7.2.1.31. Saying, "For all thy powers, celestial and terrestrial" (TS 1.4.3c), he walks past the *hotṛ* priest to the south.
7.2.1.32. He offers with the formula: “*Śvāhā! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya!*” (TS 1.4.3f).

7.2.1.26. Having offered with the formula: “*Thou art the yoke-pole, the best of the reins,*” he breathes out over the offering with the words: “*O Apānnapāt, protect my out-breathing!*” 7.2.1.27. With the formula: “*To the gods who drink the rays of light,*” he rubs his hand against the enclosing stick from west to east.
7.2.1.28. Having approached the north of the Hotṛ, he pours the residue from the Āgrayaṇa vessel [into the cup] with the formula, “This is thy womb” (1.4.3h).
7.2.1.29. He sets down the cup with the formula, “For out-breathing thee.
7.2.1.30. He touches the Upāṃśusavana stone with the formula, “For through-breathing thee.”
7.2.1.31. The cups are drawn with the mind.
7.2.1.32. Having taken the Āgrayaṇa vessel and the *upayāma* support, he draws the cup for Indra and Vāyu with [the verse]: "Come hither, O Vāyu... (RV 7.92.1).
“O Vāyu, come hither, O drinker of the pure, for the first draught! You are taken with a support: for Vāyu, you! (TS 1.4.4a,b). 7.2.2.2. He hands it over.

7.2.2.3. He takes hold of it [saying]: "O Indra and Vāyu, these [Somas] are pressed; for they yearn [for you]. You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to Indra and Vāyu. This is your womb; [I take you] for the two who are in harmony" (cf. 1.4.4d2). 7.2.2.4. Having wiped it all around with the *daśāpavitra* strainer, he sets it down. He mixes it with gold.

7.2.2.5. He takes the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa. Into it he draws [the soma] with: "This is your call, O Mitra and Varuṇa... You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to Mitra and Varuṇa. This is your birthplace; [I take you] for the two who live by the cosmic order (ṛta).
Having wiped it around with the fringed filter, he sets it down. He mixes it with milk.

7.2.2.7. Having set aside the cup for the Aśvins, he takes up the Śukra vessel. Into it he draws [the soma] with the formula: "This Vena impels... they lick... thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śaṇḍa. This is thy womb; protect manly power. (1.4.8a,b with variation). 7.2.2.8.
Having wiped it around with the fringed filter, he sets it down. He mixes it with gold.

7.2.2.9. He takes up the *manthin* cup. Into it he draws [the juice] with the formula: “As of old... thou art increasing; thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Marka; this is thy womb; protect the offspring. (1.4.9a,b with variants). 7.2.2.10. Having wiped it around with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*), he sets it down. He mixes it with flour. He draws the *āgrayaṇa* in two streams. 7.2.2.11.
They cause the water-scoop (*udaṅka*) and the *nigrābhya* waters, along with the filter, to be brought forward.

7.2.2.12. He draws [the cup] with the words: "O gods who are eleven in heaven" (1.4.10a,b with variant), "and the eleven upon the earth—enjoy! You are taken with a support; I draw you, acceptable to the Viśve Devas. You are the Āgrayaṇa; entering, protect me with power and vigor. 7.2.2.13. Having turned eastward and bent his right knee, he utters the *abhihiṅkāra* over the Āgrayaṇa cup, saying: "hīṃ hiṃ him."

7.2.2.14. Having purified [the Soma] eight times with the formula: "Soma purifies itself; Soma purifies for this *brahman*; he purifies for this *kṣatra*; he purifies for this *viś*; he purifies for this pressing sacrificer; he purifies for food; he purifies for strength; he purifies for well-being; he purifies for spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*)," he cleanses it around with the *daśāpavitra* filter using the formula: "This is thy womb; for all the gods, thee! and sets it down. He mixes it with gold.
7.2.2.15. From this point onward, the *grahas* are drawn with speech. Here he draws the *atigrāhya* cups. 7.2.2.16.

Having taken up the *ukthya* vessel together with the *atigrāhya* vessels, he draws [the juice] into it [with the formula]: "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra the Great, for Viṣṇu, I take thee who art pleasing. This is thy womb; for Indra, thee, the one desiring the *uktha*. 7.2.2.17.
Having wiped it around with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*), he sets it down. He mixes it with gold.

7.2.2.18. Having brought the *dhruva*-vessel from behind himself, he draws [the soma] into it with the formula: “The gods [placed] the head... [1.1.13a] ... O gods. Then: “Thou art taken with a support; for Agni Vaiśvānara, thee, the beloved, I draw. Thou art firm (*dhruva*), thou art immovable in thy station” [1.1.13b].
7.2.2.19. At this time, the *unnetṛ* pours water around [the vessel]; the *nigrābhya* waters are for the sacrificer: “This is thy womb; for Dhruva and Vaiśvānara, thee” [1.4.13b4 with variant].
7.2.2.20. Having wiped it with the *daśāpavitra* strainer, he sets it down. He mixes it with gold. 7.2.2.21. With the words, "May it leap unto me," he consecrates the drops that have spilled. || 6 ||
With the words, “May [the drop] not fall away from me,” he consecrates the drops that have fallen, [saying]: “… may you not strike us down, together with offspring…” (cf.
ŚB 3.1.8.3). 7.2.3.2. With the verse, “The drop has fallen” (RV 3.1.8d), he wipes both hands with the *daśāpavitra* filter, [reciting]: “... the earth … the oblations” (l.c. d).
7.2.3.3. Having touched water and taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he continues the *pavamāna* chant.

7.2.3.4. He touches the *droṇakalaśa* with the formula, “Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati thee!”; the *ādhavanīya* with “For Indra thee!”, and the *pūtabhṛt* with “For the All-gods thee!”. He steps out. The *prastotṛ* takes hold of him from behind; the *pratihartṛ* takes hold of the *prastotṛ*; the *udgātṛ* takes hold of the *pratihartṛ*; the *brahmán* takes hold of the *udgātṛ*; the sacrificer (*yajamāna*) takes hold of the *brahmán*; and others take hold of the sacrificer.
7.2.3.5. Having gone out, he performs an oblation of the scattered drops with the formula: "That drop of thine which falls... [3.1.10c] ...that I offer, svāhā (3.1.10c + svāhā).

7.2.3.6. He offers the *anucara* verse with: "Fulfill the hymn with the Ṛc (3.1.10b + svāhā)," and [the second] with: "With the Gāyatra... [l.c. b] ...on the path, svāhā. 7.2.3.7. Having mentally recited the *Saptahotṛ* formula, he offers the *sarvāhuti* (all-oblation).

7.2.3.8. [The Adhvaryu says: “May speech go first; let it go at the front” (TS 3.1.10.g). They proceed toward the north for the *āstāva* [singing ground], [reciting] “straight-going... [TS 3.1.10.g] ...and upon the sacrificer. 7.2.3.9. [The Adhvaryu] strews sacrificial grass (*barhis*) upon the *āstāva*, [saying]: “Thou art the under-layering for the *ṛc* and the *sāman*. 7.2.3.10.
Sitting down [behind the *prastara*], he hands the *prastara* bundle to the *prastotṛ*, [saying]: “For the procreation of the couple.”

7.2.3.11. He mutters the introductory formula: “Vāyu is the utterer of *hiṅ*; Agni... [3.3.2.a] ...may they bestow vital breaths upon me; Soma purifies. 7.2.3.12. The Prastotṛ says: “O Brahman, O Praśāstṛ, we shall chant the hymn (*stoṣyāmaḥ*).

7.2.3.13. The Brahman mutters the impulse formula: “O God Savitṛ, this he has told you” (3.2.7a–f). He then utters aloud: “Impel that... [3.2.7a] ...in the impulse of the god Savitṛ, accompanied by Indra, chant the hymn (*indravantaḥ stuta*).”

7.2.3.14. When the *sāman* has been chanted, the *unnetṛ* priest, purifying the King [Soma] while facing eastward, should not pour it into the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, but rather into the *ādhavanīya* vessel from the spaces for the cups (*graha*). 7.2.3.15. When the *prastotṛ* chants the fifth [verse], the *adhvaryu* recites the *daśahotṛ* formula.
7.2.3.16. Then he makes [the sacrificer] recite the *anvāroha* formula: "Thou art a hawk, having the *gāyatrī* metre... [3.2.1.1] ...carry us across."

7.2.3.17. When the *stotra* has been chanted, he issues the command: "O Āgnīdhra, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass (*barhis*); prepare the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*); O Pratiprasthātṛ, bring the animal victim near. 7.2.3.18. Having returned, he worships King Soma with the verse, "O Viṣṇu, you are our closest relative... (TB 3.1.10k), concluding with "...grant us protection... [which is] imperishable" (TB 3.1.10k). 7.2.3.19. With the verse, "O Agni, come for the feast... (TB 3.5.2.1), he honors the Āgnīdhra with the ritual service of the sacrifice, continuing with "...being praised upon the sacrificial grass" (TB 3.5.2.1).

7.2.3.20. With the verse, "O Bull, you are our closest [kinsman]," he touches the two *havirdhāna* sheds; with "Grant us imperishable shelter," and "Agni is the head... (TS 1.5.5c), he touches the *sruk* ladles; with "...enlivens the heaven... (TS 1.5.5c), he enlivens [the *sruk*s]; with "O Vāyu, of the hundred bay steeds... he touches the vessels dedicated to Vāyu; with "...you have joined... by your power," and "All [the people] have magnified Indra," he touches the *sadas*; and with "The ocean, whose expanse is vast... the lord," [he touches the *sadas*].

7.2.3.21. Having said, "Come, O sacrificer," the Adhvaryu enters the two Havirdhāna sheds and draws the draught for the Aśvins from the Droṇakalaśa with the formula: "O Aśvins, [that] stalk of yours which is honey-sweet... (1.4.6a,b); "O Aśvins... mix [it]... (1.4.6a); "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Aśvins; this is thy womb; for the two Mādhvīs, thee. 7.2.3.22. Having wiped it around with the fringe of the filter, he sets it down. He mixes it with gold and proceeds with the ritual actions pertaining to the drawing of the cups.
7.2.3.23. With the formula, "For my out-breath," he gazes at the Upāṃśu cup. || 7 ||

With the words, “For breath, ma(?),” he looks at the *upāṃśu* cup, saying: “O giver of splendor, purify yourself for splendor; grant me of that; may I partake of that; I wipe this away for the sake of sacred luster (*brahmavarcasa*).”

7.2.4.2. Whatever desire he may have, he should draw the Antaryāma cup with the formula, “For my out-breath (apāna)”; the Upāṃśusavana stone with, “For my diffused breath (vyāna)”; the Aindravāyava cup with, “For my speech (vāc)”; the Maitrāvaruṇa cup with, “For my skill and will (dakṣakratu)”; the Āśvina cup with, “For my hearing (śrotra)”; the Śukra and Manthin cups with, “For my two eyes (cakṣus)”; the Āgrayaṇa cup with, “For my self (ātman)”; if there is any Atigrāhya cup, [he draws it] with, “For my vigor (vīrya)”; the Ukthya cup with, “For my limbs (aṅga)”; [and for the Āyu cup... for my life-span (āyus).

"Ma" is for the *dhruva* cup; "for the foundation, ma" is for the seasonal cup (*ṛtupātra*); "Thou art the belly of Viṣṇu"—thus for the *droṇakalaśa*; "Thou art the belly of Indra"—thus for the *ādhavanīya*; "Thou art the belly of the All-gods"—thus for the *pūtabhṛt*. "O Soma, we take hold of thee"—thus for the *droṇakalaśa*; "The Udgātṛ, the observer of men, may he carry us across for our well-being. 7.2.4.3. "Who art thou? What is thy name?"—with these words, he gazes beyond the *āhavanīya* fire.

7.2.4.4. “For whom you? For Ka you?”—with these words he gazes at the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*). “Bestowing splendor, purify yourself for splendor; grant me of that; may I partake of that which is yours; this of yours I wipe away for the sake of cattle. 7.2.4.5. Whatever desire he may have, the Adhvaryu recites the *Daśahotṛ* formula over the offering-spoons (*sruk*) and the cups (*graha*).
7.2.4.6. Having touched water and stepped out, he recites the invitatory verse (*anuvāka*) for the one being girt with the sacrificial cord (*parivīyamāna*).
7.2.4.7. The Savanīya animal sacrifice belongs to Agni; its ritual procedure is established up to the *pravara* (invocation of ancestors).

7.2.4.8. He chooses the *pravara*. He causes the announcement to be made. He says, "O, cause [the Hotṛ] to announce!"—"Agni, the divine Hotṛ, shall worship the gods, he who is wise... from among men. He shall bring the footprint, the secondary word, the further secondary word; he shall speak the words of the Brahman and carry them forward; the Brāhmaṇas are the promoters of this sacrifice. Thus he chooses the Hotṛ. He asks him, "What is your name? He declares his name. "O Soma-worshipper... [and so on].
He who throws the entire [portion]—just as the name of the *hotṛ* occurs [in the ritual sequence, cf.
5.2.1.20–24]—the *hotṛ* offers the *pravṛtāhuti* with the mantra: “May I become beloved of speech” (3.1.10a, p.?).
Then the *adhvaryu* offers with: “I yoke Agni, who goes at dawn and awakens at the break of day; *svāhā*! (7.2.4.10).
7.2.4.11. He says, “O, cause [the gods] to hear!”—“The two Aśvins are the Adhvaryus from the office of the Adhvaryu.

7.2.4.12. “So-and-so and so-and-so are the human [officiants],” he says, as he throws in two wood-shavings (śakala) according to their names; they offer the oblation with the formula: “May I be pleasing to speech; fulfill the hymn with the Ṛg-verse. 7.2.4.12. Then the Adhvaryu offers the oblation with: “I yoke the two Aśvins, who travel at dawn and wake at daybreak; Svāhā!”
7.2.4.13. He says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard," [referring to] "Mitra and Varuṇa as the two Praśāstṛs, from the office of the Praśāstṛ.
7.2.4.14. "Such-and-such is the human [name]," saying this, he throws a splinter [of wood] according to the person's name.
7.2.4.15. The Maitrāvaruṇa offers the *pravṛtāhuti* oblation with the formula, "May I become acceptable to speech."

7.2.4.16. Then the Adhvaryu offers the oblation with: “I yoke Mitra and Varuṇa, who travel at dawn and wake with the light of the dawn; svāhā! 7.2.4.17. He says: “O, cause it to be heard!”—“Indra is the Brahman priest from the Brāhmaṇa.
7.2.4.18. He throws a wood-shaving with the words: “So-and-so, the human,” using whatever name that person may have.

7.2.4.19. The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin offers the *pravṛtāhuti* with the formula, "May I be beloved of speech. Then the Adhvaryu offers with, "I yoke Indra, who goes at dawn and awakens at the break of day; svāhā! 7.2.4.20.
He says, "Call for the *āśrāvaṇa*," and [the Āgnīdhra responds], "The Maruts from the vessel. 7.2.4.21.
He throws a splinter of wood with the words, "So-and-so, the human," using whatever name that person may have.

7.2.4.22. The Potṛ offers the Pravṛt oblation with the formula, "May I be pleasing to speech. Then the Adhvaryu offers with, "O Maruts who travel at dawn and wake at the break of day, I yoke you; svāhā! 7.2.4.23.
He says, "Call for the Śrauṣaṭ," and [the Āgnīdhra responds], "From the Neṣṭṛ, O divine ladies.
7.2.4.24. He throws a splinter of wood with the words, "So-and-so, the human," using whatever name that person has.

7.2.4.25. The Neṣṭṛ offers the *pravṛtāhuti* with the formula: "May I be beloved of speech. Then the Adhvaryu offers with: "I yoke the divine women who travel at dawn and wake with the Dawn; svāhā! 7.2.4.26.
He says, "Call for the *āśrāvaṇa*," and [the Āgnīdhra responds] from the *āgnīdhra* hearth: "O Agnīdh! 7.2.4.27.
He throws a splinter [of wood] while saying, "So-and-so, the human," using whatever name that person may have.

7.2.4.28. The Agnīdh offers the *pravṛtāhuti* with the formula, "May I become beloved of speech. Then the Adhvaryu offers with, "I yoke Agni, who travels at dawn and awakens at the break of day; svāhā!"

7.2.4.29. Then he offers these oblations: "I yoke Bṛhaspati, who goes forth at dawn and awakens at the break of day, svāhā!"—this toward the Brahman; "I yoke Sūrya, who goes forth at dawn and awakens at the break of day, svāhā!"—this toward the Udgātṛ; "I yoke Prajāpati, who goes forth at dawn and awakens at the break of day, svāhā!"—this toward the entire *sadas* assembly; "I yoke Viṣṇu, who goes forth at dawn and awakens at the break of day, svāhā!"—this toward the Acchāvāka; "I yoke the Brahman..."

"To the early-faring Dawn, Svāhā!"—thus from the Subrahmaṇya; "I yoke Parjanya, the early-farer, awakened by the Dawn, Svāhā!"—thus the Unnetṛ responds. There are only these many officiating priests (ṛtvij). 7.2.4.30. From this point he causes the announcement to be made. He says, "O, cause it to be heard!"—"Agni is the leader of the divine clans, whom the sacrificer among men brings forth. For those two, may the household-fire shine with undivided light for a hundred winters. May they be united in their purpose, yet their bodies remain distinct. Thus he says.
7.2.4.31. The sacrificial formulas (yajūṃṣi) of the *apāvya* oblations are established.
7.2.4.32. He offers two oblations following the *daśahotuḥ* formula. 7.2.4.32. And he recites that which is [prescribed] during the *pavamāna* chant.

7.2.4.33. And the ritual action is accomplished with the offering-spoons (*sruk*). 7.2.4.34. Having performed the offering with the omentum (*vapa*), they purify themselves at the *cātvāla* pit with the three-verse hymn beginning, "O Waters, you are indeed the source of bliss.
7.2.4.35. From this point on, they proceed to the procession.
7.3.1.1. They indeed proceed from here.

7.3.1.2. With the words, "O wooden sword (sphya), may there be well-being," they pay homage to the *utkara* heap; with the words, "O *vighana*, may there be well-being... O sacrifice, come hither! [they pay homage].

7.3.1.3. With the words, "May Heaven and Earth invite me hither," he approaches Heaven and Earth; with "The *āstāva* invites me hither," the *āstāva*; with "The *kalaśa* invites me hither," the *kalaśa*; with "Soma invites me hither," Soma; with "Agni invites me hither," Agni; with "The gods invite me hither," the gods; with "The sacrifice invites me hither," the sacrifice; and with "May the *hotrās* invite me hither at the call," the *hotrās*.
7.3.1.4. "Homage to Agni, the slayer of Makha; may he not take away my glory as Makha’s," with these words they worship the Āhavanīya fire.

7.3.1.5. "Homage to Rudra, the slayer of Makha; having paid homage, protect me"—with this they worship the Āgnīdhra fire. "Homage to Indra, the slayer of Makha; do not destroy my power and vigor"—with this they worship the Hotṛ fire. "Homage to Yama, the slayer of Makha; may he not take away my glory as Makha’s"—with this they worship the Mārjālīya fire. (cf. 3.2.4e) [cf. 3.2.4.2]

7.3.1.6. "'Be firm, O you two who are loose'—these two, moving together, protect me from distress. May the god Sūrya protect me from celestial distress; Vāyu from the intermediate space; Agni from the earth; Yama from the fathers; Sarasvatī from men."

7.3.1.7. With the words, "O divine doors, do not burn me," he gazes at the two doors of the *sadas*. With "Homage to the *sadas*," he looks at the *sadas*. With "Homage to the lord of the *sadas*," [he looks] at the sacrificer. With "Homage to the eyes of the friends who go before," he gazes at the eyes of those who have already entered. With "Homage to heaven, homage to earth," [he concludes]. 7.3.1.8. With the words, "O son of a remarried woman (*daidhiṣavya*), do not harm us," he takes a blade of grass from where he is about to sit down, saying, "Rise up from here; sit on the seat of another who is more foolish than we."

7.3.1.9. With the words, “Cast out is the one who dwells in another’s power,” he throws away a blade of grass. With the words, “Here I sit in the seat of life,” he turns back toward the east, makes a lap facing west toward the *hotṛ*’s altar (*dhiṣṇiya*), and sits down.

7.3.1.10. Having sat down, he mutters: “May I go forth from the hollows and from the heights; protect me today, O Heaven and Earth” (3.2.4m,n). 7.3.1.11. With the words, “Come, O Soma-loving fathers,” he gazes beyond the southern half of the *sadas*. [3.2.4.5]

7.3.1.12 “May I be possessed of fathers through you,” he says, making an añjali; “may you be possessed of good offspring through me. 7.3.1.13. Moving toward the sacrificial cakes (puroḍāśa) placed on the south side, the Adhvaryu, hastening, says: “Recite for Indra the morning libation as the sacrificial cakes are being cut off.
7.3.1.14. The Pratiprasthātṛ spreads a base of clarified butter upon two [cakes].

7.3.1.15. He takes two portions of parched grains (*dhānā*) into the *juhū* ladle; twice of the *karambha* porridge; twice of the parched barley meal (*parivāpa*); twice of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*); and twice of the curd-mixture (*payasyā*). He pours clarified butter over them. He anoints them back [with butter from the *upabhṛt*]. 7.3.1.16. He takes one portion each from the northern half [of the cakes] into the *upabhṛt* ladle. He pours clarified butter over them twice. He does not anoint them back. 7.3.1.17. Having joined [the two ladles], the Adhvaryu places them [on the fire].
7.3.1.18. He says, "O, cause it to be heard!"—"Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Indra regarding the cakes set forth for the morning pressing of the morning sacrifice.
7.3.1.19. At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ* call, he makes the offering.
7.3.1.20. While pouring together the portions for the *sviṣṭakṛt* of the cakes, he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni."
7.3.1.21. He says, “O, cause [the Hotṛ] to announce! [The Maitrāvaruṇa says,] “Prompt for Agni! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 7.3.1.22.

Having stepped across and placed the two ladles (*sruc*) in their respective places, and having handed over these sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) to the Hotṛ and set them down near him, he approaches and says, “Recite for Vāyu and for Indra-Vāyu!
7.3.1.23. He takes the cup for Indra-Vāyu (*aindravāyava*). || 9 ||
“O Vāyu, recite for Indra and Vāyu!”—7.3.2.2. with these words, the Adhvaryu takes up the Aindravāyava cup, saying: “Thou art taken with a support. (TS 3.2.10.1a1)

7.3.2.3. The Pratiprasthātṛ draws [the cup] with a four-cornered Āditya-vessel made of Udumbara wood from the Droṇakalaśa, [saying]: “Thou art the seat of speech; I draw thee for the two protectors of speech, for the two protectors of the will, for the two overseers of this firm sacrifice” (3.2.10a).
7.3.2.4. As they go out, [he recites]: “May this sacrifice be a peaceful rite, O gods” (3.1.9.3), and “For the plants, for our cattle, for our people.”
7.3.2.5. Having gone out, the Adhvaryu mutters the *yajus*: “For all beings you are the sacrifice; swell, O divine Soma, rich in ghee” (TS 3.1.9.3).

7.3.2.6. He says, “O, cause [the Agnīdh] to hear! and “Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Vāyu and for Indra-Vāyu. 7.3.2.7. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they both offer. Again at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* they offer; again at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* they offer; again at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* they offer. These two are offered twice each. The subsequent offerings to the dual deities are made once each.

7.3.2.8. He recites the after-verse: "He who seeks to harm us, O Indra and Vāyu... (TS 3.2.10.2n,p), [adding]: "...O Lords of Splendor, let the rival swell up; may I perceive this. 7.3.2.9. He pours the residue from the Pratiprasthātṛ’s cup into the Āditya vessel with the formula, "For the gods, you! Having hastened there, he places this cup down near the Hotṛ and, while running back, says: "Recite for Mitra and Varuṇa! 7.3.2.10. The Adhvaryu takes up the Maitrāvaruṇa draught.

7.3.2.11. With the words, “Thou art taken with a support” (3.2.10b), the Pratiprasthātṛ draws [the cup] back again with the words, “Thou art the one seated in the Ṛta; I take thee for the two protectors of sight, for the two protectors of the will, for the two supervisors of this firm sacrifice” (3.2.10b).
7.3.2.12. As they go out, he says, “Call for the Śrauṣaṭ! and [the Āgnīdhra responds], “Prompt for Mitra and Varuṇa!

7.3.2.13. At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, they both offer. They follow the offering with the mantra, “O Mitra and Varuṇa, whoever seeks to harm us... and, “When the rival is crushed, may I perceive [him].”

7.3.2.14. He pours the residue from the Pratiprasthātṛ’s cup into [his own]. Having run to the Āditya-shālī vessel with the formula, “Thee for the Viśvedevas,” he places this cup down near the Hotṛ and, while running back, says, “Recite the invitatory verse for the Aśvins.

7.3.2.15. The Adhvaryu takes the Āśvina draught. 7.3.2.16. With the formula, “Thou art taken with a support,” the Pratiprasthātṛ receives it in turn, saying, “Thou art heard; I take thee for the two who hear with their ears.”
7.3.2.17. As they go out, he says, “O, cause it to be heard! and “Prompt for the Aśvins! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they both offer the oblation.

7.3.2.18. He follows with the consecratory formula: “O Aśvins, lords of splendor, whoever seeks to harm us, while our rival is crushed, on this day I cast him down; so that I may be conscious as the highest one, even as Indra. 7.3.2.19.
He pours the residue from the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel into his own with the formula, “For all the gods, thee! (TS 3.2.10f).
7.3.2.20. With the verse, “O Viṣṇu of wide stride” (RV 3.2.10g), he covers this [cup] with that very vessel, saying, “This one has shown you the Soma, O Māruta.

7.3.2.21. Having run forward and placed this cup near the *hotṛ*, while running back, he says: “Recite for those being filled! Fill the *camasa* of the *hotṛ* after [the others]; make them bright on both sides; O *acamana*-adhvaryu of the *acchāvāka*, do not fill yours!”

7.3.2.22. Four wood-shavings are prepared: two sprinkled and two unsprinkled; the two sprinkled ones are white, and the two unsprinkled ones are black. 7.3.2.23. (The Adhvaryu covers the *śukra* cup from above with the two white shavings; he supports it with the two black ones. 7.3.2.24.
The Pratiprasthātṛ covers the *manthin* cup from above with the two white shavings; he supports it with the two black ones.
7.3.2.25. “Thou art praised, O bestower of people; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead thee forth,” with these words the *adhvaryu* steps out.

7.3.2.26. “Thou art praised, O bestower of people; may the gods who drink the *manthin* lead thee forth. With these words the *pratiprasthātṛ* [steps out]. [The *adhvaryu* says to the sacrificer: “Turn westward, past the front of the two *havirdhāna* sheds and behind the *āhavanīya* fire. 7.3.2.27. “May the two [cups] join at its navel; may the *brahman* join them together. Thus they join the two cups, saying, “May those two quicken this for me.”

7.3.3.1. “May those two invigorate my dominion; may they join it together and invigorate it for me. May they invigorate my people; may they join them together and invigorate them for me. May they invigorate this nourishment; may they join it together and invigorate it for me. May they invigorate that abundance; may they join it together and invigorate it for me. May they invigorate wealth; may they join it together and invigorate it for me. May they invigorate prosperity; may they join it together and invigorate it for me. May they invigorate offspring; may they join it together and invigorate it for me. May they invigorate cattle; may they join them together and invigorate them for me. May they invigorate the lordship of the herd; may they join it together and invigorate it for me. [May they invigorate] the vital breath.”

"Join together; quicken my out-breath (*apāna*). Join together; quicken my diffused breath (*vyāna*). Join together; quicken my hearing. Join together; quicken my mind. Join together; quicken my speech. (TB 1.1.1–3).

"Generating heroic offspring, go around"—with these words, the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer walk around the Āhavanīya fire on the south side, [the Adhvaryu reciting]: "The bright one with bright luster... (TS 6.4.10.4–5).

7.3.3.3. With the verse, "O you of good offspring, procreating offspring, go around" (6.4.10.5), the Pratiprasthātṛ [offers] with the northern [fire], using the mantra, "The churned [Soma], with the glow of the churned."

7.3.3.4.
