"Those two, coming together from heaven and earth"—with these words, they cause the cup to meet between the sacrificial post and the Āhavanīya fire: "Abiding in the out-breath (*prāṇa*), bestow out-breath upon me; bestow out-breath for the sacrifice; bestow out-breath upon the lord of the sacrifice. Abiding in the in-breath (*apāna*), bestow in-breath upon me; bestow in-breath for the sacrifice; bestow in-breath upon the lord of the sacrifice. Abiding in the diffused breath (*vyāna*), bestow diffused breath upon me; bestow diffused breath for the sacrifice."

Bestowing vital breath (*vyāna*) upon the lord of the sacrifice; you two are sight, bestow sight upon me, bestow sight upon the sacrifice, bestow sight upon the lord of the sacrifice. You two are hearing, bestow hearing upon me, bestow hearing upon the sacrifice, bestow hearing upon the lord of the sacrifice. You two are mind, bestow mind upon me, bestow mind upon the sacrifice, bestow mind upon the lord of the sacrifice. You two are speech, bestow speech upon me, bestow speech upon the sacrifice, bestow speech upon the lord of the sacrifice.
"O gods Śukra and Manthin, bestow offspring upon these animals, upon me, and upon the sacrificer.

(TB 1.1.1.4–5) 7.3.3.5. With the formula, "Thou art the support of the Śukra," the Adhvaryu steps onto the northern altar with his right foot; with the formula, "Thou art the support of the Manthin," the Pratiprasthātṛ steps onto it with his left foot.
7.3.3.6. With the formula, "Śaṇḍa is cast out along with so-and-so," (cf. TB 1.1.1.5) the Adhvaryu throws away a black splinter of wood. He meditates upon whoever the sacrificer hates.
7.3.3.7. Reciting, “The scorpion has been repelled along with him” (cf. ŚB 1.1.1.5), the Pratiprasthātṛ meditates upon whoever the sacrificer hates. 7.3.3.8.

Having touched water, the Adhvaryu throws a white splinter into the Āhavanīya fire with the formula, “O *śukra*, this is your fuel-stick; be kindled by it, svāhā!”; the Pratiprasthātṛ [does the same] with the formula, “O *manthin*, this is your fuel-stick; be kindled by it, svāhā!”

7.3.3.9. He causes the announcement to be made with "O, cause to hear! He says: "At the morning pressing, for Indra, announce the Soma juices that have been set forth—the bright, the stirred, the honey-dripping.
7.3.3.10. They offer at the *vaṣaṭ*-call; they offer at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-call.

7.3.3.11. “He is the first, Saṅkṛti Viśvakarman”—with these words they two offer. “He is the first, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni; he is the first—unto that Indra I offer the pressed [juice]”—with these words the Adhvaryu offers; “Unto that Sūrya I offer the pressed [juice]”—with these words the Pratiprasthātṛ offers. 7.3.3.12. “Let the cup of the Hotṛ go forward,” he says, “let the cup of the Brahman, let the cup of the Udgātṛ, let the cup of the Sacrificer go forward; let the cup-bearers of the Sadasyas and the Ṛtviks go forward. O Camasādhvaryus, having each once drawn more from the Śukra vessel, turn back.”
7.3.3.13. Having carried them around, he pours both into the Āgrayaṇa vessel; he pours both silently into the Hotṛ’s cup. 7.3.3.14.

With the formula, “Having offered thee, I pour thee down when the offering has been made,” he pours the residue into the Hotṛ’s cup; with the formula, “Full of strength for the gods, full of milk for men,” he pours into the sacrificer’s cup without interruption.

7.3.3.15. Then the Pratiprasthātṛ offers this residue of the *manthin* cup. Having made a coal on the northern enclosing-stick (*paridhi*) so that it touches its edge, he says: “This, O Rudra, is your portion, which you have requested; may there be well-being for a year, *svāhā!*” (TS 3.1.9.4f). 7.3.3.16. Having placed the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup in its vessel and taken hold of it, he causes the announcement to be made. He says, “O Śrauṣaṭ!”, and then, “O Praśāstṛ, recite the offering prayer (*yaja*)!”.
7.3.3.17. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. At the subsequent utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.

7.3.3.18. Having handed over the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa and having taken hold of the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! Make the announcement! and then, "O Brahman, recite the offering prayer! (brahman yaja). 7.3.3.19.
At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ* he offers the oblation; at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* he offers the oblation. 7.3.3.20.

Having handed over the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and having taken hold of the cup of the Potṛ, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! Make the announcement! and then, "O Potṛ, recite the offering prayer! (potar yaja).

7.3.3.21. He offers at the *vaṣaṭ*-call; he offers at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-call. 7.3.3.22. Having handed over the cup of the *potṛ* and having taken hold of the cup of the *neṣṭṛ*, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard! and then, "O *neṣṭṛ*, sacrifice! 7.3.3.23. He offers at the *vaṣaṭ*-call; he offers at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-call.

7.3.3.24. Having handed over the cup of the *neṣṭṛ* and having taken hold of the cup of the *āgnīdh*, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! Make the announcement! and "O Āgnīdh, sacrifice! 7.3.3.25. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered; he offers when the second *vaṣaṭ* is uttered. 7.3.3.26. He says, "O Āgnīdh, invite the sacrificer. Those who utter the *vaṣaṭ* invite the sacrificer.
7.3.3.27. The Adhvaryu says, “The Agnīdh has sacrificed. Having come forward, the Hotṛ says, “He has performed the auspicious rite—he who will cause us to drink Soma.
7.3.3.E. Before the *iḍā*, they consume the portions for the dual deities.
7.3.4. [Fragmentary manuscript notes: N1,86a8; T1,253 contains an unidentified portion; the final line of msṬ1, 253–264 has no correspondence with C.]
7.3.4.1. Before the *iḍā*, he holds up the cups for the dual deities (*dvidevatya*) while they are consuming [the soma].

7.3.4.2. For him, the *hotṛ* pushes forward the cup for Indra and Vāyu (*aindravāyava*) without setting it down, saying: "In me is Vasu, Purovasu. 7.3.4.3. The *hotṛ* consumes [his portion]; then the *adhvaryu* consumes [his].

7.3.4.4. With the formula, "O protector of speech, protect my speech," the Hotṛ takes up the cup for Indra and Vāyu twice; he indeed holds out the Aindravāyava vessel to him. 7.3.4.5. Without letting go of it, he pushes it back with the words, "In me is Vasu, Purovasu.
7.3.4.6. The Hotṛ consumes [the draught], and then the Adhvaryu consumes it.
7.3.4.7. Having thrown a fragment of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) into it with the words, "O protector of speech, protect my speech," he places it upon his lap.
7.3.4.8. The Hotṛ takes up the cup belonging to Mitra and Varuṇa for him.
7.3.4.9. Without letting go of it, he pushes it back with the words, "May the Vasu find wealth in me."
7.3.4.10. The Hotṛ consumes [the portion], and then the Adhvaryu consumes it.
7.3.4.11. Having placed [the cup] before his eyes, he says: "O guardian of the eye, protect my eye. 7.3.4.12. He receives a drop of curd into this [cup]; the Hotṛ [receives] the Aśvin vessel for him.
7.3.4.13. Without letting it fall away, he pushes it back with the formula: "In me is wealth, the gathering of wealth. 7.3.4.14.

The Hotṛ consumes it, and then the Adhvaryu consumes it. 7.3.4.15. Having placed it against his two ears and moved it all around, he places it within his mouth with the formula: "Protect my hearing," and having thrown the *dhānās* (parched grains) into it, he places it upon his lap.
7.3.4.16. Handing them over to the Pratiprasthātṛ, he says: "Set these down on the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart.
7.3.4.17. He sets them down; he places the *iḍā* into the *hotṛ*'s cup. 7.3.4.18.
They lift up the intermediate *iḍā* of the sacrificial cakes and take hold of the cakes and the cups.

7.3.4.19. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [the portions] for the *āgnīdhra*. 7.3.4.20. They consume [the portions], they perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*), they set aside a fragment of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) for the *acchāvāka*, and they distribute [the portions].

7.3.4.21. He consumes these sacrificial cakes over which the *iḍā* has been invoked and the cups; before the consumption, they mutter: "Come, consume; enter into me"—and [further]: "For long life, for sound health... for virility, for vigor, for life, for splendor."

7.3.4.22. They replace [the cups] with the formula: "Of the Vasu-rich troop, having Soma as its deity," and they consume [the draught] with the formula: "I, being invited, consume the invited [portion]—which is the knower of thought, belonging to the morning pressing, having the *gāyatrī* metre, drunk by Indra, full of sweetness.

7.3.4.23. They leave behind a remnant for the invitation; they cause the King [Soma] to swell with the formula: "Swell up! Let [the drops] come together to thee from all sides, O thou who art gathered. 7.3.4.24.
With the words "May thy milks be abundant," [they swell] the King for the Kṣatriya; and with the words "Let them come together... do thou hold," [they swell him].
7.3.4.25. The *nārāśaṃsa* cups are set down behind the axle of the southern *havirdhāna* cart.

7.3.4.26. Once the *nārāśaṃsa* cups have been set down, having grasped a fragment of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) with blades of grass, he offers it to the *acchāvāka*, saying: "O *acchāvāka*, speak what is to be spoken by you.
7.3.4.27. The *acchāvāka* begins his recitation with: "Toward Agni for help... (*acchā vo agnim avase*).

7.3.4.28. When he knows: "The Brahmins are calling upon us; call the Brahmins," then he says: "O Brahmin, [invite] whomsoever desires the invitation. The Adhvaryu says this. 7.3.4.29. The Hotṛ responds with a verse: "Recite for the one being filled! O Camasādhvaryu of the Acchāvāka, fill [his cup]; make it bright on both sides! 7.3.4.30. Having taken hold of the Acchāvāka’s cup, he causes the announcement to be made. He says: "O Śrauṣaṭ! and "O Acchāvāka, recite the offering prayer (yaja)!"

7.3.4.31. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered; he offers when the *anuvaṣaṭ* is uttered. 7.3.4.32. The *acchāvāka* consumes [the portion]; his *nārāśaṃsa* cup sits down. 7.3.4.33. As he is sitting down, he issues the command: “O *acchāvāka*, sit down! O *neṣṭṛ*, set down the *pānnejanī* waters following the *acchāvāka* as he sits down! O *āgnīdh*, lead the *acchāvāka*’s [portion]... the Ādityas.”

7.3.4.34. The Neṣṭṛ leads the Patnī together with the *pānnejana* water to the south of the southern pillar of the Sadas, to the north of the western door. The Neṣṭṛ sets down the *pānnejana* water with the formula: "To the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas," and "I set you down as the *pānnejana* for the Viśve Devas; I set you down as the *pānnejana* for the sacrifice. 7.3.4.35. "The Acchāvāka has sat down," says the Āgnīdhra. Then the Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ take up their respective *ṛtu*-cups. 7.3.5. [N1,87a4]

7.3.5.1. "The Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ both receive the *ṛtu*-vessels; they should not follow one another," so says the Brāhmaṇa. The Adhvaryu enters [the *sadas*]. 7.3.5.2. He takes [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee for Madhu... 7.3.5.3. He steps out and says: "O Śrauṣaṭ! Command for the *ṛtu*!"

7.3.5.4. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 7.3.5.5. The Pratiprasthātṛ enters and takes [the draught], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; for Mādhava . . . I take thee. 7.3.5.6. He goes out and says: "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard!"—"Prompt [the Hotṛ] with the season! he says.

7.3.5.7. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 7.3.5.8. The Adhvaryu enters and takes [the draught], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; for the *śukra* (bright one), thee, I offer. 7.3.5.9. He goes out and says: "O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce!"—"Command [the Hotṛ] according to the season! he says.

7.3.5.10. He offers at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*. 7.3.5.11. The Pratiprasthātṛ enters [the Sadas] and takes [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śuci. 7.3.5.12. He goes out and says: "O Śrauṣaṭ!"—"Prompt for the season! he says.
7.3.5.13. He offers the oblation when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.

7.3.5.14. The Adhvaryu enters [the Sadas] and draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Nabhas. 7.3.5.15. He goes out and says: "O, cause it to be heard!"—"Prompt [the Hotṛ] according to the season!"—thus he says.
7.3.5.16. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.

7.3.5.17. The Pratiprasthātṛ enters; he draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Nabhasya. 7.3.5.18. He goes out; he says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard!"—"Command [the Hotṛ] according to the season!"—thus he says.
7.3.5.19. At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, they place [the cup] in the mouth of the *potr̥* priest from the other side.
7.3.5.20. The *adhvaryu* enters [the *sadas*], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the beloved, for nourishment (*iṣ*)," and thus he draws [the cup].
7.3.5.21. He goes out, saying: "O, cause [the *āgnīdhra*] to announce! and says: "Prompt [the *hotr̥*] with the seasons (*ṛtu*)!"

7.3.5.22. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 7.3.5.23. The Pratiprasthātṛ enters; he takes [the draught] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the beloved, for strength. 7.3.5.24. He goes out and says, "O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce!"—"Command [the Hotṛ] by means of the seasons! he says.

7.3.5.25. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 7.3.5.26. The Adhvaryu enters and draws [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the one beloved by *sahas*. 7.3.5.27. He goes out and says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard!"—"Command [the Hotṛ] by means of the seasons! he says.

7.3.5.28. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 7.3.5.29. The Pratiprasthātṛ enters and takes [the cup], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the beloved of... 7.3.5.30. He goes out and says, "O announce! and "Command for the seasons!"
7.3.5.31. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 7.3.5.32. While the two vessels are being turned over, he places his face on the other side; the *adhvaryu* [does so]. 7.3.5.33.
The *pratiprasthātṛ* enters [the enclosure] and takes [the draught], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Tapas."

7.3.5.34. As he steps out, the Adhvaryu says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! Make it heard!"—this is the *ṛtuyāja* of the Adhvaryu. When [the Hotṛ] says, "O Adhvaryu, recite the offering prayer (*yaja*) for Indra . . .", he [the Adhvaryu] says, "O Hotṛ, recite this offering prayer. 7.3.5.35. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the oblation. 7.3.5.36.
The Pratiprasthātṛ enters [the Sadas] and takes [the draught], saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Tapasya."

7.3.5.37. As he steps out, the Adhvaryu, following him as he enters, says: "Stop! Once you have called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, we two shall both offer. Having entered, he draws the thirteenth cup. 7.3.5.38. He draws it with: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art the *saṃsarpa*; I take thee, acceptable to Aṃhaspati. 7.3.5.39. As they step out, the Pratiprasthātṛ says: "'O, cause to hear!'—'Prompt with the season!'"* *Note: The phrase "ṛtunā preṣya" is a call for the Hotṛ to recite the offering formula according to the specific season.*

7.3.5.40. This is the seasonal sacrifice (*ṛtuyāja*) of the householder (*gṛhapati*), when he says: "O Hotṛ, sacrifice for the Gṛhapati!"—[and] "O Hotṛ, sacrifice this [portion] here! He then says: 7.3.5.41. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, they both offer the oblation. 7.3.5.42. With the words, "Spring, Summer," the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite: "May the rains, the autumn, the winter, and the dewy season—those well-established ones—come to us with benevolent minds; may we partake of them while bearing [the sacrifice]; invite them here. The Pratiprasthātṛ should say, "Adhvaryu, invite them!"

7.3.5.43. He pours the residue from the *pratihartṛ*’s cup into the *prasthātṛ*’s cup. 7.3.5.44. Taking that cup from his lap and handing over another vessel, he says: "With this, come for the *aindrāgna* draught. 7.3.5.45. With it, he draws [the cup], saying: "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [juice]. You are taken with a base; I take you, acceptable to Indra and Agni. This is your womb: for Indra and Agni, you!"* [N1,88a2] *yajus* (concluding formula).
7.3.5.46. Having wiped it with the *daśāpavitra* (fringed filter), he sets it down; he mixes it with gold. 7.3.5.E.
Having run [to them], the *adhvaryu* priest causes these officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) to partake [of the draught].
7.3.6.1. Having gone quickly to them, the Adhvaryu causes the officiating priests (ṛtvij) to partake [of the offering] in turn.

With the formula, "May the spring season bestow life upon me," he hands the cup to the Hotṛ; with "May the summer season bestow splendor upon me," to the Potṛ; with "May the rainy season bestow sight upon me," to the Neṣṭṛ; with "May the autumn season bestow hearing upon me," to the Agnīdh; with "May the winter season bestow vigor upon me," to the Brahmanācchaṃsin; and with "May the cool season bestow speech upon me," to the Maitrāvaruṇa;
thus he passes the vessel around, turning its opening toward the other side.

7.3.6.3. Then he addresses the Hotṛ alone with: "May the year bestow seed upon me; may we, together with our entire company, be possessed of offspring. In this same way, he addresses the Potṛ and the Neṣṭṛ, and likewise the Acchāvāka; he shifts the vessel and turns its opening toward the other side.
7.3.6.4. Then he addresses the Hotṛ alone with: "May the year place me within itself; may we, together with our portions, be long-lived."

7.3.6.5. Then the Adhvaryu turns away from the Hotṛ; standing to the east of the Hotṛ with the cup, he says, "May the gods eat the iḍā; may men, the Agnīdh, and the ancestors rejoice after. He continues this until he reaches the end of this sacrificial formula (*yajus*).

7.3.6.6. The Adhvaryu calls out to him, "Śom-sāv-oṃ," and "Śom-sāmo daiva. The Adhvaryu rises, and the Hotṛ begins the *śastra* in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). The Adhvaryu should respond to that in the same manner.

7.3.6.7. With the sixth [verse], "O God, come to the dwelling of the god," the Hotṛ pronounces the *praṇava*; with that very same [verse], the Adhvaryu pronounces the *praṇava*. With the *anuṣṭubh* verse, "Forward to the god Agni," the Hotṛ begins.
7.3.6.8. He sets down two [verses] of that [hymn]; the Adhvaryu likewise sets down two [verses] of this [hymn]. 7.3.6.9.
The Hotṛ pronounces the *praṇava* with the two following [verses] of the combined [hymn]; the Adhvaryu pronounces the *praṇava* with the two following [verses] of the combined [hymn].

7.3.6.10. The response (*pratigara*) is established either on the *anūyāja* or on the *praṇava*. Having said, "This is the *ājya* hymn; O reciter of the hymn (*ukthaśas*), [recite]! he hastens forward. 7.3.6.11. He takes this cup; the goblets are lifted up in succession. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ!";
[the Adhvaryu says], "O reciter of the hymn, offer the oblation of Soma! 7.3.6.12. "O Śrauṣaṭ! he says—"O reciter of the hymn, sacrifice the Soma!"—[and so on].

7.3.6.13. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* he offers, and at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*... they consume the vow-food (*vrata*). 7.3.6.14. They do not offer from the *camasa*s. 7.3.6.15. When the offering has been made but not yet consumed, he pours the residue into the *hotṛ*'s *camasa*, saying: "I remove it," and [adding]: "Full of strength for the gods, full of milk for men. Having set this vessel aside with the words, "The sacrificer [is] superior," they come back.

7.3.6.16. They consume [the Soma] with the formula: "O gods, we consume the Soma drunk by Narāśaṃsa. Then they restore it with: "We, the finders of thought, at the morning pressing, of the Gāyatrī metre, drunk by the Pitṛs, with the honeyed . . . being invited, I consume. Thus, with the call for invitation, they leave remnants of the King (Soma).
7.3.6.17. They cause it to swell with: "Swell up! Let [the milk] come together to thee...
[be] united. 7.3.6.18. With the words "May thy milks be... [they swell it] for a Kṣatriya; with "Let them come together... [place] within" for a Vaiśya.
7.3.6.19. The Nārāśaṃsa goblets are set down.
7.3.6.20. When the Nārāśaṃsa goblets have been set down, he says, "O Unnetṛ!

7.3.7.1. "O Unnetṛ! says the Adhvaryu, "when I take this draught, then pour the *śukra* into the *pūtabhṛt*. With the *śukra* cup, he draws the draught for the Viśve Devās. 7.3.7.2. "Om! O you who support the people, O All-Gods, come hither! You who are worshipped, come to the worshipper's flowing [libation]. You are taken with a base; I take you, acceptable to the Viśve Devās. This is your birthplace; [I place you] for the Viśve Devās. Having wiped it around with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*), he sets it down and mixes it with gold.

7.3.7.3. The Unnetṛ pours the *śukra* cup into the *pūtabhṛt*. 7.3.7.4. Having turned the jar upside down and taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he hastens with the chant, muttering the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the *hiṃ*-singer. He approaches those chanting with the words: "O vital breaths, turn toward me; approach the sacrificer! He turns away from them once they have finished the final verse. 7.3.7.5.
Before the Hotṛ, while reciting the formula "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods," he calls out to him as soon as he reaches this *yajus*; the Hotṛ responds to him.

7.3.7.6. This is the *prauga* *uktha*; before it, the *nivid*s are recited with three feet. Having responded to them by means of the insertion (*nyāsa*), he responds to the triple-verses (*ṛca*) by means of the insertion and the *praṇava*.

7.3.7.7. Having said, "This is the *utvaṃ* [verse]; O reciter of the *uktha*! he runs forward. 7.3.7.8. He takes up these cups for the first-time drinkers. He says, "O Śamitar, announce the cups! 'O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice to Soma!'"
7.3.7.9. He offers at the *vaṣaṭ*-call; he offers at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-call. 7.3.7.10.

They shake the cups but do not offer them. When it has been offered and consumed, he pours the residue into the Hotṛ’s cup with the formula: "I pour thee down, full of strength for the gods, full of milk for men. 7.3.7.11.
Having set aside the sacrificer’s cup without placing it between, they come back with that vessel.

7.3.7.12. "They consume, they consume; O Narāśaṃsa, of thee, O Soma, [is] the divinity," [saying this], the Agnīdh consumes the entire portion. "Being impelled," they perform the *mārjana* purification. [The Adhvaryu says: "Fill up the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa. The Adhvaryu, moving forward, says: "O Unnetṛ, make the Soma flow forth! He takes [the draught] from the *ukthya-sthālī* with the *upaśaya* vessel: "Thou art taken with a support; for the gods, thee, the one who yearns for the gods, for the *ukthas*, for the call (*havam*)."
"I take [the portion] acceptable to Mitra and Varuṇa; this is your womb; for Mitra and Varuṇa, you!"—having wiped it with the *daśāpavitra* strainer, he sets it down and mixes it with gold.
(7.3.7.13) Having touched the vessel with "Thou art the oblation again," and having taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he hastens to the *stotra*.

(7.3.7.14) "Vāyu is the utterer of *hiṅ*," with these words he mutters the introductory formula (*upākaraṇa*). "May the vital breaths return to me; approach the sacrificer"—with these words he waits upon those who are chanting the *stotra*. Recognizing "This is the last [verse]," he turns away. [N1, 89a5]

7.3.7.15. Before the Maitrāvaruṇa's [response], he continues until he reaches the formula: "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods. 7.3.7.16. He calls out to him; he responds in turn. 7.3.7.17. Having said, "O reciter of the *uktha*, this is the *uktha*," he runs forward.
7.3.7.18. He takes up this vessel and lifts it up after the cups have been raised.
7.3.7.19. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ!"—"O reciter of the hymns (ukthaśas), offer the Soma libations!
7.3.7.20. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they make the offering.

7.3.7.21. With the formula, "I pour the residue from the offered into the unoffered," he pours the residue into the Maitrāvaruṇa’s cup; with the formula, "Full of vigor, for the gods... for men," he pours it into the Hotṛ’s cup and that which is shared by the sacrificer. 7.3.7.22. Having set down this vessel with the formula, "Not between," they come back. 7.3.7.23. They consume [the Soma] with the formula, "O God Soma, of the Vasumat-gaṇa... [authorized] by the Agnīdh to consume all. Then they perform the *mārjana* (sprinkling) rite.

7.3.7.24. Having said, "Come, O sacrificer," the Adhvaryu enters the two Havirdhāna sheds and remains there with the formula: "May the Viśve-devās, the Maruts, and Indra [protect] us. 7.3.7.25. He pours half of the *pariṇah* (the enclosing cord) into this second jar, with the verse: "In this [earth], in this benevolent favor... 7.3.7.26. Following that, they bring in the *ekadhana* (the single-vessel water).

7.3.7.27. Having brought down the King (Soma), the Adhvaryu says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, these are your two poles," and "Fill the cups following the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. The Pratiprasthātṛ, moving forward, says, "Fill the cups following the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. Moving forward, he says, "O Unnetṛ, make the Soma swell. He takes [the portion] from the Ukthya vessel with the auxiliary cup.

7.3.8.2. "You are one who has been taken with a support; for the gods you, the god-seeking; for the hymn the hymn-seeking; for Indra I take you, who are pleasing. This is your womb; for Indra you. Having wiped it around with the *daśāpavitra* filter, he sets it down with [the word] "hira... (gold).

7.3.8.3. Having touched the vessel with the words, "Thou art the oblation again," and having taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he hastens forward with the chant. He mutters the introductory formula, "Vāyu is the maker of the *hiṅ*. He waits upon those chanting with the words, "May the vital breaths return to me; come near to the sacrificer. Having recognized [the end of the chant] with the words, "This is the last one," he turns away. 7.3.8.4. He remains in front of the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin*, as far as he can recite this sacrificial formula (*yajus*) beginning with, "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods."

7.3.8.5. He calls out to him; he responds, "This is the hymn, O reciter of hymns," as he says [it]. 7.3.8.6. He takes up this cup; the goblets are not lifted after it. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ!"—"Recite the offering prayer for the Soma juices, O reciter of hymns!
7.3.8.7. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, they offer; when the second *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, they offer.
7.3.8.8. With the words, "Having offered you, I pour you down into the offering," he pours the residue into the cup of the Brāhmaṇacchaṃsin with the formula, "Full of strength for men.
7.3.8.9. Having placed the Hotṛ’s cup and the Sacrificer’s cup so that they do not come between them, they proceed toward this vessel.
7.3.8.10. They consume [the Soma] with the verse, "O divine Soma, [we have drunk] the kinsman of the assembly."
7.3.8.11. "Impelled by the fire that devours all things," they purify themselves.
7.3.8.12. "Fill the cups following the cup of the Acchāvāka," says the Pratiprasthātṛ as he moves forward.

7.3.8.13. "O Unnetṛ, do not let the Soma overflow! With these words, he draws [the Soma] from the Ukthya-vessel using the *upaśaya* cup: "Thou art taken with a support; for the gods thee, the god-loving; for the hymns thee, the hymn-loving; I take thee, acceptable to Indra and Agni. This is thy womb; I take thee, acceptable to Indra and Agni; for Indra and Agni thee. Having wiped it around with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*), he sets it down. He mixes it with gold.
7.3.8.14. If the Soma for Vāyu is left over, he pours it into the *acchāvāka*’s cup; he empties these vessels toward the *āgnīdhra*. 7.3.8.15.
Without touching [the Soma] here with the formula "Thou art the oblation again," he takes the *prastara* and hastens away with the chant.

7.3.8.16. He mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the *hiṅ*-utterer. He attends to those chanting with the formula: "May the vital breaths return to me; come near to the sacrificer! Having recognized [the chant] as "this is the last," he turns back.
7.3.8.17. Before the Acchāvāka [sings], he recites as far as this sacrificial formula (*yajus*): "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods.
7.3.8.18. He calls out to him; he responds in kind. 7.3.8.19. Having said, "O reciter of the *uktha*, this is the *uktha*," he runs forward.
7.3.8.20. He takes up this cup and raises it after the other cups have been lifted.
7.3.8.21. "O Śrāvaya," he says—"O Ukthaśas, recite the offering prayer for the Soma-libations.
7.3.8.22. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they offer; at the subsequent utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they offer.

7.3.8.23. With the formula, "I pour the offering into the non-offering," he pours the residue into the *acchāvāka* cup, saying, "Full of strength for the gods, full of milk for men. He then pours it into the *hotṛ*'s cup and the cup of the sacrificer's wife. 7.3.8.24. Having set down this vessel with the formula, "Not between," they come back. 7.3.8.25. They consume [the soma] with the formula, "O Soma-deity of the Vasu-group. Being impelled by the *agnīdh*, they cleanse themselves.

7.3.8.26. He says: "O Brahman, let the serpent proceed! O Praśāstṛ, let the serpent proceed! O Sadasyas, let the serpent proceed! O Yajamāna, let the serpent proceed! 7.3.8.27. But having stepped out from the serpent-path, the Brahman causes the Yajamāna to recite the *doha* (milking) formula for the *stotra* and *śastra*: "Thou art the *stuta* of the *stuta*. May the *stuta* milk strength for me! May the *stuta* of the *stuta* come to me; may the *śastra* of the *śastra* come to me! Of the *stuta* and the *śastra*, we win the powers of the senses; may we milk forth progeny and food. Thus the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) concludes. 7.4.1. [N1,90a5; T263]
7.4.1.1. Having paid homage to the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, they proceed toward the midday pressing: to the Āhavanīya, the Āgnīdhriya, the Hotriya, and the Mārjālīya. 7.4.1.2.

Having said, "Come, O Sacrificer," the Adhvaryu enters the two *havirdhāna* sheds and pours the *nigrābhya* waters from the *vasatīvarī* waters into the Hotṛ’s cup. 7.4.1.3. Over those waters, he causes the Sacrificer to recite: "You are the *nigrābhya*s; you are heard by the gods, bright, bearers of brightness. Satisfy my life; satisfy me with all my followers; satisfy my followers; let them not thirst for me."
7.4.1.4. He pours out the grains for the King Soma. 7.4.1.5. He gives the entire Soma-turban to the Grāvastut priest.
7.4.1.6. Having tied it around his head with that [turban], he praises the pressing-stones.
7.4.1.7. With the formula, "Thee, belonging to the god...," he takes the pressing-stone (*grāvan*) from the one who is praising.

7.4.1.8. With the formula, "Of these very stones, another one, the Aśvins, take with their hands; thou art a stone, the performer of the sacrifice," he places it facing upwards, having set down the *upāṃśugraha* vessel, and measures out the King Soma over it with the formula, "Thee for Indra! Thee for Indra! 7.4.1.9.
He does so five times with the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) and five times silently.
7.4.1.10. He pours water [into the vessel] with the formula: "You are refreshing, O subduers of Vṛtra. 7.4.1.11.

From the *nigrābhya* waters, the sacrificer [takes a portion], saying: "...may Soma drink. 7.4.1.12. He touches it with the formula: "O Soma, that light of yours which is in heaven... that which is on earth... speak for the giver."
7.4.1.13. With the words, "O two pressing-boards, being firm, do you two become firm," he touches the two crosswise boards...

[and] with the words, "May the sacrifice be well-established. 7.4.1.14. With the words, "The Soma for Indra has increased; O well-born ones, [I have increased] you with my mind," he satisfies the King (Soma) with water, [saying], "Born of Truth, [I satisfy] the Soma for the pressing."

7.4.1.15. With the formula, "Gold is light," he mixes this [Soma] with gold: "With that... (4) light is the waters; with them I mix thee; light are the meters; with them I mix thee; light are Indra and Agni; with them two I mix thee; light are Heaven and Earth; with them two I mix thee; thou art cooked; cooked... for thee, most beloved by Indra and Vāta. Thus they stir it apart. 7.4.1.16.
He pours out the King [Soma]; they press him. 7.4.1.17. They go to the *nigrābha* water.

7.4.1.18. Having taken up the King [Soma] with his joined palms while saying, "From the east, from the west, from the north, from the south," the Adhvaryu causes him to flow over the *nigrābhya* waters while reciting, "O Mother, let these [waters] flow down upon you.
7.4.1.19. This indeed is the approach to the *nigrābha*; they pour [the water] and press [the Soma].
7.4.1.20. They proceed to the *nigrābha*.
7.4.1.21. He pours [the water] in; they press [the Soma]. 7.4.1.22. They go to the *nigrābha* [formula].
7.4.1.23. He pours [the water] in; they press [the Soma].
7.4.1.24. They collect [the Soma] with the fourth [verse].
7.4.1.25. The Unnetṛ brings it into the western jar.
7.4.1.26. From there, they should not bring back the King (Soma).
7.4.1.27. Having poured out the *ekadhana* waters and having dripped them from the *vasatīvarī* waters, the *unnetṛ* pours them in. 7.4.1.28.
Having poured them in with the words, "May birds be yours," they cause the King (Soma) to swell with the words, "May they come together... do thou hold. He pours it in with these words.
7.4.1.29. They press [the Soma].
7.4.1.30. They approach the *nigrābha* water.
7.4.1.31. He pours [the soma] in; they press it. 7.4.1.32. They approach the *nigrābha* water.
7.4.1.33. He pours [the water] in; they press [the Soma]. 7.4.1.34. They approach the *nigrābha* [water].
7.4.1.35. He pours [the water] in; they press [the Soma].
7.4.1.36. They collect [the Soma] with the fourth [verse].
7.4.1.37. The Unnetṛ brings it into the western jar.
7.4.1.38. From there, they should not bring back the King (Soma).
7.4.1.39. Having poured out the *ekadhana* waters themselves, the *unnetṛ* pours them over from the *vasatīvarī* waters and lets them flow down.

7.4.1.40. Having added [the water] with the verse, "May thy vital powers unite," they cause the King (Soma) to swell with the verse, "May they come together... do thou hold. One [priest] presses [the Soma]; they should press it while reciting, "Hither, hither, hither! if it has the *Rathantara* as its *sāman*; "Great, great, great! if it has the *Bṛhat* as its *sāman*; and "Hither, hither, hither! Great, great, great! Hither, hither, hither! if it has both *sāmans*. They press [the Soma] while adding [the water]. 7.4.1.41. They proceed to the *nigrābha* [formula]. 7.4.1.42. They add [the water] and press [the Soma].
7.4.1.43. They approach the *nigrābha* water.
7.4.1.44. He pours it out; they press [the Soma]. 7.4.1.45. They approach the *nigrābha* water.
7.4.1.46. They pour [the water] over; they press [the Soma]. 7.4.1.47. They collect [the Soma] with the fourth [verse].
7.4.1.48. They do not cause it to swell.

7.4.1.49. With the words, "The gods are the pressing-stones," the Pratiprasthātṛ consecrates them: "The drops have spoken to Indra; they have urged Indra forward from the furthest distance, from this common dwelling-place, from the wide mid-air. They have pressed out prosperity; they have pressed out spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). Drive away the demons in the conflict; strike them down! 7.4.1.50.
Now, they perform the *nigrābha* nine times; they collect [the water] three times; they cause [the Soma] to swell twice. 7.4.1.51. They make the King (Soma) well-milked.
7.4.1.52. The Unnetṛ brings that [Soma] from the two *daśāpavitra* strainers into the rear new pitcher (*navakalaśa*).
7.4.1.53. The Udgātṛs drive the oxen forward with their faces turned toward one another and push the dregs away from them. 7.4.1.54. They place the *droṇakalaśa* over these [oxen].
7.4.1.55. They spread out the filter with its fringe pointing northward.
7.4.1.56. He issues the command: "O Śukra, purify yourself continuously; O Sacrificer, we shall draw the cups. 7.4.1.57. They do this.
7.4.1.58. They spread out the filter with its fringes pointing northward.
7.4.1.59. The water flows through the *nigrābhya* waters into the *droṇakalaśa* jar; it is drawn from that jar. 7.4.1.60.
The *nigrābhya* waters flow through the filter; the pure Soma, continuous in the *droṇakalaśa*, flows forth.
7.4.1.61. The cups are drawn with the *śukra* as the first.
7.4.1.62. He takes up the *śukra* vessel; into it he draws [the soma] with [the verse], "This Vena has impelled...
7.4.1.63. He mixes it with gold.
7.4.1.64. He takes up the *manthin* cup; he draws [the juice] into it with the verse, "Him as of old," and mixes it with groats. 7.4.1.65.
From the three streams, he draws the *āgrayaṇa* cup.
7.4.1.66. They cause it to proceed.

7.4.1.67. [He takes] both the *udaka* and the *nigrābhyā*s... (4) ...of the *āgrayaṇa* itself, with the third [verse]: "O gods in heaven, you ten are here"—thus he draws [the *āgrayaṇa*], saying: "From the earth... may you enjoy it; thou art taken with a support (*upayāma*); I take thee, acceptable to the Viśve Devas; thou art the *āgrayaṇa*; entering, do thou protect us... (4) ...he says, "O *āgrayaṇa*."

7.4.1.68. Having turned toward the east and bent his right knee, he utters the *abhihiṅkāra* over the Āgrayaṇa vessel, saying: "Hiṃ hiṃ hīm! Soma purifies himself; Soma purifies himself; Soma purifies himself. He purifies himself for this *brahman*, he purifies himself for this *kṣatra*, he purifies himself for this people (*viś*), he purifies himself for this pressing sacrificer. He purifies himself for food, he purifies himself for strength, he purifies himself for the waters, he purifies himself for the plants, he purifies himself for the trees, he purifies himself for well-being, he purifies himself for spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*).
Brahma . . . [N1,91b1]
7.4.1.69. Having purified these ten times, he cleanses them with the *daśāpavitra* filter using the formula, "This is thy womb; for all the gods thee," and sets them down.
7.4.1.70. He mixes them with gold. 7.4.1.71. With the two *ṛtupātra* vessels, he draws the two *marutvatīya* cups, [reciting]: "O Maruts, you who increase the prosperity... etc. (N1, 91b2).
7.4.1.72. He mixes it with gold. 7.4.1.73. With the verse, "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, the bull for the battle," he mixes the *taraṃ* with gold itself.

7.4.1.74. He takes up the *ukthya* vessel; into it he draws [the soma] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra thee... for the *ṣuṣṇavat* [Indra] thee; I take thee as one who is pleasing."

7.4.1.75. At this time, the Unnetṛ pours out the water-vessel. 7.4.1.76. While the Nigrābhya waters are being held, the sacrificer [recites]: "This is thy womb; for Indra thee, the eager one! Having wiped the two *daśāpavitra* strainers, he sets them down. With the formula "May it not leap away," he consecrates the drops that have fallen.
7.4.2.1. He consecrates the drops that have fallen with the mantra: "May it fall upon me. 7.4.2.2.
He wipes his hands with the *daśāpavitra* filter while reciting: "The drop has fallen. 7.4.2.3. Having touched water and taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he continues the *pavamāna* chant.
7.4.2.4. With the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati thee," he touches the *droṇakalaśa*.
7.4.2.5. With "For Indra thee," [he touches] the *ādhavanīya*; with "For the All-gods thee," the *pūtabhṛt*. 7.4.2.6.
He goes out, while those who follow him touch him from behind.

7.4.2.7. Having gone out, he offers an oblation of the drops (*vipruṣ*) with the formula: "The drop that has fallen from the stalk—that I offer, svāhā! 7.4.2.8. With the verse, "Fulfill the hymn with the *ṛc*," he recites the *anucara* verse; then, having mentally recited the Saptahotṛ formula—"With the *gāyatra* [sāman], the *rathantara*; the *bṛhat* is the path of the *gāyatra*, svāhā!"—he offers a spoon-oblation (*sruvāhuti*). 7.4.2.9. With the words, "Let Speech go first; let it go at the front," they creep back toward the *āstāva*. [He continues: "Going straight to the gods, bestowing glory upon me, vital breaths, cattle, and offspring upon both myself and the sacrificer."
7.4.2.10. With the formula, "Thou art the strewing for the Ṛc and the Sāman," he throws down sacrificial grass (barhis) upon the Āstāva.
7.4.2.11. With the formula, "For the procreation of the couple," while sitting down, he hands the prastara-bunch to the Prastotṛ.
7.4.2.12. He mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the utterer of *hiṃ*; may Soma purify the oblation of breath within me."
7.4.2.13. The Prastotṛ says, "O Brahman, O Praśāstṛ, we shall chant the stotra. The Prastotṛ says, "O divine Brahman, O Praśāstṛ, we shall chant the stotra.
7.4.2.14. The Brahman mutters the *prasava* (impulse) formula: "O divine Savitṛ, he has declared this to you.
7.4.2.15. He pronounces: "Impel it forward and sacrifice; chant in the impulse of the divine Savitṛ; chant accompanied by Indra!"
7.4.2.16. When the *sāman* has been chanted, the *unnetṛ* purifies the King [Soma] toward the east. 7.4.2.17. Over the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, the *adhvaryu* recites the *caturhotṛ* formula. 7.4.2.18.

When he begins the chant with the eighth verse, he then causes [the sacrificer] to recite the *anvāroha*: "You are a well-winged bird, having the *triṣṭubh* as your meter; I take hold of you; carry me safely across."

7.4.2.19. When the praise has been performed, he issues the command: "O Āgnīdh, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; prepare the sacrificial cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, hasten with the curds for the *dadhigharma*; O Hotṛ, recite what is to be recited by you. 7.4.2.20.

Having gone to the Āgnīdhra shed, he pours curds into the offering-spoon across the filter with the verse: "As great as heaven and earth are in their greatness," and with the verse: "And as far as the seven rivers have spread out—unconquered."

7.4.2.21. Saying, "The oblation is cooked," while running toward the middle of the Āhavanīya fire, the Adhvaryu says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard! and "Recite the offering prayer for the *dadhigharma*. 7.4.2.22. At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 7.4.2.23. He offers with the verse: "In me be that great power (*indriya*), in me skill (*dakṣa*), in me wisdom (*kratu*). May the *gharma* rich in heroes be established in me; may the three-fold *gharma* shine forth together with intention, with mind, with sovereign splendor, with light, with sacrifice, and with milk. May we partake of its milking; *svāhā*!"
7.4.2.24. He makes the offering when the second *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.

7.4.2.25. Having approached together, the officiating priests consume this *mahāvīra* vessel with the formula: "May we milk from thee, who art drunk by Indra, the bright, radiant, thousandfold, and glorious one—offspring and nourishment.
7.4.2.26. The Hotṛ consumes first, then the Adhvaryu, then the Brahman, then the Pratiprasthātṛ, then the Āgnīdh, and then the Sacrificer.
7.4.2.27. They consume it with their vital breaths; the consumption is directly perceived by the sacrificer.
7.4.2.28. He proceeds with the midday sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*).
7.4.2.29. Following the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering of these, he offers the oblation of the Caturhotṛ formula.

7.4.2.30. Having set down those [verses] which he recites during the *pavamāna* [laud] upon the *hotṛ*'s [altar], he says as he approaches: "Recite for the cups being filled! Fill the *hotṛ*'s cup! Fill [the cups] from both sides with the *śukra* [juice]! You, the *acchāvāka*'s *camasādhvaryu*, also fill yours!
7.4.2.31. Four wood-shavings (*śakala*) are prepared: two sprinkled and two unsprinkled. 7.4.2.32. The two white ones are the sprinkled; the two black ones are the unsprinkled.

7.4.2.33. The Adhvaryu takes the *śukra* cup; the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the *manthin* cup. 7.4.2.34. He covers them from above with two *śukra*-colored wooden splinters. He removes them with two black splinters, saying: "Thou art praised, O bestower of people; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead thee forth. [He goes out. Saying, "Thou art praised, O bestower of people; may the gods who drink the *manthin* lead thee forth," [he goes out].

7.4.2.35. The Pratiprasthātṛ says to the sacrificer, "Turn westward, past the front of the two *havirdhāna* carts and behind the *āhavanīya* fire," and he [the sacrificer] touches his navel with [the formula]: "...turn. 7.4.2.36. They join together in the established manner; they walk around in the established manner; the performance is in the established manner, starting from the *āśrāvaṇa* call. 7.4.2.37. He says, "Call for the *āśrāvaṇa*! (*āśrāvaya*).

7.4.2.38. "Offer the Soma-draughts for Indra—the *niṣkevalya* portion of the midday pressing, accompanied by the *śukra* and *manthin* vessels, flowing with sweetness; they are spread out! [N1,92b2] 7.4.2.39. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, they offer. 7.4.2.40.
"He is the first, the fashioner, the maker of all" (*sa prathamaḥ saṃkṛtir viśvakarmā*)—with these words, the two of them offer.

7.4.2.41. "He is the first friend... to that Indra I offer the pressed juice" (*sa prathamo mitraḥ... tasmā indrāya sutam ājuhomi*)—with this the *adhvaryu* offers. "To that Sūrya I offer the pressed juice" (*tasmai sūryāya sutam ājuhomi*)—[with this the other offers].

7.4.2.42. He says: "Let the *prasthātṛ* go forward with the cup of the *hotṛ*; let [the cups] of the *brahman*, of the *udgātṛ*, and of the sacrificer go forward; let the *camasādhvaryus* of the officiating priests of the assembly go forward. Having each time drawn more of the *śukra* [Soma], turn back!"

7.4.2.43. He pours [the remnants] into both the Hotṛ’s cup and the Āgrayaṇa vessel silently. When the [Āgrayaṇa] has been offered, he pours the residue from the Hotṛ’s cup into it with the formula: "I pour thee, who hast been offered, into that which has been offered. He pours the residue from the sacrificer’s cup into the Hotṛ’s cup with the formula: "Full of vigor for the gods... for these [deities]. Without interruption, [he pours] from the sacrificer’s cup. 7.4.2.44. Then he offers this residue of the *manthin* cup.

7.4.2.45. Having made the coals touch the front of the northern enclosing stick (*uttaraparidhi*) with the formula, "This is your portion, O Rudra; may there be well-being, *svāhā*," he places it in the vessel. Having taken hold of the *maitrāvaruṇa*-cup, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! and "O Praśāstṛ, recite the offering prayer! 7.4.2.46. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers; at the subsequent utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers. 7.4.2.47. Having lifted up the cup of Varuṇa and having taken hold of the cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ!"

7.4.2.48. "O Brahman, sacrifice! O Potṛ, sacrifice! O Neṣṭṛ, sacrifice! O Acchāvāka, sacrifice! O Āgnīdh, sacrifice!"—thus [he says]. 7.4.2.49. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered; he offers when the second *vaṣaṭ* is uttered. 7.4.2.50. "O Āgnīdh, invite the sacrificer," he says.
7.4.2.51. Those who utter the *vaṣaṭ* call invite the sacrificer.

7.4.2.52. Having come to the *sadas*, the Adhvaryu says, "The Āgnīdhra has sacrificed. The Hotṛ says, "He has performed what is auspicious," [referring to him] as "he who will cause us to drink the Soma.
7.4.2.53. They consume the goblets after the *iḍā* has been invoked.
7.4.2.54. Before the consumption, they recite: "O Soma, enter me with food" (*bhakṣehi mā viśa*), and "For long life, for vitality, for splendor" (*dīrghāyutvāya... āyuṣe varcase*). 7.4.2.55.

As for the *gaṇa* of Rudra, they take it back with the formula: "O divine Soma, [of thee] drunk by Indra, belonging to the midday pressing, having the *triṣṭubh* metre, full of sweetness, being invited, I, invited, consume thee. 7.4.2.56. They leave a remnant for the common invitation (*samupāhava*).
7.4.2.57. They cause the King Soma to swell with the formula: "May those seats and milks come together; do thou take them up. 7.4.2.58.
The Nārāśaṃsa goblets are set down. 7.4.2.59. When the Nārāśaṃsas have been set down, having gone around the north of the Āgnīdhra fire-shed, he offers the Dākṣiṇā oblations.
Having gone around the Āgnīdhra fire-altar by the north, he offers the dakṣiṇā oblations.
7.4.3.1. He ties a piece of gold to a fringed offering-cloth (*daśāhomīya*) and places it into the offering-spoon (*sruk*).
7.4.3.3. From that [fire], he takes four spoonfuls.
7.4.3.4. He offers it into the Gārhapatya fire with the verse, "Upwards that Jātavedas," and with the formula, "To the god Sūrya, svāhā! 7.4.3.5. He takes another four spoonfuls.
7.4.3.6. He offers that [oblation] into the Gārhapatya fire with the verse, "Upwards that Jātavedas... and with the formula, "...the gods carry Sūrya, svāhā. 7.4.3.7.
He takes another fourfold portion [of clarified butter]. 7.4.3.8.
He offers that into the Gārhapatya fire itself with the verse, "The bright face of the gods has risen... and with the formula, "...the eye of the stationary and the moving, svāhā."
7.4.3.9. Having come to the Āgnīdhra fire, he takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter.

7.4.3.10. He offers it in the Āgnīdhra fire with the verse containing the word "lead" (*naya*): "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth... and continues, "...O God, knowing all ways, keep away from us the crooked sin; with that, may we offer the greatest worship—*svāhā*! 7.4.3.11. Having offered a piece of gold with the words, "Go to heaven, fly to the light," he lifts it up.
7.4.3.12. “With form I approach your form,” with these words he approaches the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*); “with vitality your vitality. 7.4.3.13.
“May Tutha, who knows all, distribute you,” with these words he steps between them; “upon the highest firmament. 7.4.3.14.

“This gift of yours, O Agni, comes, distilling Soma,” with these words he causes them to move forward: “Lead them by the path of Mitra, by the path of Ṛta—ye, the bright sacrificial gifts, being led by Savitṛ along the path of the sacrifice; may I today prosper as a Brāhmaṇa. ... [as in 1.4.43k] ... “the southern.”

7.4.3.15. He says, “Who [is there] for the descendant of Atri? To him he leads [the Soma]. 7.4.3.16. “This is the moon; this is the dawn”—in this very manner he leads [it] to the Āgnīdhra; likewise to the Brahman, likewise to the Hotṛ, likewise to the Udgātṛ, likewise to the Adhvaryu, likewise to the Sadasya, likewise to the Prastotṛ, likewise to the Pratiprasthātṛ... (5) ...likewise to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, to the Potṛ, to the Neṣṭṛ, to the Acchāvāka, to the Unnetṛ, to the Dhruvagopa, to the Grāvastut, to the Saṃśrāvayitṛ, to the Subrahmaṇyā, to the Abhigara, to the Pratihartṛ; “Lead it to the last one!”—thus [he says].

7.4.3.17. Having led them with the mantra, "Behold the sun; behold the mid-region" (ŚB 1.4.43.2l), he looks toward the sacrificial hall (*sadas*) with the words, "Exert yourself together with those in the *sadas*" (Ibid.
m). 7.4.3.18. He consecrates these [gifts] with the formula, "Go among the gods as gifts from us" (Ibid. n, o, p), and with the verse, "Sweet is the giver... may that be prepared for us" (Ibid. q).

7.4.3.19. Here he offers the Vaiśvakarman oblations with the verse, “The seers have charged the lord of the sacrifice with sin” (TS 3.2.8.1c). He offers five spoonfuls in the Āgnīdhra fire with the formula, “Thou art the womb of Indra; do not harm me. 7.4.3.20. When the sacrificial gifts have been led forth, he throws the black antelope horn into the Cātvāla pit. 7.4.3.21.
In this very same manner, the Adhvaryu, without making a sound, says to the wife, “Recite for Indra accompanied by the Maruts,” while moving forward.
7.4.3.22. The Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ take up these two cups separately; the Adhvaryu says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! Pronounce the call for Indra accompanied by the Maruts!

7.4.3.23. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation; at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* (if the Hotṛ utters the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*), they both offer. 7.4.3.24. The Pratiprasthātṛ should say, "Adhvaryu, invite [the Hotṛ]!"
7.4.3.25. He pours the residue from the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel into his own.

7.4.3.26. Taking that [residue] from him and handing over his own vessel, he says: "With this, take the third Marutvatīya draught. With that [vessel], he takes it, saying: "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink here... [suyajñā] ... thou art taken with a base; I take thee, acceptable to Indra accompanied by the Maruts. This is thy womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, thee! Having wiped it around with the fringe of the *daśāpavitra*, he sets it down. 7.4.3.27. He mixes it with gold.
7.4.3.28. Having run toward him, the Adhvaryu causes the Hotṛ to partake [of the Soma] with the formula: "May Speech, being pleased, be satisfied with the Soma. 7.4.3.29.
The Adhvaryu turns away from the Hotṛ, moving to the east while holding the cup, with the formula: "Iḍā, the invoker of the gods... may they rejoice. 7.4.3.30.
As soon as he has completed this Yajus, he calls out to him: "O Adhvaryu, recite the Śastra! Oṃ vauṣaṭ!"
7.4.3.31. With the words, “Let us two recite, O divine one,” the Adhvaryu rises up. 7.4.3.32. With the verse beginning, “Like a chariot for aid,” the Hotṛ begins the Anuṣṭubh.
7.4.3.33. He deposits two [verses] of it with the first two feet; likewise, the Adhvaryu deposits two [verses] of it.

7.4.3.34. The Hotṛ pronounces the *praṇava* with both [the preceding and] the following [verses] combined. 7.4.3.35. The Adhvaryu pronounces the *praṇava* with both [the preceding and] the following [verses] combined.
7.4.3.36. The response (*pratigara*) is established; he responds both at the placement and at the *praṇava*.

7.4.3.37. Having said, "This Marutvatīya hymn has been recited; the hymn has been spoken," he moves forward. 7.4.3.38. He takes up this cup; the goblets are lifted up in succession. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ!"—"Recite the offering prayer for the Soma, O Ukthaśas!
7.4.3.39. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* he offers; at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* he offers.
7.4.3.40. He causes the cups to vibrate; they do not offer the oblations.

7.4.3.41. With the formula, “I pour you, who have been offered, into the one who has eaten,” he pours the residue into the Hotṛ’s cup with the words, “Full of vigor for the gods, full of milk for men.
7.4.3.42. Without passing between the sacrificer’s cup, having set down this vessel, they come back.
7.4.3.43. They consume [the portion] of that which has been drunk by Narāśaṃsa.

7.4.3.44. With the words, "O Soma, you are the deity," they replace [the cup]. With the formula, "I consume the sweet [Soma] of the midday pressing, found through inspired thought, having the *triṣṭubh* metre, drunk by the Fathers"—thus they leave behind the invitation for consumption (*samupahāva*).
7.4.3.45. They cause King Soma to swell with the formula, "May there be for you... (7) ...the highest treasures. [N1,93b10]
7.4.3.46. The Nārāśaṃsa cups settle. 7.4.3.47. When the Nārāśaṃsa cups have settled, he issues the formal command.

7.4.4.1. He issues the command: "O pressers, sit around; prepare the mortars; O Āgnīdh, having tied up the *āśīra* mixture, O Pratiprasthātṛ, take heed of the Soma. This is the command from behind the scenes. 7.4.4.2. They do this. 7.4.4.3.
Sitting down around the pressing-skin with the pressing-stones, the pressers proceed with the pressing.
7.4.4.4. Having thrown rice and barley grains to the east of the *śālā* and to the west of the *sadas*, he prepares the mortar and pestle.
7.4.4.5. With the formula, "O gods, look upon our beauty," the Āgnīdhra pours the *āśira* (milk-mixture) into it, saying, "The house prospers through the *āśira* which is rich in food.
7.4.4.6. The Pratiprasthātṛ says to the Āgnīdhra, "Pour the portion for Śaunaka."
7.4.4.7. "O Unnetṛ," says the Adhvaryu while moving forward, "when I draw this cup, then pour the *śukra* into the *pūtabhṛt*.

7.4.4.8. He draws the *māhendra* cup with the *śukra* vessel: with the *gāyatrī* verse, "Great is Indra who by his might... if the *rathantara-sāman* is used; with the *triṣṭubh* verse, "Great is Indra, acting like a man for the sake of the people... if the *bṛhat-sāman* is used; he should draw it with both verses if both *sāmans* are used.
7.4.4.9. "This is your birthplace; for Mahendra you!"—having wiped it around with the *daśāpavitra*, he sets it down.
7.4.4.10. He mixes [the soma] with gold. 7.4.4.11. The Unnetṛ pours the bright [soma] into the Pūtabhṛt vessel.
7.4.4.12. Having taken the Prastara-bunch and the overturned jar, he hastens away with the chant.

7.4.4.13. He mutters the introductory formula: “Vāyu is the utterer of *hiṅ*; may the vital breaths return to me; approach the sacrificer! 7.4.4.14. When the *sāman* has been chanted, he issues the command: “O pressers, press! Make the mortars resound! O Āgnīdh, pour out the milk for mixing! O Pratiprasthātṛ, take note of the boiled Soma-oblation! This is the direct command. 7.4.4.15. They perform this accordingly.

7.4.4.16. "The pressers have pressed with the stones; they sit within the skin for pressing. 7.4.4.17. To the east of the hall, behind that [fire], he throws rice and barley into the mortar and pestle and makes them resound.
7.4.4.18. "He who makes them resound is the one who threshes, the one who strikes back, the one who smites."

7.4.4.19. While the mortars are being struck, the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite: "Whether they have slain or whether they have struck down, and have given the cows to this donor; he prospers in his house, conquering in assembly, prevailing in battle, and victorious over those who do not conquer. 7.4.4.20.
With the words, "May the husband and wife obtain the desirable through the milk-mixture," the Āgnīdhra pours out the milk-mixture (āśir). 7.4.4.21.
With the words, "Unharmed, may wealth leave him," the Pratiprasthātṛ stands near the one praising the Vedas while the cooked oblation for Soma is being prepared.
7.4.4.22. Having recognized, "This is the last," the Adhvaryu turns away from the Hotṛ, who is in front, with the words, "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods. 7.4.4.23.
As long as he has not finished reciting this *yajus*, 7.4.4.24.
he calls out... (7) ...having said, "This is the exclusive *uktha*; the *uktha* has been spoken," he hastens away.
7.4.4.25. He takes this cup while the other cups are being lifted up. 7.4.4.26. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ!"—"O reciter of the hymn (ukthaśas), offer the oblation of Soma!
7.4.4.27. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* he offers; at the subsequent utterance of *vaṣaṭ* he offers.

7.4.4.28. They shake the *camasa*s, but they do not offer [the remnants]. 7.4.4.29. After it has been offered and consumed, he pours the residue into the *hotṛ*’s *camasa*, saying, "I pour thee down for men, full of vigor," and [he pours] the residue into the *hotṛ*’s *camasa*.
7.4.4.30. He does not pass between the sacrificer’s *camasa* and [his own]; having set down this vessel, they come back.
7.4.4.31. "O gods, [partake] of the Soma drunk by Narāśaṃsa," they say as they consume it.
7.4.4.32. "The Agnīdh has given leave for all to consume," they say as they perform the *mārjana* (sprinkling) rite.
7.4.4.33. "Fill up the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa," says the Adhvaryu while moving forward; "O Unnetṛ, make the Soma flow forth."

7.4.4.34. He draws [the Soma] from the *uktha* vessel with the auxiliary cup, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, agreeable to the gods, for the gods, agreeable to the hymns (*uktha*s), for Indra—this is thy birthplace; for Indra, thee! Having wiped it around with the *daśāpavitra* strainer, he sets it down.
7.4.4.35. He mixes it with gold. 7.4.4.36. Having touched the vessel with the formula, "Thou art the oblation again," and having taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he hastens toward the *stotra*.
7.4.4.37. He mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the utterer of *hiṅ*; may the vital breaths return to me; approach the sacrificer. 7.4.4.38.

When he perceives that [the chanters] are about to sing the *stotra*, he turns away from them and stands facing eastward before the Maitrāvaruṇa, [reciting]: "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods. 7.4.4.39.
As soon as he has reached this sacrificial formula (*yajus*), he calls out for the response.
7.4.4.40. He responds to him. 7.4.4.41. He runs toward it. 7.4.4.42. He takes up this cup.
7.4.4.43. They lift up the cups in succession. 7.4.4.44. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! Proclaim!"—"O reciter of the hymns, sacrifice the Soma-libations!
7.4.4.45. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they offer; at the subsequent utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they offer.

7.4.4.46. With the formula, "Having offered thee, I pour thee down into the offering," he pours the residue into the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup with the words, "Full of vigor for men. 7.4.4.47. He does not pass between the *hotṛ*'s cup and the sacrificer’s cup; [he pours from] this vessel... [with the formula], "O Soma, whose deities are the Rudra-hosts. 7.4.4.48. Having been permitted by the *agnīdh* to consume the entire portion, they perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*).

7.4.4.49. Having said, "Come, O sacrificer," the Adhvaryu enters the two Havirdhāna sheds; then, while pouring out the Vasatīvarī waters with the formula, "This is the third pressing of the sages," he pours them into the western jar with the formula, "Without leading [the Soma], O Camasādhvaryus... 7.4.4.50. Following that, they bring in the Ekadhana waters.
7.4.4.51. The Adhvaryu says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, these are your two poles."
7.4.4.52. "Fill the *camasa* of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin after [filling yours]," says the Pratiprasthātṛ as they move forward—"O Unnetṛ, make the Soma swell!
7.4.4.53. "O Śarva! O Aindriya! O Dhurs! O Brahman, creep along! O Praśāstṛ, creep along! O Sadasyas, creep along! O Sacrificer, creep along!"—thus he says. 7.4.4.54.
"Thou art the *stuta* of the *stuta*," [he says] as they creep out; however, the milking (*doha*) of the *stuta* and *śastra* occurs while they have already crept out.

7.4.4.55. The Brahman makes the sacrificer recite: “May we go to the praised [Stotra] with vigor; may we go to the recited [Śastra] from the Śastra. Of the praised and the recited, we win the power of the senses; may we milk forth progeny and nourishment. 7.4.4.56. The midday pressing (mādhyandina-savana) is concluded. 7.5.1. [N1,95a1; M219; T1,274]
7.5.1.1. Having paid homage to the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, they proceed to the third pressing.

7.5.1.2. Having said, "Come, O sacrificer," the Adhvaryu enters the two *havirdhāna* sheds. With the three verses beginning, "O wife of Pīvarya, who has a neck of ghee," he pours in the *āśir* (milk-mixture) into the rear jar, reciting: "May Savitṛ grant us vigor, our sons, and a good invocation; may Indra be our advocate every day. May we press the Soma for Indra without being excluded. May Mitra and Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us greatness. 7.5.1.3. They enclose [the shed] on both sides.

7.5.1.4. He says, “Recite the invitatory verse for the Ādityas,” [specifying them as] “those who are dear, whose abodes are dear, whose vows are dear, the lords of the great dwelling, the overseers of the wide mid-region. 7.5.1.5. With the verse, “Never art thou barren,” he draws the Āditya cup with a four-cornered vessel made of Udumbara wood. It is mixed with the residue of the Agnidra juice. 7.5.1.6. “Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas. Thus [he speaks].

7.5.1.7. With the words, “At no time do you fail to grant,” he pours from the *dadhi* across the *pavitra* filter into both vessels. Having recited, “Thou art taken with a base; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas,” 7.5.1.8.

He recites, “The sacrifice of the gods approaches for their favor,” and after the remnants have been poured out, he says, “O Ādityas, be present and grant us prosperity; may your most abundant knowledge encompass us. Having recited, “Thou art taken with a base; I take thee, acceptable to the Ādityas,” he takes the draught.

7.5.1.9. With the words, “O Vivasvat Āditya,” he causes the *upāṃśusavana* pressing-stone to float upon this [water]. He lifts it up with the formula, “This is your Soma-drink; rejoice in it—[you who are] the satisfier. 7.5.1.10. A drop falls. He mixes [the Soma] with it, saying, “With that which is the divine rain, I mix you. 7.5.1.11. With the verse beginning, “From the ocean,” they lift it up from below by means of that very pressing-stone, saying, “O Prajāpati, release the skin-bag from the intermediate space.”
7.5.1.12. "Bring him along, O presser," he says.
7.5.1.13. He causes him to flow along into another jar. 7.5.1.14. Having taken the plants and covered themselves with a black antelope skin, they both go out.

7.5.1.15. "O, cause it to be heard!"—thus he says; "Prompt [the offering] for the Ādityas, who are dear, whose abodes are dear, whose vows are dear, who are the lords of the great light, the overseers of the wide mid-region.
When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, having thrown the plants into the fire, they offer the Āditya cup while looking elsewhere, saying: "May Mitra protect me with his laws."

7.5.1.16. When turning away, they both consecrate [the act] with the mantra: "May Varuṇa protect me with the *vidhṛti*, Aryaman with the *mitras*, Jitvan with Bhaga, and Kāla with Aṃśa. Having entered, he draws the Āgrayaṇa cup from four streams.
7.5.1.17. They cause it to be sent forth.

7.5.1.18. They spread out the fringe of the *daśāpavitra* over the *udaṅka*, the *āgrayaṇa* vessel, the *ādityasthālī*, and the *ādityapātra*. Into the eastern jar he draws [the Soma] with the formula: “O gods who are eleven in heaven,” “on earth indeed eleven—enjoy! You are taken with a support; for the gods, I take you who are dear; you are the *āgrayaṇa*; through you, O Indra, may we be carried by power and vigor.”

7.5.1.19. Having turned eastward and bent his right knee, he utters the *hiṅ* over the Āgrayaṇa vessel: "Hiṃ hiṃ hiṃ. ... Soma purifies himself; Soma purifies himself for this priesthood (*brahman*), he purifies himself for this nobility (*kṣatra*), he purifies himself for this people (*viś*), he purifies himself for this pressing sacrificer.

"He purifies from the waters; he purifies from the plants; he purifies from the trees; he purifies from heaven and earth; he purifies for well-being; he purifies for spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*)"—thus twelve times.
Having wiped it around with the *daśāpavitra* filter using the formula, "This is thy birthplace; for all the gods thee," he sets it down. He mixes it with gold.
7.5.1.22. He consecrates the drops that have fallen with the mantra: "May they fall unto me. 7.5.2 [N1,95b8; M221; T1,267] Cf. 7.4.2. 7.5.2.1.
He consecrates the drops that have fallen with the mantra: "May they fall unto me"; he wipes his hands with the *daśāpavitra* filter while reciting: "The drop has fallen."

7.5.2.2. Having touched water and taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he connects the *pavamāna* chant. 7.5.2.3. He touches the *āgrayaṇa* vessel with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati thee!"; the *ādhavanīya* vessel with, "For Indra thee!"; and the *pūtabhṛt* vessel with, "For all the gods thee! Having stepped out, those who follow him take hold of him. Having stepped out, he offers the oblation of drops (*vipruṣ*) with the formula: "That drop of thine which is honeyed and full of power, I offer it to Indra, svāhā!"

7.5.2.5. Having mentally recited the *anucara* verse, "With the *ṛc*, fulfill the *stoma*," and the *saptahotṛ* formula, "With the *gāyatra* [chant], the *rathantara*; on the path of the *gāyatra*, svāhā!," he offers a spoonful of oblation.
7.5.2.6. With the words, "Let Speech go first; let it go at the front," they creep toward the *āstāva*. [They proceed] straight forward, saying, "And upon the sacrificer. 7.5.2.7.
With the words, "Thou art the under-layer for the *ṛc* and the *sāman*," he strews sacrificial grass (*barhis*) in the *āstāva*.
7.5.2.8. Saying, "For the procreation of the pair," he hands the *prastara* grass-bundle to the *prastotr* while sitting down.

7.5.2.9. Saying, "Vāyu is the *hiṅ*-singer," he mutters the introductory formula: "May Soma purify the oblation of breath within me. 7.5.2.10. The *prastotr* says, "O Brahman, O Praśāstṛ, we shall chant the hymn."
7.5.2.11. "O God Savitṛ, he has declared this to you"—with these words, the Brahman mutters the *prasava* (impulse).

7.5.2.12. He proclaims: "Praise that! Praise in the impulse of the god Savitṛ; praise accompanied by Indra! 7.5.2.13. When the *sāman* has been chanted, the Unnetṛ purifies the King (Soma) facing eastward.

7.5.2.14. The Adhvaryu recites the Pañcahotṛ formula over the *pūtabhṛt* vessel. 7.5.2.15. When he begins the chant with the ninth verse, he then causes [the sacrificer] to recite the *anvāroha*: "Thou art a friend, having the Jagatī as thy metre; I take hold of thee. Carry me safely across. 7.5.2.16. When the chant has been performed, he issues the direction: "O Āgnīdh, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; prepare the sacrificial cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, hold the dialogue regarding the animal sacrifice. He then proceeds with the animal sacrifice.
7.5.2.17. He offers the oblation of the Pañcahotṛ twice for each of the quarters.

7.5.2.18. He recites the five *pavamāna* verses. Having performed the animal sacrifice ending with the *iḍā* in this manner, he proceeds with the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) belonging to the third pressing.

7.5.2.19. Having placed those [cakes] down near the *hotṛ*, while running forward, he says: "Recite for the cups being filled; fill the *camasa* of the *hotṛ* after [the others]; make them strong and accompanied by blessings."

7.5.2.20. Having taken hold of the *hotṛ*’s cup, he says, “O, cause to hear! and [the *āgnīdhra*] says, “Do thou cause to hear! 7.5.2.21. He gives the command for the third pressing: “For Indra, announce the pressed Soma-juices—those accompanied by *Ṛbhu*, *Vibhvan*, *Prabhu*, *Vāja*, *Savitṛ*, *Bṛhaspati*, and the *Viśve Devās*; those that are strong, accompanied by the blessing, and set forth. 7.5.2.22. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* they offer; at the subsequent utterance of *vaṣaṭ* they offer, saying: “*Svāhā* to the flying falcon!”

7.5.2.23. He consecrates the *hotṛ*’s cup that has been offered with the formula: “*Vaṣaṭ*! Homage to the one who has spontaneously approved! 7.5.2.24. [He consecrates the cup] at the second *vaṣaṭ*-call with: “May the *hotṛ*s be satisfied with the honey and the ghee. 7.5.2.25. He says: “Let the *hotṛ*’s cup go forward;

let the *brahman*’s, the *udgātṛ*’s, and the *yajamāna*’s go forward; let the cups of the *sadasyas* and the officiating priests go forward. O *camasādhvaryus*, having each once drawn the portion accompanied by the blessing, turn back.”

7.5.2.26. When the *āśrāvaṇa* and *pratyāśrāvaṇa* have been performed, they set down the vessels of the Hotṛs, having taken hold of the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa. He causes the announcement to be made, saying, "O, cause the announcement to be made! and says, "O Praśāstṛ, recite the offering prayer (*yaja*). 7.5.2.27.
At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering, saying: "To the Support of the Law (*dharma*), Svāhā! 7.5.2.28.

After the offerings have been made, he follows them with the consecratory formulas (*anumantraṇa*): "Vaṣaṭ! Homage to the self-praised one; to the enclosing-stick that spreads the people, Svāhā!—Svarga-vāṭ, Svāhā! Vaṭ! Homage to the self-praised one! To the Hotṛ who possesses manly power, to the lower part of the clarified butter."
7.5.2.29. He says, "O Agnīdh, invite the sacrificer. Those who utter the *vaṣaṭ* call invite the sacrificer.
7.5.2.30. The Adhvaryu says, "The Agnīdh has sacrificed. Having come forward, the Hotṛ says, "He has performed what is auspicious—he who will cause us to drink Soma.
7.5.2.31. He consumes the cups for which the *iḍā* has been invoked, saying, "Consume; enter me. Before the consumption, they mutter, "For long life—for life and luster..."
7.5.2.32. "Of the host that has Āditya as its leader, O Soma, you are the deity"—thus those who know the sacred thought respond as they replace [the cups].
7.5.2.33. "Of the third pressing, which has the *jagatī* meter, which is drunk by Indra, which is full of sweetness, and which has been invited—I, being invited, partake.
7.5.2.34. They leave a remnant for the invitation; they cause King Soma to swell with the formula, "Swell up! Let it come together unto thee," and they sit down twice with this same verse.
7.5.2.35. After the *nārāśaṃsa* verses have been recited for those who have consumed their portions, they scatter the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) upon the domestic fire-places (*aupāsana*).
They scatter the sacrificial cakes upon the domestic fire-places with the formula: "O Fathers, rejoice here according to your respective shares in each of your cups. (Cf. 7.3.6.9)

7.5.3.2. “Recite for the god Savitṛ,” says the Adhvaryu as he hastens; with the Antaryāma vessel, he draws the Sāvitra cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel, saying: “The lovely [wealth], today... may we win. You are taken with a base; I offer you, acceptable to the god Savitṛ. 7.5.3.3. He goes out. 7.5.3.4.
“O, cause [the Agnīdhra] to announce! he says. “Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the god Savitṛ.”
7.5.3.5. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. He does not perform the *anuvaṣaṭ* for this [offering]. 7.5.3.6.

With that residue, using the *savitṛ*-cup, he draws the *vaiśvadeva* portion from the jar: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art a good refuge, well-established, [thou art] in the great skill. Homage to the All-gods! I take thee, who art pleasing, for the All-gods. This is thy womb; for the All-gods thee! Having wiped it around with the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*), he sets it down. 7.5.3.7. He mixes it with gold.
7.5.3.8. Having wiped his hands together, he runs forward.
7.5.3.9. There is no *prastara* [grass-bundle] here.
7.5.3.10. The Adhvaryu turns away; standing to the east of the Hotṛ, [he recites]: "The *iḍā*, the invoker of the gods."

7.5.3.11. As soon as he reaches the end of this *yajus*, he calls out to him. 7.5.3.12. [The Hotṛ says: "O Adhvaryu, may you recite the *śastra*! [The Adhvaryu replies: "We shall recite, O divine one! With these words, the Adhvaryu stands up.
7.5.3.13. The Hotṛ begins the *anuṣṭubh* verse: "That of Savitṛ we choose."

7.5.3.14. He places [the two stones] upon it twice with the first two feet; likewise he places them twice... 7.5.3.15. Having joined [the two stones] together, the Hotṛ pronounces the *praṇava* with the latter two [feet].
7.5.3.16. Having joined [the two stones] together, the Adhvaryu pronounces the *praṇava* with the latter two [feet].
7.5.3.17. The response (*pratigara*) is established. 7.5.3.18.

When he recognizes [the verse], "With one and with ten, O self-existent one," he then covers the vessels for the sake of releasing them. When he recognizes [the verse], "I have exalted Heaven and Earth, who increase the *ṛta* through sacrifices," 7.5.3.19.
he then responds to the four verses of the *Abhiṣṭhūrīya* chant: "We rejoice, O divine one! We rejoice, O divine one! We rejoice, O divine one! And we rejoice, O divine one!"

7.5.3.20. Having responded to the *nivid* with the *nyāsa*, he responds to the *niṣṭhurīya* verse following a single *ṛc* with the words: "That desirable gift of Savitṛ today... [N1,97a4]. 7.5.3.21. The response (*pratigara*) for this is established both at the *nyāsa* and at the *praṇava*. Having responded, and having said, "This is the great *vaiśvadeva* hymn; the hymn is uttered for Indra," he hastens forward. 7.5.3.22. He takes up this cup; the *camasa*s are lifted up after him.
7.5.3.23. He says, "O, cause [the sacrificer] to hear!"—"O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice the *soma*!
7.5.3.24. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering; at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, he makes the offering.
7.5.3.25. They shake the cups along, but they do not offer.
7.5.3.26. With the formula, "Having offered thee, while thou art being consumed, I pour thee down," he pours the residue into the Hotṛ’s cup with the words, "Full of strength for men.
7.5.3.27. Having set aside the sacrificer's cup with the formula, "Not between," they come back with this vessel.
7.5.3.28. They consume it with the formula, "O God Soma, of thee drunk by Narāśaṃsa..."
7.5.3.29. "Born from the fire that consumes all things," they say as they perform the *mārjana* (sprinkling purification). Having been purified, the *camasa* cups are set down.
7.5.3.30. He issues the command: "O Āgnīdhra, prepare the *śālā*-fires! and "O Pratiprasthātṛ, come with the *saumya* and the clarified butter (*ghṛta*). 7.5.3.31.
He performs the secondary sacrifice (*pariyajana*) of the *saumya* cup with clarified butter.
7.5.3.32. He should take four spoonfuls of clarified butter.
7.5.3.33. He says, "O, cause [the Agnīdhra] to announce," and having uttered "Agni" in a low voice, he says, "Sacrifice with the clarified butter.
7.5.3.34. Having uttered the *vaṣaṭ* call loudly, he makes the offering.
7.5.3.35. He takes [the portion] of the Soma-oblation, having spread a base-layer [of ghee] and poured a libation over it.
7.5.3.36. He says, "O, cause [him] to hear! and "Recite the offering-verse for the Soma-oblation!
7.5.3.37. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the oblation.
7.5.3.38. One should take four spoonfuls of clarified butter alone.
7.5.3.39. He says, "O, cause [the offering] to be heard," and having uttered "Viṣṇu" in a low voice, he says, "Sacrifice with clarified butter alone.
7.5.3.40. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered loudly, he makes the oblation.

7.5.3.41. Having filled [the cup] with clarified butter using the verse, “That mind of mine which has gone away,” and having made it overflow, he gazes at the Soma with the verse, “Or that which of mine has not come back, O King, may we maintain that [in us].

7.5.3.42. He sends this [cup] to the Udgātṛs. 7.5.3.43. Having taken nine portions with the *pracaraṇī* spoon, he issues the command: “O Agnīdh, light the fire-sticks; O Pratiprasthātṛ, take the Pātnīvata portion from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Upāṃśu vessel; sit down.”
7.5.3.44. They do this. 7.5.3.45. The Agnīdh kindles the śālākā-sticks.
7.5.3.46. The Pratiprasthātṛ draws the portion for the Pātnīvata from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the upāṃśu-vessel, saying: "iṣadasī."

7.5.3.47. They do this. 7.5.3.48. The Āgnīdhra kindles the śālākā sticks. [The Adhvaryu says: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, draw the Pātnīvata cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Upāṃśu cup; sit down. 7.5.3.49. They do this.

7.5.3.50. The Āgnīdhra kindles a firebrand. 7.5.3.51. The Pratiprasthātṛ draws the Pātnīvata portion from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Upāṃśu cup, [saying]: "Thou art taken with a support; I take the draught belonging to Indra accompanied by the wives, which has been pressed by Bṛhaspati and is endowed with power. 7.5.3.52. Having drawn it, he pours it as an oblation; he does not set it down.

7.5.3.53. Having run [to the Āgnīdhra fire], standing facing west or sitting, he sprinkles the Dhiṣṇiya hearths.
