With the formula, “Thou art pervasive, the carrier,” he first makes an offering upon the wooden splinter placed on the Āgnīdhra Dhiṣṇiya with the words, “With the [oblation] for Rudra—do not harm me, svāhā!”

7.5.3.54. With the formula, “Thou art Vahni, the carrier of oblations,” [he places the fire] on the *dhiṣṇiya* of the Hotṛ; with “Thou art Aśvattha, the wise one,” on that of the Maitrāvaruṇa; with “Thou art Tutha, the all-knowing,” on that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; with “Thou art Uśij, the sage,” on that of the Potṛ; with “Thou art Aṅghāri, the descendant of Bambhāri,” on that of the Neṣṭṛ; with “Thou art Avasyu, the worshipper,” on that of the Acchāvāka; and with “Thou art Śundhyū, the purifier,” on the Mārjālīya. With the formula, “With thy fierce aspect, O Agni, protect me; carry me across; do not harm me,” he applies the term “aspect” (*anīka*) to all of them.

7.5.3.55. With the words, "Seven are thy kindling-sticks, O Agni, seven thy tongues," he makes an offering over the ninth [oblation] that has reached the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, using the *śālāka* [wooden spoon], with the formula: "The seven seers, with ghee, svāhā! 7.5.3.56. Having taken [the vessel] with the words, "I am from above, I am from below," and having placed it within the *barhis* grass, he anoints that cup with the *pracaraṇī* [ladle] while reciting: "I have dispelled the darkness with light—of my equals. 7.5.3.57. Having touched water, he takes this [cup] from the *pratiprasthātṛ*. The *āgnīdh* says, "O, cause [the announcement] to be heard! [and] "Recite the offering prayer for the *pātnīvata* [cup]."

7.5.3.58. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers with the formula, “O Agni, accompanied by the wives, drink [the Soma], *svāhā*,” while this is whispered (*upāṃśu*). The *agnīdh* pronounces the secondary *vaṣaṭ* for this offering. 7.5.3.59. Having run back, the *adhvaryu* causes the *agnīdh* to partake of that [Soma] with the formula, “May Speech, being pleased, be satisfied with the Soma.
7.5.3.E. Rising, he issues the command.

7.5.4.1. Rising, he issues the command: "O Agnīdh, sit upon the lap of the Neṣṭṛ! O Neṣṭṛ, lead up the wife and have her look at the Udgātṛ! Cause the waters to flow forth! Fill the cups following the Hotṛ’s cup! O Unnetṛ, do not leave any Soma remaining! If it is an Agniṣṭoma, this is the final [command]: "Make it radiant! If it is an Ukthya or an Atirātra, having washed this vessel, he says: "Pour the water into it! Come, O Sacrificer!"

7.5.4.2. Having spoken thus, the Adhvaryu enters the two *havirdhāna* sheds and gazes at the *dhruva* vessel, saying: "Thou art being; bestow being upon me. He gazes at the mouth [of the vessel], saying: "Thou art the mouth; may I become the mouth. Thou art life; grant me life. 7.5.4.3. Having touched water and taken the *prastara* grass-bundle, he hastens toward the place where the sacrifice is performed while reciting the *stotra*, carrying water while remaining covered by his knees. 7.5.4.4. He mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the *hiṅ*-singer," and then: "O vital breaths, return to me; approach the sacrificer."
7.5.4.5. When the *sāman* has been chanted, the *adhvaryu* recites the *saptahotṛ* formula.

7.5.4.6. The *neṣṭṛ* leads the wife forward together with the water for washing. 7.5.4.7. For her, having uncovered her right thigh while [the *udgātṛ*] chants, "Of thee, the all-pervading one... and saying, "Let the waters flow forth," he causes her to count the *nidhana* three times, [while the *adhvaryu* recites]: "...of thee, O Agni, who art rich in rain, may I partake."

7.5.4.8. With the words, “The sacrifice has gone to the gods,” he consecrates the water that has been poured out: “O divine waters, the sacrifice has stood in the ocean for the gods; it has followed the Gandharva of the sacrifice. In the footprint of the wind, O *iḍā*s, being praised, watch over the sacrifice. 7.5.4.9. He waits upon those who are chanting, thinking, “This is the last verse. Having recognized this, he turns away from the front of the *hotṛ* priest. As soon as he reaches the end of this *yajus*, “*iḍā* is the invoker of the gods,” he calls out to him. 7.5.4.10. He responds, thus moistening this *āgnimāruta* hymn.
7.5.4.11. When he recognizes [the verse], "O Waters, you are indeed sources of bliss," then he causes the greatest amount of water to flow out.
7.5.4.12. When he recognizes [the verse], "Sweet-making and honeyed is this one," then he responds to the four verses containing the *ubhayatomada* (double-refrain) until the *vyāhāva* (call).
7.5.4.13. The response (*pratigara*) is established.
7.5.4.14. And in the *nyāsa* as well as in the *praṇava*, he responds with this *uktha*.
7.5.4.15. Having said, "The *uktha* is for Indra in speech," he runs forward. 7.5.4.16. He takes up this cup; the *camasa*s are lifted up after him.

Having said, "Come, O sacrificer," the Adhvaryu enters the two *havirdhāna* sheds. He encloses the *dhruva* post with the formula, "I enclose thee for Heaven and Earth," and he supports it with the *hotṛ*'s cup, saying, "I support thee with the intermediate space.

He causes it to move forward with, "May all the gods, common to all men, cause thee to move forward," and [concludes] with, "In heaven we establish the gods, in the intermediate space the birds, on earth the earthly beings; with the firm oblation, we lead the firm Soma."

7.5.4.19. He pours the *dhruva* cup into the *hotṛ*’s goblet with [the formulas]: for a Vaiśya, “So that all this world may be free from disease and well-disposed toward us”; for a Rājanya, “So that Indra may make all these subjects ours alone and unanimous”; for a Brāhmaṇa, “So that all these quarters may be ours alone. 7.5.4.20. He pours it out together with everything; thus he makes the Brāhmaṇa the one whose mouth is the *yajus*.
7.5.4.21. He recites the *daśahotṛ* formula over this [goblet].
7.5.4.22. Having taken hold of the *hotṛ*’s cup, he causes the announcement to be made; he says, “O, cause it to be heard!”—“O reciter of the *uktha*, offer the *soma*s!
7.5.4.23. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ* they make the offering; at the subsequent utterance of *vaṣaṭ* they make the offering. 7.5.4.24. He makes the offering together with the *hotṛ*’s offering.

7.5.4.25. They come and consume [the Soma], saying: "Of the troop belonging to the Ādityas, O god Soma. 7.5.4.26. Having been permitted by the Agnīdh to consume all [the Soma], they perform the *mārjana* (sprinkling purification) rite.
7.5.4.27. Saying, "O Lord of Bay Steeds, impel my limbs," they touch themselves; then, saying, "O Aśvins, restore sight to my eyes," they [touch their eyes].

7.5.4.28. He issues the command: “O Āgnīdhra, bring the embers for the supplementary offerings (aupayaja)! O Upayaṣṭṛ, sit down! O Brahman, we shall set forth; having placed a fuel-stick on the fire, O Āgnīdhra, cleanse the fire once each time. 7.5.4.29.
Having brought the embers for the supplementary offerings from the Āgnīdhra hearth, the Āgnīdhra pours them out upon the Hotṛ’s Dhiṣṇya altar.
7.5.4.30. The Upayaṣṭṛ sits down with a ball of molasses.
7.5.4.31. He performs the after-offerings (*anūyāja*) with speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*).
7.5.4.32. Having poured the speckled butter from the *upabhṛt* into the *juhū*, 7.5.4.33.
he says, "O Śrauṣaṭ! and then, "Prompt the gods! Prompt from here! Prompt, prompt!"—with these words he performs the after-offerings.
7.5.4.34. When the Maitrāvaruṇa priest offers the *upayaj* oblations, he says: "Go to the ocean, svāhā! 7.5.4.35.

Without cutting off a piece of the rectum and without turning it over, he finally offers the entire rectum with the formula: "Go to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! 7.5.4.36. With the formula, "Thee for the waters... (and so forth), he wipes his hand on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), saying: "Bestow breath, mind, and heart upon me."
7.5.4.37. The *upayaṣṭṛ* makes the sacrificer recite: "May I attain my own body, my son, and my grandson. 7.5.4.38.

Having performed the *anūyāja* offerings and having walked around, he anoints the *svaru* with the formula: "The controller for the controller. With the words, "Here is stability," he places it in the *sruk* ladle; with the words, "Here is support, here is self-support. 7.5.4.39–40.
With the formula, "May your smoke go to heaven," he offers it, saying: "May your flame go to the intermediate space; fill the earth with ashes, *svāhā*!"
7.5.4.41. Following the *svaru*, he offers the oblation of the Saptahotṛ with [the formula]: "That which he proclaims for the sacrifice of the one worthy of sacrifice at the *stotra*...
7.5.4.42. Having returned, he separates the two offering-spoons (*srucau*) with the two *vājavatī* verses.
7.5.4.43. With the *śaṃyu*-formula, he scatters the *prastara* and the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*).
7.5.4.E. The Unnetṛ should take the Hāriyojana cup.
The Unnetṛ should take the Hāriyojana cup.

7.5.5.2. Whatever remains of the King [Soma] in the Āgrayaṇa vessel, he pours that into the Droṇakalaśa, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art the tawny one, the one who brings joy to the tawny ones; for the recited hymn, I take the draught accompanied by the tawny ones. 7.5.5.3.
With the words, "Ye two tawny ones, the parched grains for the tawny ones," he scatters the parched grains therein.
7.5.5.4. Having placed [the vessel] upon his head, he goes out.
7.5.5.5. Saying, “Recite the invitatory verse for the *dhānās* and *soma*,” he steps forward and causes the announcement to be made with “O, cause it to be heard!
7.5.5.6. He says, “Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the *adhāna-soma*s that have been set forth.
7.5.5.7. At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering with “The *soma*s, together, for Indra, *svāhā!*”; at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering.

7.5.5.8. Having run after him, the Unnetṛ causes the Hotṛ to consume [the remnant] with the formula: “Vāṭ! May she, being pleased, satisfy herself on the Soma. 7.5.5.9. They seek permission to consume from the Unnetṛ.
7.5.5.10. The roasted grains (dhānā) that remain, they crush; whichever he takes hold of, he places them in both hands.

7.5.5.11. Those [cups] which are on his right, he presses together mentally; while they are being consumed, he says: "O divine Soma, of thee who hast the *iṣṭayajus*, whose *stotra* has been praised, whose *śastra* has been recited, who art drunk by Indra, who art full of honey, who art invited—I, being invited, consume thee.
7.5.5.12. With the words, "May we two be filled with breath! Fill yourselves! they pour these [cups] down upon the high altar (*uttaravedi*), saying, "With offspring and with wealth!
7.5.5.13. With those [cups] which are on his left, they go out.
7.5.5.14. At the *mārjālīya* fire-altar, they perform the *prācīnāvīta* ritual (wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder).

7.5.5.15. Having spread out that sacrificial grass (*barhis*), he sprinkles it three times with a handful of grass, saying: "May the fathers cleanse themselves"; "May the grandfathers cleanse themselves; may the great-grandfathers cleanse themselves. 7.5.5.16. He offers three heaps [of food], saying: "This for you, O father," and: "Those whom you follow and those who follow you, those who are around you and those who are with you—[this is] the *svadhā*, the dwelling place of *svadhā*."

7.5.5.17. With the words, “This for you, O Father, with the second [offering], the dwelling-place,” and “This for you...,” and “This for you, O Grandfathers and Great-grandfathers,” he should eat as much as he desires from what remains. Having said, “O Fathers, rejoice here according to your respective portions,” he turns toward the north and sits until the fire is extinguished.
7.5.5.18. With the verse, “We [look upon] you, O fair-to-behold one,” he gazes at the Āhavanīya fire, saying, “O Maghavan, may we gladden you. (cf. Ṛgveda 1.8.5c, with variation).
7.5.5.19. With the verse, "Now forth with the full-seated chariot," he worships from that very place with the verse, "Praised, O Indra, you go according to your will;
the two bay steeds [follow]. 7.5.5.20. With the verse, "They have eaten, they have rejoiced," he worships the Gārhapatya fire;

with the verse, "The two dear bay steeds [have come] to you. 7.5.5.21. With the verse, "That very chariot, O powerful ones," he stands upon the Mārjālīya mound, [reciting]: "The vessel that finds cattle, which Indra knows as full for the sake of the Hāryojana; O Indra, those two bay steeds of yours [have reached] the knees."
7.5.5.22. He turns around [the vessel] with the words, “The Soma-loving ancestors have rejoiced.

7.5.5.23. Whatever remains in the vessel, he smells at that three times, [reciting]: “May those kinsmen who are of one mind, living... 7.5.5.24. With the words, “May the ancestors cleanse themselves,” he sprinkles [the water] three times with a handful of grass, [saying]: “May the grandfathers cleanse themselves; may the great-grandfathers cleanse themselves.”

7.5.5.25. He cuts off the fringe, saying: "This for you, O Fathers... [He does not cut the hair, for the Brāhmaṇa says, "He should not cut the hair," and thus he cuts only the fringe. 7.5.5.26. He pays reverence with: "The Fathers have eaten;
the Fathers have rejoiced... 7.5.5.27. With: "Go forth, O Soma-loving Fathers, by those ancient paths... and: "Then go to the benevolent Fathers, who rejoice in the company of Yama."
7.5.5.28. With the three verses beginning, “We invoke the mind,” he invokes the mind; and with the verse, “May we be united with the Nārāśaṃsa troop. 7.5.5.29.

With the verse, “Whatever [fault] in the mid-air, on earth, or in heaven,” he worships the Gārhapatya fire from that very spot; and with the verse, “When [the son] approaches his mother, sinless. 7.5.5.30.
Having put on the sacrificial cord (yajñopavīta) with the verse, “O Prajāpati . . .,” he goes toward the half-way point of the Āhavanīya fire with the verse, “All beings . . . of riches.”
7.5.5.31. Having arrived and touched water, he takes six wood-shavings.
He takes six wood-shavings.

7.5.6.2. With the formula, “Thou art the expiation for the sin committed against the gods,” he throws one [piece] after each into the Āhavanīya fire, saying: “Thou art the expiation for the sin committed against men; thou art the expiation for the sin committed against the fathers; thou art the expiation for the sin committed against the seers; thou art the expiation for the sin committed against oneself; thou art the expiation for every sin. 7.5.6.3. They come with the *apsuṣoma* portions in the *camasa*s, or the *dadhiṣoma* portions in the *vāyavya* vessels, which have been prepared by the *camasādhvaryu*s and previously placed at the northern edge of the altar.

7.5.6.4. With the verse, "O God Soma, of thee washed in the waters," they consume the previous *apsuṣoma* cups with the formula: "Of that which was pressed by the seers, for which the *yajus* was offered, for which the *uktha* was recited—whatever portion is the winner of horses... 7.5.6.5. With the verse, "O Maruts, let this song of praise reach you through our breath," he pours out the *apsuṣoma* cups with the verse: "Viṣṇu has poured forth [the oblation] with his powers; may he bestow vigor upon the singer for the sake of progeny. Do you protect us always with your blessings."
7.5.6.6. With the words, "I send you forth to the ocean," he consecrates the water that has been poured out: "Go back to your own womb; may our heroes be unharmed; do not let us be excluded. 7.5.6.7.
With the words, "Of the pressed juice that remains here," he partakes of the curd-mixed Soma: "When Indra drank with the Śasas, he slew... [the enemy]; here I consume the King Soma. 7.5.6.8.
Having gone outside, they perform the *saṃyāja* offerings for the wives at the crossroads.

7.5.6.9. This cake on ten potsherds for Varuṇa is to be heard of as the *avabhṛtha* (concluding bath) cake. They bring it forth adorned, along with the dipping-spoon (*sruva*), the offering-ladle (*sruc*), the vessel for clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*), the clarified butter, and the cake on ten potsherds for Varuṇa; the Pratiprasthātṛ sets these down for the *avabhṛtha*. 7.5.6.10. To the north of the two *havirdhāna* carts and to the south of the *āgnīdhra* shed, he places the King’s throne-seat (*rājāsandi*). 7.5.6.11. Upon it he spreads the pressing-skin (*ādhiṣavaṇacarma*). On the pressing-skin he places the *droṇakalaśa* vessel; in the *droṇakalaśa* he places the mixing-vessel (*sthālī*), the pressing-stones (*grāvan*), the Vāyu-cups (*vāyavya*), and the two *daśāpavitra* filters. He deposits all these together in the *droṇakalaśa*.
7.5.6.12. They cut [the wood] and place it on the wooden board. 7.5.6.13. "Rising up," he says, [referring to] the posts made of *udumbara* wood.
7.5.6.14. They lean that [board] against them.
7.5.6.15. When it has been thus agreed upon, the Adhvaryu enters the two *havirdhāna* sheds and takes four portions of clarified butter.

7.5.6.16. He offers that with the verse for the unyoking: "The auspicious one has come, as if against the current; knowing the way by the paths traveled by the gods, I unyoke the priests who are yoked with the yokes of the gods, for the sake of the sacrifice to the gods, through the sacred word (*brahman*), svāhā!"

7.5.6.17. He offers nine *samiṣṭayajus* oblations with the formulas: “May Dhātṛ, Anumati, Śaviṣṭha, and Ida enjoy this—svāhā! Prajāpati shall establish it—svāhā! O Indra, among those worthy of sacrifice—svāhā! May it be united with splendor—svāhā! May what was torn apart be joined together—svāhā! Whatever today you, knowing, [did]—svāhā! To you, O gods, the riches—svāhā! Those whom you brought hither—svāhā! 7.5.6.18. He has recited six verses. 7.5.6.19.

He offers three *yajus* formulas with: “O Sacrifice, go to the sacrifice—svāhā! Go to the lord of the sacrifice—svāhā! Go to the lord of the world—svāhā! Go to the lord of the good—svāhā! Go to the lord of the brave—svāhā!”

7.5.6.21. Having offered with the *sruva* spoon and having replenished the *dhruvā* vessel, he offers with the *sruc* ladle, saying: "O gods who know the way, having found the way... and "...place it in the wind. 7.5.6.22. With the words, "O Agni, giver of life, enjoying the oblation," he offers the tenth oblation while seated.

7.5.7.1. He offers the tenth oblation with the verse, “He whose face is ghee... svāhā. 7.5.7.2. At this point, he offers the Naiṣṭhyayana oblations. 7.5.7.3. They take up the water for the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha).
7.5.7.4. Having gone between the *cātvāla* and the *utkara*, and standing at the edge of the altar (*vedi*), he says, "Recite the *śyāma*!
7.5.7.5. The *prastotṛ* sings the *avabhṛtha-sāman*.
7.5.7.6. They perform the *nidhana* three times; each person performs the *nidhana*.
7.5.7.7. With the words, "For the king has made wide room for Sūrya; Varuṇa has pierced even the heart," they proceed.
7.5.7.8. Having stood still, he says, "Recite the *Sāman*. 7.5.7.9. The *Prastotṛ* recites the *Avabhṛtha-sāman*.
7.5.7.10. They perform the *nidhana* exactly three times; each individual performs the *nidhana*. 7.5.7.11.
They proceed with the words, "For wide [space] has King Varuṇa made"—[ending with] "he has pierced even hearts. 7.5.7.12.
Having stood still, he says, "Recite the *sāman*."
7.5.7.13. The Prastotṛ indeed sings the Avabhṛtha-sāman.
7.5.7.14. They reach the *nidhana* three times; each individual reaches the *nidhana*.
7.5.7.15. "For wide indeed King Varuṇa has made," with these words they proceed, ending with "he has pierced even the hearts."

7.5.7.16. With the verse, "A hundred physicians are yours, O King," he causes him to recite this from wherever he can see across; with the words, "Release us from a thousandfold wide [bond]," he causes him to recite. 7.5.7.17. With the words, "The noose of Varuṇa has been stepped upon," he steps onto the edge of the water; with the words, "The face of Agni has entered the waters. 7.5.7.18. Having thrown that sacrificial grass (*barhis*) [into the water], he offers [an oblation] while looking toward the water with the words, "Svāhā! [N1,100b5]
7.5.7.19. He performs four fore-offerings (prayāja) excluding the one for the sacrificial grass (barhis). 7.5.7.20. He performs the two butter-portions (ājyabhāga).
7.5.7.21. Saying, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni," he takes four portions of clarified butter (ājya).
7.5.7.22. He says, “O, cause [the Hotṛ] to announce,” and then, “Sacrifice to Agni.
7.5.7.23. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering. 7.5.7.24. He says, “Recite for Soma,” while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
7.5.7.25. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ!"; [the Adhvaryu] says, "Sacrifice to Soma. 7.5.7.26. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. 7.5.7.27.
He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Varuṇa," while spreading the underlayer and cutting the portions.
7.5.7.28. He cuts portions from both the back and the front of the *puroḍāśa*. 7.5.7.29. He sprinkles clarified butter over them and anoints them back.
7.5.7.30. He says, “O, cause [the Āgnīdhra] to announce! and “Sacrifice to Varuṇa!”
7.5.7.31. He offers when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered.
7.5.7.32. Saying, "Recite for Agni and Varuṇa," he places the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), which has been spread with a base of butter and sprinkled over it.
7.5.7.33. He says, "O, cause [the fire] to hear! and "Sacrifice to Agni and Varuṇa!"
7.5.7.34. He makes the offering when the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered. 7.5.7.35. He takes four spoonfuls [of clarified butter].
7.5.7.36. He performs two after-offerings (*anūyāja*) without the *barhis* grass.

7.5.7.37. With the formula, “*avabhṛtha niceruḥ . . . mārayasi*, *nicerur asi martyakṛtam*,” [he performs the act]. 7.5.7.38. Having wiped away the drops with the formula, “*uror ā naḥ deva riṣaḥ pāhi*,” he consumes the water with his breath using the formula, “*sumitrā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu*,” and [the remainder] with, “*durmitrā .
. . dviṣmaḥ*. 7.5.7.39. With the formula, “*san tvā viśa . . . r utāpa*,” he pours out the *avabhṛtha* (concluding bath) water with, “*yajñasya tvā vidhema*.”

7.5.7.40. With the verse, "O divine waters, this is your embryo," he consecrates the scattered [grain] with the formula, "We have made you well-pleased and well-nourished; may you, being well-pleased and well-nourished, protect us. O gods... speak. 7.5.7.41. With the formulas, "The noose of Varuṇa is released; the noose of Varuṇa is cast off," they place the two upper garments (*uttarasicau*) into the water. 7.5.7.42.
With the formula, "On this day, may I be released from the nooses of Varuṇa," they wrap themselves with the two garments.

7.5.7.43. With the words, "Loosen the uppermost bond of Varuṇa from us," they untie their two girdles. 7.5.7.44. With the words, "May we be free from the lowest for Aditi," having stepped down, the two run toward each other like rain. 7.5.7.45.

With the words, "May we rise up out of the darkness," the Unnetṛ leads them upward with the words, "Beholding the highest light. 7.5.7.46–47. With the words, "Fuel art thou; may we prosper through thee," they prepare the fuel and return to their respective places.

7.5.7.48. With the formula, “Thou art the kindling-stick; thou art splendor; thou art splendor; bestow splendor upon me,” the sacrificer places [a stick] on the Āhavanīya fire. 7.5.7.49–50. In the same manner, [he does so] at the Gārhapatya fire... [with the formula] “May I not suffer harm. He pays homage with this [formula]: “With sap... do thou unite me with luster. 7.5.7.51. Before the Avabhṛtha bath, [he says]: “Offer the Udayanīya oblation.”

7.5.7.52. Having placed the sacrificial implements to the west of the *gārhapatya* fire and having carried forward the water, the *pratiprasthātṛ* offers the concluding oblation (*udayanīya*), [saying]: "I pour thee out, favored by the god Savitṛ...
"...with the two hands of the god Savitṛ, I pour thee out, acceptable to Aditi, Agnivati, Somavati, Savitṛvati, and Pathyāvati"—thus [he pours] four handfuls of rice.
7.5.8.2. Once the oblation has been poured out, he recites the *prāṇagraha* formulas and the *pṛśni* verses.
7.5.8.3. Having released his speech with the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*), they remove [the vessel].

7.5.8.4. Having brought down this sacrificial grass for the guest-offering (*ātithyabarhis*) and having scattered the sacrificial grass for the introductory offering (*prāyaṇīyabarhis*), he pours the grains into the receptacle for the wash-water; he who prepares the *caru* pours the grains [into it].
7.5.8.5. When this [milk] has been boiled, he pours clarified butter (*ājya*) into it with which he is about to proceed.
7.5.8.6. Having placed that back into the *ājya*-pot, he performs the *stambayajus* rite.
7.5.8.7. He encloses the altar (*vedi*) and mutters the *karaṇa* formula.
7.5.8.8. Once permitted, he performs the second tracing around of the altar.

7.5.8.9. Having leveled it and propped it up, he issues the call: "Set down the sprinkling waters; place the fuel and the sacrificial grass nearby; cleanse the dipping-spoon and the offering-ladles; gird the wife; come forth with the clarified butter!
7.5.8.10. They do these things.
7.5.8.11. Having wiped the *sruva* and *sruk* ladles, he takes up the clarified butter; all six portions are taken up. 7.5.8.12.
He sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*idhmābarhis*), he sprinkles the altar (*vedi*), and he sprinkles what has been placed near it. 7.5.8.13.
Having poured out the water, he takes up the *prastara* bundle.
7.5.8.14. He strews the sacrificial grass (barhis). 7.5.8.15. Having stepped forward toward the east, he lays down the enclosing sticks (paridhi).
7.5.8.16. He places two fuel-sticks (samidh) upon the fire.
7.5.8.17. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*), he yokes the fire.

7.5.8.18. Having returned, he places the *tiraścī* [ladle] down; upon the two *tiraścī* [sticks] he places the *prastara* [bundle of grass], upon the *prastara* the *juhū* [ladle], and the other two [ladles, *upabhṛt* and *dhruvā*], upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). 7.5.8.19. When they have been placed together, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite the formulas for the *apānagraha* cups and the *pṛśni* [cups].
7.5.8.20. Having touched [the fire] while reciting, "The firm ones have sat down; come to me, O Agni," he recites the *daśahotṛ* formula.

7.5.8.21. He says, "Recite for Agni as he is being kindled. 7.5.8.22. After the *samidhenī* verses have been recited, having poured the *āghāra* libation with the *sruva* spoon, he says, "O *āgnīdh*, cleanse the fires thrice."
7.5.8.23. Having crossed over without letting the two offering-ladles touch each other, having anointed the *dhruvā* and set it down, he chooses the *pravara*.
7.5.8.24. The *hotṛ* sits down.
7.5.8.25. Being impelled, he takes up the two ladles.
7.5.8.26. He performs the *prayāja* offerings.
7.5.8.27. Having performed the *prayāja* offerings and having stepped across, he pours clarified butter over the *dhruvā* five times, and then over the oblation and the *upabhṛt*.
7.5.8.28. Disregarding the two *ājyabhāga* portions, while taking four portions of clarified butter, he says, "Recite for Agni."
7.5.8.29. He says, "O, cause [the Hotṛ] to announce," and then, "Sacrifice to Agni.
7.5.8.30. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering in the southern half [of the fire].
7.5.8.31. Saying, "Recite for Soma," he takes four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
7.5.8.32. He says, "O, cause [the sacrificer] to hear," and [the Adhvaryu] says, "Sacrifice to Soma.
7.5.8.33. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers [the oblation] in the rear half [of the fire].
7.5.8.34. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Savitṛ," while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
7.5.8.35. He says, "O, cause [the Hotṛ] to hear," and then, "Sacrifice to Savitṛ.
7.5.8.36. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers [the oblation] in the northern half [of the fire].
7.5.8.37. He says, "Recite for Pathyā Svasti," while taking four portions of clarified butter (*ājya*).
7.5.8.38. He says, “O, cause [the announcement] to be heard! [and then] “Sacrifice for the path-finding well-being!
7.5.8.39. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers in the eastern half [of the fire]. 7.5.8.40. He says, “Recite for Aditi,” while spreading [the butter] underneath and taking the portions.
7.5.8.41. He cuts portions from both the back and the front of the sacrificial porridge (caru).
7.5.8.42. He pours clarified butter over it and anoints the offering-spoon. 7.5.8.43. He says, "O, cause [the Adhvaryu] to announce! and "Sacrifice to Aditi!"
7.5.8.44. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers in the middle.
7.5.8.45. He says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.
7.5.8.46. Spreading [ghee] five times, he takes portions from the northern half of the *caru* with the stirring-spoon only once.
7.5.8.47. Having made those portions, he hands the two ladles down, one after the other, to the Agnīdh.
7.5.8.48. He pours clarified butter over them twice; he does not wipe [the ladle]. 7.5.8.49. The Sviṣṭakṛt portion consists of eight cuttings.
7.5.8.50. He says, "O, cause [the gods] to hear! [and then], "Sacrifice to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.
7.5.8.51. When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he makes the offering in the northern half, having passed over the previous oblation.
7.5.8.52. He throws the stirring-stick (*mekṣaṇa*) after [the oblation] into the fires.
7.5.8.53. He makes an offering with that residue.
7.5.8.54. Having stepped across and placed the two ladles in their respective places, he cuts off the *prāśitra* portion.
7.5.8.55. Having touched water, he spreads out the *iḍā* nine times.
7.5.8.56. He cuts [the portion] twice; he pours clarified butter over it once.
7.5.8.57. [This constitutes] the twelvefold cutting for the *iḍā*.
7.5.8.58. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, he places [a portion] for the *agnīdh*.
7.5.8.59. They consume [the portions], they sprinkle themselves for purification, and they carry [the remains] around.
7.5.8.60. When the *prāśitra* has been consumed by the Brahman priest, he offers the oblation of the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula continuously along with the [consumption].
7.5.8.61. Saying, "O Brahman, we shall set forth," he performs the *anūyāja* offerings.

7.5.8.62. Having arrived, he separates the two offering-spoons with the two *vājajit* verses. 7.5.8.63. With the *śaṃyu* formula, he throws together the *prastara* grass-bundle and the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*). 7.5.8.64. He takes four ladlings of clarified butter.
7.5.8.65. He offers that with the verse: "O Agni, those which are all thy fuel-sticks...
7.5.8.66. ...and with "The fire on earth, the protection, svāhā!
7.5.8.67. He takes another fourfold portion.
7.5.8.68. Having caused the *dhruvā* ladle to swell, he offers it with its own *yajus* formula.

7.5.8.69. Having silently poured out the *praṇītā* water within the altar, the *udayanīya* offering comes to a conclusion. 7.5.8.70. Having run forward, the *pratiprasthātṛ* cleanses the *sruva* and *sruk* spoons either at the *āgnīdhra* fire or to the west of the *āhavanīya* fire, and takes portions of clarified butter together with the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*).

7.5.8.71. Having taken the *juhū* and *upabhṛt* ladles in the prescribed manner, he makes an under-layering for the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) with the formula: “Thou art the milk of the great ones; thou art the draught of the bodies of all the gods who are worthy of praise.

7.5.8.72. He pours curd across the filter into the ladle with the formula: “Thou art the draught of the speckled ones. 7.5.8.73. He pours clarified butter over it from above with the formula: “Thou art the heart of Viṣṇu; one portion of nourishment.”
7.5.8.74. With the words, "May Viṣṇu stride after thee," he [performs] the second [offering].
7.5.8.75. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite, "May prosperity increase through curds and ghee," and [the sacrificer recites], "Of that mine, may it be unassailable" (TS 3.2.6.1a-b).
7.5.8.74. At the time for the *dhruvā* [ladle], he lifts up the vessel of clarified butter.

7.5.8.75. He sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass; he sprinkles the altar; he sprinkles what has been placed near. 7.5.8.76. Having poured out the water, he takes up the prastara-bunch. 7.5.8.77. He spreads the sacrificial grass.
7.5.8.78. Having stepped forward to the east, he lays down the enclosing-sticks made of *kārṣmarya* wood.
7.5.8.79. He places two fuel-sticks upon the fire. 7.5.8.80. Having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the enclosing-sticks, he yokes the fire.

7.5.8.81. Having returned, he places the *tiraścī* [ladle] down; upon the two *tiraścī* [ladles] he places the *prastara* [grass-bundle]; upon the *prastara* the *juhū* [ladle]; and upon the *barhis* [sacrificial grass] the other two [ladles]. 7.5.8.82. Having set them all down and touched them together with the formula, "The *dhruvā* has sat down; that which is mine, O Agni," he recites the *daśahotṛ* formula. 7.5.8.83. Having touched water and gone out, he pronounces the invitatory verse for the one being girded.

7.5.8.84. The animal to be bound after the sacrifice (anūbandhya) is dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa; its sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) consists of eleven potsherds and is accompanied by the heart-spit (hṛdayaśūla).
7.5.8.85. Its ritual procedure is established as being identical up to the *samiṣṭayajus* offerings.
7.5.8.86. Having offered the *samiṣṭayajus* oblations, he causes the fire to ascend into the two kindling woods (*araṇī*) with the verse: "This is your womb, according to the season."

With the words, “This is your seasonal womb,” he causes the fire to ascend [into himself], [reciting]: “From whom born... wealth. 7.5.9.2. With the words, “Whatever debt remains unpaid by me,” he burns down the northern corner of the altar [with fire], [reciting]: “By which [debt] of Yama... I become free from debt.”
7.5.9.3. With the mantra, “O all-consuming one, O all-devouring one, I offer thee into myself,” the sacrificer and his wife, while offering, shall pour out the groats with their joined palms.
7.5.9.4. With the words, “One has eaten,” they wipe their hands together; with the words, “One has not offered the oblation—the desirable one. 7.5.9.5.
With the words, “May this come to us through the sky,” he worships the sun; with the words, “May we be full and the vessels be filled.”
7.5.9.6. With the words, "O thou, lord of the clouds, come to us," he addresses Vāyu; with the words, "Bestow strength upon us—do so," 7.5.9.7.
he addresses Āditya with the verse beginning, "O God, Increaser," ending with, "Thou art master of thousandfold nourishment—[grant] well-being.
7.5.9.8. With the words, "[Hoping for] heroic vigor," he addresses the sacrificial post (*yūpa*); with the words, "Stand [granting] increase of wealth and prosperity to the sacrificer."

7.5.9.9. Having taken up the wooden sword (*sphyam*) and a vessel of water, they go out with the heart-spit (*hṛdayaśūlena*). 7.5.9.10. Having gone between the *cātvāla* pit and the rubbish heap (*utkara*), he digs up the ground to the east of the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) outside the altar with the wooden sword, saying: "Make the earth swell! and sprinkles it with the vessel of water, saying: "Burst this skin! 7.5.9.11. Saying: "Thou art the arrow," he throws the heart-spit away from him toward the junction of the dry and the moist, saying: "Burn him! Burn him!"

7.5.9.12. He worships with the verse: “From every station, O King... (RV VII.89.5): “Release us from this, O Varuṇa; release us from the waters, O inviolable ones! In the waters the golden house of King Varuṇa has been built; from there the King of firm vows beholds all laws. 7.5.9.13. Having sprinkled water around with the formula, “May the waters and plants be friendly to us,” they return without looking back, saying, “May those that are unfriendly be our enemies. 7.5.9.14. They go out together with the fires.
7.5.9.15. Having gone between the *cātvāla* pit and the *utkara* heap, they come to three fire-hearths (*uddhana*).

7.5.9.16. Having sprinkled [them], he takes a chip [of wood] with the formula, "Thou art the birthplace of Agni"; [he takes] the two *vṛṣaṇa* [chips] with the formula, "Ye two are the testicles"; the lower fire-drill (*araṇi*) with the formula, "Thou art Urvaśī"; and the upper fire-drill (*uttarāraṇi*) with the formula, "Purūravas. 7.5.9.17.
With the formula, "He anoints with ghee," he anoints [the fire-drills].

7.5.9.18. He places [the two kindling sticks] with the words, "Do you two bestow virility. 7.5.9.19. With the words, "Be born after the Gāyatrī metre," he turns himself toward himself by means of the metres; [he does so] with the words, "Be born after the Triṣṭubh metre.
7.5.9.20. He recites the Daśahotṛ formula over the two fire-drills.
7.5.9.21. They churn the fire.
7.5.9.22. On the Gārhapatya fire, he offers an oblation with four ladlings for the Daśahotṛ formula, using [the vessel] that withstands the oblations.
7.5.9.23. He carries forward the Āhavanīya fire.

7.5.9.24. He places down the *anvāhāryapacana* fire. 7.5.9.25. He casts away the *āhavanīya* fire and places down the *anvāhāryapacana* fire. 7.5.9.26. With four spoonfuls (*caturgṛhīta*), he offers the oblation of the *daśahotṛ* formula into the *āhutiṣāha* *gārhapatya* fire; the *saptahotṛ* formula into the *āhavanīya*; the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* formula into the *anvāhāryapacana*; the *pañcahotṛ* formula into the *āmātya*; and the *caturhotṛ* formula into the assembly hall (*sabhā*).

7.5.9.27. Having returned, he spreads a double-layered base of clarified butter (*ājya*) and pours curd (*dadhi*) over it; he then pours a double-layered libation of clarified butter over it. 7.5.9.28. He offers that with the formula: "The crawling, moving world, rich in ghee, has come for *iḍā*. He offers it in the *āhavanīya* fire with the words: "The gods found it; may there be delight in me, *svāhā*! 7.5.9.29. With the formula, "Return again with strength," he offers curd in the *gārhapatya* fire with the words: "Again, O Agni, with nourishment from all sides, *svāhā*!"
7.5.9.30. With the verse, "Return with wealth," he offers the *anvāhārya* rice; with the verse, "O Agni, overflow from all sides, svāhā! (7.5.9.31).

With the verse, "From the ocean the honeyed wave has risen up," he offers the rice grains into the water with the *upāṃśu* formula: "It has attained immortality together with that which is the secret name of ghee, the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality, svāhā! (7.5.9.32).
With the verse, "O Waters, you are indeed the source of bliss," he offers a vessel of water into a bunch of *darbha* grass with the words, "So lead us to strength, svāhā! (7.5.9.32).
7.5.9.33. With the words, "O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred branches, svāhā," he offers an oblation after having placed gold upon a *palāśa* leaf.
7.5.9.34. From this point on, he offers only the full-offering (*pūrṇāhuti*). 7.5.9.35. He takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter.
7.5.9.36. Having filled [the vessel], he recites the *saptahotṛ* formula.
7.5.9.37. He places this verse, "Sevenfold," in the middle.
7.5.9.38. Having laid on a fuel-stick, he offers with the oblation of the *hotṛ*.
7.5.9.39. He gives to another.
7.5.9.40. The Agniṣṭoma is completed; the Agniṣṭoma is completed.
